title: Special Census Supervisory and Administrative Duties
content:
## Appointing Your Staff During Operational Training
## Overview
The Special Census FR employees are appointed to a temporary Schedule A position in the excepted service with a specific not-to- exceed (NTE) date of 180 days from the date. At the end of the 180 days, the FR must be terminated for Expiration of Appointment. If the work is done earlier than the 180 days, the employee is to be terminated for Lack of Work. Between day 90 and 135 of their appointment, the FR can be converted to a current survey vacancy. See ROAM 2024-07 for guidance. Employees are assigned to an intermittent work schedule; that is, they work on an *as needed* basis and are not eligible for employee benefits or federal retirement.
Employees who work 130 hours in 90 days are eligible for health insurance.
Employees assigned to an intermittent work schedule are paid only for the hours worked, and the number of hours can vary depending on the assignment need. The employee*:*
- Does not earn or use paid annual (personal) or sick leave.
- Is not eligible for life insurance coverage.
- Is not eligible for federal retirement coverage.
- Is not eligible to receive holiday pay.
- Night Differential pay is not authorized.
    Is not eligible to participate in the Thrift Savings Plan
    Smart E-Verify and Swearing-In for Special Census Staff
    The RO will have several options for handling Smart E-Verify and Swearing-In SC Field Staff
    Smart E-Verify must be completed by RO admin prior to day 1 of training. The RO has guidance on this procedure. No one should be allowed to attend training if they have not completed their I-9 verification using Smart E-Verify. The appointee does not need to bring any identifying documents to the training session. The I-9 is not to be included in any of the training packets.
    RO Admin can also swear in the appointee while completing Smart E-Verify. If this is done, the appointee should be emailed the BC-61. The appointee should be instructed to print the BC-61, sign, and date it. And then email it back to the RO. The date should be the date the new employee was sworn in by RO Admin. Note: The 180-Day counter begins when the person is sworn in.
    The RO can also have the person sworn in at the training. If this is done, the BC-61 must be included in the training packet.
    Note: If the RO is swearing in appointees at the training session, the training session MUST be held within 3 days of when the I-9 was verified with RO Admin. That is why we recommend having RO admin conduct the swearing in while also completing Smart E-Verify.

title: Completing the appointment and training process
content:
It is your responsibility, as the Special Census Supervisor to ensure the trainees complete the required appointment forms.
You are provided complete verbatim instructions on the appointment process in the various operational training guides.
Follow these steps to complete the appointment and training process:
1. Ask trainees to introduce themselves, as they do annotate their attendance.
2. Distribute to trainees, their individual appointment folder. (You should have already obtained these from the SCO. If you do not have the folders or are missing any, contact your SCO.)
3. Have trainees review and complete various personnel documents. Have the trainees verify their folder contains the following forms:
- BC-61, Appointment Affidavits (if being sworn in during training)
- OF-306, Declaration for Federal Employment. Require 17B signature
- SC-186F, Special Census Employment Agreement Temporary Excepted Service
- SC-999, Overtime Policy Agreement SC-287, Post Employment Restrictions
- SC-1129, Personal Telephone Reimbursement Policy Agreement
- SC-472, Top 10 Ethics Rules for Special Census Employees
- SC-473, General Ethics Principals
- W-4, Employee's withholding Allowance Certificate
4. Upon completion of the first day of Operational training, hand-carry or send by UPS (next day or overnight) all appointment folders and folders for the no-shows to the appropriate Special Census Office or the Regional Office for immediate processing. You must account for and return all appointment folders. A delay in returning the appointment folders to the SCO or RO will cause a delay in the employee's paycheck.

title: Effective Dates
content:
The effective date is the date that a personnel action takes place. No personnel action can be made effective prior to the date the manager/supervisor approves the request for processing an action unless the action is death or resignation.
When processing a Hire or Rehire, use the date the Oath of Office was administered on the BC-61, *Appointment Affidavits.*

title: Position Descriptions
content: A position description (PD) is a narrative statement of specific duties and responsibilities comprising the work assigned to an employee. An employee may receive a copy of their assigned PD, upon request, and their SF-50, *Notification of Personnel Action* when an action is processed for the employee.

title: Duty Station
content:
The duty station represents the official city, county, and state in which the employee works.
- The duty station for employees assigned to a **field** position (i.e., Field Supervisor, and Field Representative) will be their home address.
- The duty station for employees assigned to an **office** position who work most of their work in the office (i.e., clerk) will be the location (city, county, and state) of the Special Census Office (SCO).

title: Initiating Personnel Actions
content:
## Type of Personnel Actions the Special Census Supervisor Can Request
There are several personnel actions you can request as a supervisor including:
**Extension of Appointment:** The administrative staff at the RO will notify the Special Census Supervisor of those employees that are coming to the end of their current appointment. The Special Census Supervisor will decide based on the status of the current operation and terminate the employee for End of Temporary Appointment or request an Extension of Appointment. See ROAM 2024-07 for additional guidance.
**Cancellation:** If a previous personnel action was requested in error, the RO will initiate a PAR action CHRIS to request a cancellation of that personnel action.
Any terminations processed for Performance and/or Conduct must have been documented to support the termination and be approved by both ERB and the RO.
**Termination:** The RO will need to initiate termination actions for Lack of Work, Expiration of Appointment, Resignation, or Performance and/or Conduct. **Discuss performance and conduct terminations** with ERB and the RO. Do not allow employees that should be terminated for performance or conduct issues to be terminated for Lack of Work or Expiration of Appointment. If this was done erroneously, the employee will be available for future job openings.
Refer to Topic 3 PERFORMANCE AND CONDUCT-BASED ACTIONS.
**Name Change:** If an employee has a name change due to marriage or divorce, attach a copy of the marriage certificate or legal document so the RO can initiate the name change.
**Personal Updates:** Employees can request updates to their home or mailing address, telephone number, tax deductions, race, and ethnicity. The employee can log into EPP to make these updates if the employee has a census email address. If the employee is requesting change in tax status, a W-4 should be submitted by the employee.

title: Performance and Conduct-Based Actions
content:
## Conduct
Unacceptable conduct covers a range of employee work behaviors. Some of them include, but are not limited to:
- Tardiness.
- Insubordination, which is an employee's refusal to obey an order, such as refusing an assignment or not completing a work assignment by a deadline; The burden is on the supervisor to phrase the order in such a way that there are no options. Make it very clear that the work must be completed by a certain time, for example: "You must complete this by the end of the day."
- Creation of work disturbances.
- Hitting or striking another employee or respondent.
- Falsifying data on job applications.
- Falsifying Census Bureau data.
- Permitting employees to work unauthorized hours, manipulate hours or work unauthorized overtime.
When a conduct-related situation occurs, counseling the employee should be the immediate starting point for dealing with conduct problems. The employee is to be counseled and the counseling session must be documented along with recommended steps for correction given to the employee as well as a recommendation for action. For Field Staff, document the discussion on the Form BC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems. Make certain to alert your manager and Employee Relations Branch (ERB) specialist when you need to counsel or provide OJT to a team member. 
The nature and seriousness of the misconduct may warrant going directly to a recommendation for termination of employment as the most appropriate action. Given the temporary nature of these appointments, termination of employment without progressive discipline may be warranted in many cases. If the Field Supervisor decides that termination is the recommended action, the Field Supervisor will discuss the situation with the Special Census Supervisor, and Employee Relations Branch (ERB) specialist who will make the final decision.

title: Performance
content:
Unacceptable performance occurs when an employee fails to meet acceptable performance standards. Unacceptable performance could be deficient production, response, accuracy, and/or transmittal/timeliness rates.
First line supervisors must advise an employee with less than satisfactory work performance of their performance deficiencies and advise that an improvement is expected within 24 to 48 hours, or termination from census duty will result. Employees who continue to exhibit less than satisfactory work performance or conduct problems must be terminated from employment.

title: Conduct and Performance Provisions
content:
Statutory and regulatory provisions that apply to conduct and performance-based actions are different. However, there are some basic rules of thumb to follow when dealing with either conduct or performance problems:
- The supervisor needs to respond in a timely manner to a conduct or performance problem counseling the employee and providing him or her with specific steps for improvement. The supervisor will consult with the Special Census Supervisor about the counseling plan prior to providing the counseling to the employee. The supervisor will try to secure the employee's commitment to positive change.
- The supervisor selects the response that fits the problem. The supervisor considers the nature and seriousness of the problem, including any history of a similar problem and the action, if any, taken at the time.
- The supervisor needs to be consistent in responding to similar problems.
- The supervisor will ensure the employees are aware of what is expected of them and the possible consequences for not improving their conduct or performance.
- The supervisor providing the counseling must document **all** counseling sessions including date and time, the matters discussed, the supervisor's responses, including recommendations, and those of the employee. Make sure you clearly state your expectations for improvements and the consequences if these expectations are not met.
    **For 180 Days Field Reps Only: All documentation must be completedon Form BC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems.**

title: Disciplinary Adverse Action File (DAAF) and Documenting Conduct and Performance Issues
content:
The Disciplinary Adverse Action File (DAAF) is an individual file for each employee involved in a performance or conduct based action. The file, which is maintained at the SCO/RO in a locked cabinet, will contain record counseling session(s) with an employee. The DAAF will be created for the employee, and it will be included in the employee's folder that is kept at the SCO/RO.
The first line supervisor must document all counselling sessions and terminations for cause on the BC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems for FR. This file will be used to document the reason(s) for termination and to respond to any unemployment compensation claims, congressional inquiries, or EEO complaints that might arise.

title: Summary
content:
It is critical that conduct and performance issues be addressed in a timely manner. When discussing the issue with the employee, the supervisors need to accurately describe the issue to the employee, recommend steps to resolve the problem, get feedback from the employee, and make sure that the employee understands that future occurrences will result in termination.
The employee will be given a specific date for performance issues to be corrected. If it is a conduct issue, the employee must understand that termination will result if it happens again.
The employee's immediate supervisor seeks approval from the Special Census Supervisor or designee to conduct the counseling session and document on the on the BC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems

title: Releasing Your Staff
content:
Employees can be released for various reasons, some of which are:
- Resignation
- Expiration of appointment
- Lack of work
- Unsatisfactory work performance
- Conduct problems (for example, refusing an assignment)

title: Release upon Resignation
content:
Employees who wish to resign must submit a written request for resignation to their supervisor. The request should include the employee's name, effective date of resignation, and a brief reason for the resignation. Employees determine the effective date of their resignation.
If the resignation is made verbally, the immediate supervisor will try to obtain written confirmation of the resignation from the employee. If this is not possible, the person to whom the resignation request is made (usually the supervisor) must prepare a memorandum for the record documenting the employee's request to resign.
The immediate supervisor must ask employees to complete their final SC-308, Daily Pay and Expense Record. The supervisor certifies the SC-308 and forwards it to the SCO for processing.
RO will initiate a termination action in HRC and attach either the employee's written resignation or a memorandum for record. A copy of the SF-50, *Notification of Personnel Action* will be forwarded to the employee.

title: Release upon Expiration of Appointment (Not-to- Exceed Date) or Lack of Work
content:
FRs cannot work past 180 days. They may be converted to a current survey vacancy between days 90 and 135. See ROAM 2024-07 for more guidance.
At 180 days, terminate the FR for Expiration of Appointment. If the work ends early, terminate the FS and FR for Lack of Work.

title: Terminating Employees for Conduct or Performance Problems
content:
Employees who exhibit continued performance or conduct problems must be terminated from employment. The first-line supervisor should have already advised an employee whose performance is less than satisfactory that improvement is expected within 24 to 48 hours, or release from census duty could follow.
The counseling session for FR's should have been documented on the BC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems and reviewed with their supervisor. During the counseling session, the employee's immediate supervisor offered suggestions on how to improve and, if necessary, re-trained the employee through on-the-job activities. If the employee's performance is still less than satisfactory, or misconduct reoccurs, the employee's immediate supervisor will discuss the termination with the Employee Relations Branch (ERB) specialist and Special Census Supervisor.
The employee's immediate supervisor will document what suggestions for improvement were made and what the outcome was; and then make a recommendation to terminate the employee. If the Employee Relations Branch (ERB) specialist. approves the termination, he or she will work with the RO to process a termination. Also, the Special Census Supervisor needs to consult with the RO when it is recommended that an employee be terminated for cause.
Additionally, after the Employee Relations Branch (ERB) specialist approves the termination recommendation, the SCO will request a termination action due to conduct and/or performance. The immediate supervisor will reassign any remaining work to another employee within the Field Supervisor District.
Unacceptable conduct covers a range of employee work behaviors including, tardiness, insubordination, creation of work disturbances, hitting or striking another employee or respondent, and falsifying data on employee applications or census questionnaires or other documents.

title: Release for refusing an assignment
content: If an employee refuses an assignment for **ANY** reason, they are to be released from census duty. The immediate supervisor will document on the BC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems stating the refusal for a work assignment and make a recommendation for termination to the Special Census Supervisor. If the termination is approved, the Special Census Supervisor will work with the RO.

title: Reporting the Death of an Employee
content:
Report all Census Bureau employee deaths immediately to the RO. Provide the RO the following information:
- Employee's name, age, and address
- SCO name
- Date and time of death
- Cause of death (circumstances surrounding the death), if known
- Duty status (on duty/off duty)
- Position title
- The RO will communicate this information to Field Division and Human Resources at Census
- HRD will process the action.
- RO Admin should confirm in HRConnect that the personnel action was processed by HRD.

The immediate supervisor should advice the employee there may be a delay in receipt of their final paycheck if they fail to return any government owned property.

title: Employee Grievances
content:
## Employee Grievances
The Administrative Grievance Procedure is a streamlined complaint process which provides Special Census Office (SCO) employees an opportunity to seek resolution to employment concerns. Specifically, this is a one-step grievance system which incorporates a higher-level management concurrence requirement when the deciding official does not grant the full relief requested by the grievant.
When employees voice displeasure about any facet of their working environment, supervisors should attempt to resolve the matter by discussing the issue with the employees. Importantly, experience has shown that supervisors resolve most concerns informally through dialogue with the employees. However, employees have a right to file a grievance under the Administrative Grievance Procedure.
**Note:** Separated employees and applicants who have not been hired by the Census Bureau are not entitled to file a complaint using the Administrative Grievance Procedure.
A grievance is a request by employees for personal relief in a matter of concern or dissatisfaction regarding their employment that is subject to the control of Census Bureau or Department of Commerce management officials.
Employees are considered to have elected the Administrative Grievance forum at the time they complete, in writing, the SC- 244, *Administrative Grievance Intake Form,* and present it to the SCO Supervisor. When the SCO Supervisor receives a grievance, they must promptly notify the Regional Office Administrative Officer who will contact the Equal Employment Opportunity Specialist. When employees have already filed an EEO complaint about the same issue, the grievance is dismissed.

title: Employee Options
content: Employees who elect to file a formal EEO complaint regarding an aspect of their employment are precluded from raising the same matter under the Administrative Grievance Procedure.

title: Time Limits
content: Employees must complete and submit a SC-244, *Administrative Grievance Intake Form*, to their supervisors within 15 calendar days following the date of the act or occurrence or on the date the employee become aware of the grievance.

title: Deciding Official
content: Generally, SCO employees must file a grievance with the SCO Supervisor who supervises their work. In cases where the SCO Supervisor does not have responsibility for the matter being grieved or does not have authority to grant the requested relief, the SCO Supervisor should forward the grievance directly to the RO and advise the grievant of such. When SCO Supervisors are unsure who the appropriate decision official should be, they must consult with the RO.

title: Personal Relief
content: The grievant must specify the personal relief sought. Personal relief is a specific remedy directly benefiting the grievant. A request for disciplinary action or other action affecting another employee of the agency is not personal relief

title: Official Time
content: Allow the grievant a reasonable amount of official work time to present the grievance. The grievant is **not** entitled to official work time to prepare the grievance.

title: Processing Requirements
content:
The appropriate SCO deciding officials must confirm that the following items are completed on the SC-244, *Administrative Grievance Intake Form*:
- The name of the deciding official.
- The name of the grievant.
- The subject of the grievance.
- The dates of the incident(s) forming the basis for the grievance.
- The date the grievant submits the SC-244.
- The date of the grievance meeting or telephone conference call.
- The personal relief requested.
A grievance cannot be processed until all the above information has been entered on the form. If the employee refuses to provide any of this information, this will serve as a basis for dismissing the grievance.
Deciding officials complete the back portion of the SC-244, *Administrative Grievance Intake Form*, documenting the acceptance or rejection of the grievance, the reasons for the rejection, if applicable, and the final written grievance decision.
Deciding officials do the following when determining the acceptability of the grievance
- Confirm that the grievance is filed according to the specified time limits. If the grievance is not filed in a timely manner, deciding officials reject the grievance and cite the basis for the rejection on the SC-244.
- Confirm that the grievance falls within the scope of the Administrative Grievance Procedure. Refer to the next section, *Exclusions*, for a list of subject areas that are excluded from the Administrative Grievance Procedure. If the grievance concerns an excluded subject, deciding officials reject the grievance and cite the basis for the rejection on the SC-244.
- Establish a grievance file containing a copy of the SC-244 and any other documentation submitted by the employee.
- Conduct whatever fact-finding is appropriate to the situation.
- Issue a written decision to the employee within 15 calendar days after receipt of the grievance.
When deciding officials grant less than the full relief requested by employees, the deciding official's supervisors must make the final decision. In this case, deciding officials provide their supervisors with a written recommendation with justification and a copy of the grievance file.

title: Exclusions
content:
The Administrative Grievance Procedure does not apply to:
- A decision which is appealable to the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) or subject to final administrative review by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) or the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC).
- Published policy or regulations of Field Division (FLD), the Census Bureau, or the Department of Commerce.
- Non-selection for a higher paid position or the failure to receive a conversion to a higher paid position under battlefield conditions.
- An action that terminates a temporary promotion and returns the employee to the position from which he or she was temporarily promoted.
- An action that terminates a term promotion at the completion of the project and returns the employee to the position from which promoted, or to a different position of equivalent grade and pay.
- The granting of or failure to grant an employee award, or the adoption of or failure to adopt an employee suggestion or invention.
- The receipt or failure to receive an award or quality step increase.
- A preliminary warning notice of an action which, if effected, would be covered under the grievance system, or excluded from coverage because it is appealable to the MSPB or subject to administrative review by OPM or the EEOC.
- The substance of the critical elements and performance indicators of an employee's position.
- A return of an employee from an initial appointment as a supervisor or manager to a nonsupervisory or nonmanagerial position for failure to satisfactorily complete the probationary period.
- Any separation actions.
- A matter previously grieved by the same employee.
- An action taken in response to a formal agreement that was voluntarily entered into by employees which assign them from one geographical location to another.
Additionally, upon a grievance becoming moot due to the employee's death or separation from employment with the Census Bureau, the deciding officials must cancel the grievance unless the personal relief sought by the employee involves compensation or other personal relief that could be granted after termination of their employment.

title: Employee Rights
content:
Advise individuals who have access to grievance-related information of the requirements for confidentiality, privacy, and need-to-know.
Persons involved in the processing or adjudication of a grievance must protect the confidentiality of all related communications with the grievant and others involved in the grievance and the right of the individuals to privacy. Additionally, persons with access to information related to the grievance must not disclose that information to anyone except those who have a legitimate need to know.
Employees, in pursuing resolution of a grievance under the Administrative Grievance Procedure, should have:
- Freedom from restraint, coercion, interference, discrimination, or reprisal in connection with filing a grievance.
- Full, impartial, and prompt consideration of the grievance by appropriate supervisory or management officials.

title: Additional Employee Rights
content:
When employees have questions that fall outside the scope of the Administrative Grievance Procedure, they are entitled to communication with and advise from:
- A supervisory or management official of higher rank than their supervisor.
- The Census Bureau's EEO officer or EEO counselors.
- The Regional Director (RD).

title: Records Maintenance
content:
The SCO Supervisor must establish a grievance file for each case. The following documents are the *only* records that are maintained in each file:
- The SC-244, *Administrative Grievance Intake Form*, prepared by the grievant and reviewed/completed by the appropriate SCO Supervisor.
- All documents supplied by the grievant and any documents used by deciding officials to decide on the case.
- The recommended grievance decision or the final grievance decision, as appropriate, that is documented on the SC-244.
- A copy of any settlement agreement.
Maintain Administrative Grievance Procedure files as follows:
- Keep grievance files in a secure area within the SCO. Retain active cases in the SCO, but forward resolved cases to the RO.
Forward all remaining grievance files to the RO when the SCO closes. Grievance files will be retained for a period of seven (7) years from the decision date.
For further guidance regarding the Administrative Grievance System, contact your supervisor at the RO

title: Employee Assistance Program
content:
## Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
The Special Census Office employees can receive assistance for marital or family stress, alcohol and /or drug abuse, mental or emotional problems, financial difficulties, and other problems. Employees should call the SCO Supervisor.

title: Guidance
content: To assist employees with personal problems, SCO Supervisor should provide the employee with the appropriate national hotline number, which is 1-800-211-6015. Expenses for outside services will be the employee's responsibility

title: SCO Supervisors Function
content: The SCO Supervisors role is to ensure accurate referral information reaches all employees, as needed. The SCO Supervisor should not attempt to diagnose or counsel employees with personal problems

title: Voluntary Use
content: The use of the EAP is voluntary (that is, an employee may choose not to use the referral resources and may not be required to call the Headquarters EAP office is referred). Conversations with the Headquarters EAP Counselor are confidential. The SCO Supervisor should also treat all inquiries as confidential.

title: Special Sworn Status
content:
## Definition
Individuals with Special Sworn Status (SSS) are defined as non-Census Bureau personnel who require access to census information or confidential data, and/or are working in Census Bureau space. Individuals with SSS are paid by a third party and are not considered Census Bureau employees for pay purposes. These individuals' salary and related job expenses are actually paid by the company that hired them and contracted them to perform a service in the RO/SCO. These individuals with SSS could be researchers, private industry personnel and individuals from other government agencies working on special projects sponsored by the Census Bureau, or work performed by members of a formal Census Advisory Committee for the purpose of responding to a request for advice from the Census Bureau. This includes individuals serving on an Intergovernmental Personnel Act assignment. In addition, they could be janitors, building inspectors, building maintenance staff, construction workers, electricians, copy machine repair people, security guards employed by lessor, contractors, and other service organizations with access to Census Bureau space.
To preserve the confidentiality of census data, no person may begin work, or be allowed access to sensitive data until the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR)/ Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Sponsor has received notification of a favorable suitability determination by the Census Investigative Service Division. And, if they have been appointed and administered the Affidavit of Nondisclosure using Form BC- 1759 or BC-1759(DV), Special Sworn Status. A notary is not required if the individual is administered the Oath of Office by a Census Bureau employee who has been delegated the authority to administer the oath (for example, Administrative Specialist). While individuals with SSS are not considered Census Bureau employees, they are required to have favorably cleared the pre-employment suitability process.
Use the BC-1759 for SSS individuals **not exempt** from the OSY, Counter-Espionage Branch clearance processing. Use the BC-1759(DV) for SSS individuals who are **exempt** from the OSY, Counter-Espionage Branch clearance processing. These SSS individuals are usually visitors, observers, GAO auditors, or Oversight Committee members.

title: COTR
content: Each RO/SCO should designate an employee to serve as the COR. The COR must be someone from the administrative staff who has been delegated authority to administer the Oath of Office. The COR is responsible for technical management of a contract and ensures that required paperwork is accurately completed in a timely manner.

title: Appointment Procedures
content:
The following HSPD-12 process must be followed to achieve the pre-employment suitability clearance:
The COR will access the Centralized Application of Managing Personnel Investigations and Non-Employees (CAMPIN) tool and submit an onboarding application. This application will contain the necessary data to initiate the onboarding/clearance process of any new Special Sworn Employee. The Census Investigative Services (CIS) will contact the Special Sworn Employee to provide the necessary requirements dependent upon their requested Position Sensitivity Level. In addition, the COR may be required to provide the following required forms in person or via mail:
- BC-1759, Special Sworn Status
- A copy of two Forms of Identification (one must be a picture I.D.)
- Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification
- BC-1085-Contractor/Position Sensitivity Level Designation
- Fair Credit Reporting Act form
- FD-258, FBI Fingerprint Card (two cards) or the individual may be printed via livescan at the local Regional Offices.
- OF-306, Declaration for Federal Employment
- Current Fiscal Year Title 13 Data Stewardship Certificate
- Management (OPM), Electronic Questionnaire for Investigations Processing Questionnaire for Public Trust Positions (e-QIP) website at [[www.opm.gov/e-qip]{.underline}.](http://www.opm.gov/e-qip) (Contractor or SSS individual will be invited in to OPM's website (e-QIP) to complete the appropriate investigation form (SF-85 or SF-85P) by CIS personnel, upon receipt of initial investigation package.)
The contractor or SSS individual must submit their completed forms to the CIS **two weeks** prior to the expected start date in the RO or SCO. They must also present two original identity documents as identified on the I-9 Form. (Non-U.S. citizens must provide INS documentation, such as passport, permanent resident card, alien registration card, or work VISA, and so on.) Special Sworn Employees who are not U.S. Citizens and have a valid Visa, Employment Authorization Card, etc. must wait 30 calendar days before accessing any Census data/centers. Permanent Residents are exempt from the 30 day wait period.
Please note the Foreign National visit request must be submitted via CAMPIN in the Foreign National section of the tool.
The FD-258, Fingerprint cards must also be turned in as part of the completed forms. Fingerprints may be taken at local police station.
Only use the FD-258, Fingerprint cards for contractors or SSS individual(s).
If the COR opts to collect all the required documents, they must forward the completed package (original copies), along with clear and legible copies of the contractor or SSS individual's two acceptable identity source documents to Census Investigative Services by the way of KTA. **Note:** The contractor or SSS individual must retain a signed copy of the BC-1759 with them while in the Census Bureau space, and/or while performing service with the Census Bureau.
The Administrative personnel and CIS Office, will review the package for completeness and will, concurrently, submit the fingerprint cards for initial clearance. (Incomplete package will be returned to the COTR and will create delay in the clearance processing.)
A contractor or SSS individual is not allowed to work in the RO/SCO until the COR has received notification of a favorable suitability determination from the Census Investigative Services (CIS).
After completion of a fingerprint check and review of all required forms, the COR will be notified via e-mail of any unfavorable suitability determinations, as well as favorable results with instruction for issuance of a badge.
At scheduled appointment time, the contractor or SSS individual appears to the COR and presents identity source documents. The contractor or SSS individual is sworn to uphold Title 13, and is given Title 13, IT Security, No Fear Act, and Personal Identifiable Information training documents, as appropriate.
For questions concerning security clearances of contractors and SSS individuals, contact the Census Investigative Services (CIS) at (301)763- 4191 from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time

title: Position Sensitivity Level Designation
content:
It is the COR responsibility to determine the position sensitivity level for the Special Sworn Employee. The level is determined by the actual tasks the contractor or SSS individual is performing or will be performing, for example, a janitorial service would be a low risk whereas a computer support would be moderate risk-IT.
If the sensitivity level designation is moderate risk-IT or higher, then a Fair Credit Reporting Act form is required, and SF-85P is also completed instead of the SF-85. Since additional time is needed for the processing of suitability packages containing the SF-85P, request contractor or SSS individual's forms **three weeks** prior to the expected start date in the RO or SCO.
Request for James Bond ID (IT access) and any special requirements must be indicated on the BC-1759 and the CAMPIN application approved by the COR.

title: Instructions for Completing BC- 1759(SC), Special Sworn Status (SSS)
content:
The contractor or SSS individual must complete Part A, Identification; Part B, Waiver of Compensation; top portion of Part C, Affidavit of Non-Disclosure; and Items 1 through 3 of Part D of the BC-1759, SSS.
Part B must be signed by the contractor or SSS individual in the presence of a witness; that is, designated census employee or a notary public. Witnesses must sign their name on the Witness *signature* line and enter the date in the space provided.
A contractor or SSS individual who refuse to sign Part C will not be allowed to work for the Census Bureau.
Part C must be signed by the contractor or SSS individual in the presence of an employee authorized to administer the Affidavit of Non-Disclosure, or a notary public. The employee authorized to administer the affidavit or notary public must sign their name on the *Signature* line.
The COR signs item 4c of Part D of the BC-1759. The authorized signature indicates that the COR is responsible for the actions of the contractor or SSS individual.

title: SSS Individual(s) Exempt from OSY Counter-Espionage Branch clearance process
content:
The following individuals with SSS are **exempt** from the CIS clearance processing because of the special nature of their contract with the Census Bureau:
- Tribal Liaisons
- Advisory Committee Members
- Volunteers assisting in questionnaire assistance centers
- Local Update of Census Addresses (LUCA) state and local officials
- Oversight Committee Members
- General Accounting Office (GAO) Auditors
The above individuals are exempt from completing the clearance processing, that is, Fingerprinting, completion of SF-85/SF-85P, and so forth; but they are required to complete the BC-1759(DV), SSS and be sworn in before they are allowed access to protected data.

title: BC-1515, Temporary Visitor Pass
content: Issue this ID to all other SSS personnel exempt from the clearance processing, excluding the questionnaire assistance center volunteers. The NTE expires at the end of a contract or service performed with the Census Bureau and must not exceed six months.

title: SSS Renewal
content:
The COR will be required to recertify the SSS individual during the semiannual recertification. Each valid and active COR will receive an automated e-mail to complete the process.
The renewed SSS and approved access will be granted upon verification of individual's record and provided investigation requirements are met. A new or updated investigation will be initiated at that time, if required.

title: SSS Termination
content:
The COR must immediately terminate the SSS by accessing CAMPIN when a contractor or SSS individual separates from the Census Bureau.
By exiting the contractor using CAMPIN, a remedy ticket will be executed to terminate all network accounts. All accounts will be terminated within 24 hours from the date of separation.
When the contractor or SSS individual terminates their contract with the Census Bureau, the COR must collect the contractor or SSS individual's ID badge, office key(s), and parking permit, if applicable on the day of separation.
The badge should be attached, and the word *Terminated* written in red on the BC-1759. This package should be filed in Inactive SSS file.

title: Recordkeeping
content:
Establish a separate folder for contractor or SSS individuals completed BC-1759 forms, and for SSS individuals exempt from the clearance processing. File forms alphabetically by last name in a locked cabinet.
Maintain copies of BC-1759, and file as follows:
- SSS Individuals **(Active)** -- documents from contractors or SSS individuals that have been cleared by CCCPB to work within census space. To include, actively working SSS Individual(s) exempt from the CCCPB clearance processing.
- SSS Individuals **(Inactive)** -- documents from contractors or SSS individuals identified as a security risk and those who have not been cleared by CCCPB to work within census space. To include, SSS individual(s) exempt from the clearance processing when their service expired.

title: Other Administrative Items
content:
## Use of Personal E-mail
With the exception of mailing your BC27 and BC27a, never use your personal e-mail account (i.e., your AOL, Yahoo, Hotmail, GMAIL, or any other personal e-mail account) to send Title 13 data, such as information about the addresses you are working with, or the information collected from a census respondent.
Never use your personal e-mail account to send Personally Identifiable Information (PII), such as the name and address, name and Social Security number, or other information that could be used to identify another person. Also, never send e-mail with attachments to your Special Census Office except for your BC-27 and BC27A. These attachments may contain hidden computer viruses that damage census files or create a security risk.
Finally, be aware that if you use your personal e-mail account for work related business, the messages could be used as evidence in an investigation (for example, if a complaint is filed by another employee). The Census Bureau does not require you to use your personal e-mail to do your job (with the exception of your BC-27 and BC27A) and will NOT provide reimbursement for your Internet connection or the use of your personal e-mail account. If you have questions about the definition of Title 13 or PII, please refer to the Title 13 or PII materials you received when you were hired

title: Information that Can be Released
content:
All documents required in connection with the employment of an individual are subject to provisions of the *Privacy Act.* The *Privacy Act of 1974* places restrictions on the collection, use, maintenance, and release of specific information about individuals such as Social Security number, date of birth, telephone number, and so forth.
In accordance with 5 CFR 293.311, the following information on federal employees is considered public information and can be released to a third party without specific written consent of the employee, you must forward all such requests to the FOIA Office:
- Name
- Present and past position titles and occupational series
- Present and past grades
- Present and past annual salary rates
- Present and past duty stations (provided it is not employee's residence)
- Position description and identification of job elements
Requests for information pertaining to current Special Census employees must be forwarded to the RO since they maintain the SF-66, *Official Personnel Folder (OPF),* for each special census employee. Refer to Chapter 3*, Selecting, Appointing, and Training Your Staff*, for information on the OPF.

title: Rights and Duties of a Special Census Employee Arrested or Charged with Criminal Activity

title: Fraud, Waste, and Abuse
content:
## Fraud, Waste and Abuse Overview
## Recognizing Fraud, Waste, and Abuse
Fraud, waste, and abuse of federal government funds and property occurs through:
- Violations of the federal law or regulations
- Mismanagement
- Theft
- Abuse of authority
- Conditions leading to substantial danger to health and safety

title: Reporting Acts of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse
content:
Each employee has an obligation to report to his/her supervisor, or to the Office of Inspector General (OIG), information concerning the possible existence of a violation of law, rules, or regulations; mismanagement; gross waste of funds; abuse of authority; or a substantial and specific danger to public health or safety. Employees are protected by law from reprisal for making any disclosure supported by reasonable evidence.
Make reports directly to the Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Inspector General by email at [[Hotline@oig.doc.gov]{.underline}](mailto:Hotline@oig.doc.gov).
The Internet is not secure, it is possible, though unlikely, that e-mail complaints may be read by persons other than your intended source. If you are concerned about this, you may choose to mail or call us. Please do not include Personally Identifiable Information (PII) through the website or via e-mail. PII is items containing Social Security numbers, dates of birth, credit card and passport numbers, or other personally identifying information that could adversely affect an individual. E-mails and web submissions containing such information will be blocked by our system administrator and will not be processed by our Complaint Department. Should you desire to provide this information, please contact the Hotline by telephone at the numbers listed below.

title: Safety, Accidents, Injuries, and Personal Property Loss
content:
## Safety
This chapter provides safety information and accident/injury reporting instructions for Special Census Office (SCO) employees.
Office supervisory personnel are responsible for creating a safe environment for all special census (SC) employees. Statistics show that new office employees have the highest accident rate of any employee group. Slipping on paper, paper clips, rubber bands can seriously injure office workers, as well as other objects left on the floor or by tripping over electrical cords. Paper cuts are a hazard of office work. While these cuts are usually not serious, they are painful and can become infected.
Supervisors are responsible for eliminating such unsafe conditions and practices and for the safety of employees under their supervision. Supervisors have the responsibility for the safety education of all employees under their direction, and for the reporting of all hazardous conditions found in their units.

title: Safe Office Practices
content:
The following safe office practices and conditions help to avoid accidents:
- Arrange furniture and equipment so that it doesn't interfere with walkways (that is, allows space for extended drawers for filing cabinets, and so forth).
- Keep desk and file cabinet drawers closed.
- Do not lift heavy cartons. Get help or use a hand truck.
- Keep work areas neat and free of clutter.
- Place heavy materials in bottom drawers of file cabinets so that the cabinets don't become top-heavy.
- Keep corridors and pathways unobstructed for at least a three (3) foot width.
- Keep aisles free of clutter (that is, waste baskets, electrical and/or telephone cords, and so forth).
- Be alert. Watch where you're going and look out for hazards in your path.
- Move slowly on stairs, in hallways, aisles, and work areas.
- Report falling hazards such as poor lighting, spills, broken stairs, and loose flooring.
- Make sure you can see where you're going. Don't carry a load that you can't see over.
- Use handrails whenever possible when using stairs.
- Be courteous and keep to the right when passing through dual doorways against normal traffic.
- Wear good shoes. Nonskid soles are a good choice. Remember that high heels or platforms are less stable than flat shoes.
- Do not use worn or frayed electrical extension cords or let amateur electricians repair electrical equipment.
- Do not operate defective mechanical and electrical equipment.
- Wear seat belts while operating, or as a passenger, in a motorized vehicle.
- Do not operate electrical equipment in a damp or wet work area.
- **Smoking is prohibited in all federal office space.** Discard cigarette stubs only in ashtrays when in authorized smoking areas outside of the office only.
The SCO must ensure compliance with Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations. Failure to comply can result in an OSHA citation. Be aware that OSHA can conduct site inspections at any time and place without notice.
The SCO should prepare for such inspections by ensuring that an RO safety representative is providing the SCO employees with appropriate hazardous materials information and training and is maintaining a centralized listing of hazardous materials used/stored at the SCOs along with Materials Safety Data Sheets for the same.
The SCO will send all safety documentation to the RO. The SCO should display the poster CD-499, *Occupational Safety and Health Protection for Federal Employees*, in a conspicuous place where notices to employees are customarily posted. The CD-499 should include the name and location of the Regional Office (RO) safety representative.
The form can be printed from the OSHA.gov website. If the SCO cannot print, they should contact the RO to print and send the form to the SCO.

title: Rules for Evacuating the Building in Case of a Fire
content:
In the case of a building evacuation, secure Title 13 materials to the extent possible given the nature of the emergency.
Follow these rules when evacuating a building:
- Learn where the fire exits are located and know the evacuation routes.
- Stop work immediately at the sound of the alarm and Secure all Title 13 and 26 materials and PII information in a locked area.
- Turn off all electrical equipment and lights.
- Take personal items (for example, keys, purse, and medication) with you.
- Proceed promptly, and in an orderly manner, to the nearest exit. **Do not use elevators**.
- Activate the fire alarm if the fire is in your area, and telephone the fire department immediately to report the location of the fire.

title: Safe Field Practices from Experienced Employees
content:
As a part of the Census Bureau's continuing safety program, the following safety outline for field employees will be an integral part of all initial training sessions. This outline is also included in the various operational field manuals.
To prevent unauthorized persons from viewing or seizing equipment or documents, do not leave laptops, questionnaires, and other materials containing *Title 13* data or PII in a visible place in a home

title: Animals
content:
- Obey the signs displayed in respondents' yards. If you observe a "Beware of Dog" sign, take extra precaution.
- If warning signs are posted, try to call the respondents to the door before entering the premises. If the owner does not respond DO NOT enter an area where a dog is present.
- Do not run past a dog. The dog's instinct is to chase and catch prey.
- If confronted by a dog, STAND STILL and slightly sideways without making direct eye contact and back away slowly. Be submissive, but don't run. If you run, the animal might try to knock you to the ground, and you could be seriously hurt.
- Put something between you and the dog, such as a bag. Do not try to make friends with the dog, don't try to pet the dog, and do not put your hands or face near it. If the dog does bites you, do not pull away, it will cause a tear and make a worse wound. Instead, try to make the dog release its hold.
- Many dog bites occur inside respondents' homes. If you encounter a dog inside, ask respondents if they would mind confining the dog to another room during the interview.
- Learn to recognize the warning signs that a dog is about to attack; tail high and stiff, ears up, hair on back standing up, and teeth showing.
- If a bite or scratch from a dog or other wild or domestic animal breaks your skin, consult your doctor or an emergency room about the advisability of receiving rabies inoculation or other medical treatment.

title: Walking
content:
- Never take walking for granted. Slips, trips, and falls are by far the most frequent cause of serious injuries to Census Field workers.
- Stay on well-lit streets when walking at night. Avoid walking past dark shadows near buildings, or walking too close to doorways, shrubbery, and other potential hiding places. If needed, carry a flashlight.
- In freezing weather, be alert for "black ice." Walk slowly and take small steps.
- Obey traffic signals including Walk/Don't Walk signs, and don't jaywalk. Cross the street only at intersections, using marked crosswalks.
- Carry bags close to your body, with the flap or clasp next to you.
- Be cautious when riding elevators. If you are suspicious of another passenger, wait for the next elevator.
- Carry wallets in an inside or front pocket to avoid pickpockets.
- Avoid walking on uneven, broken, or poorly constructed surfaces or stairs. Never text or use electronic devices while walking. Distracted walking dramatically increases the likelihood that you will trip or fall. Always pay 100 percent attention to your walking and your surroundings. Grasp the handrails along stairways, if one is not provided, proceed with extra caution.
- Wear comfortable easy-walking shoes. These shoes may come in handy should there be a need to run. Dress appropriately for the weather.
- Do not carry valuables, such as large sums of money, expensive jewelry, and watches.
- When entering a building, pause and let your eyes adjust to the indoor lighting before moving on.
- Stay alert for objects that may pose tripping hazards.
- Always be aware of your surroundings.
The U.S. Census Bureau in coordination with the Department's COVID-19 Task Force is closely monitoring daily changes in the COVID-19 Community Levels as determined by the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and Prevention. COVID-19 Community Levels can be low, medium, or high and are determined by looking at hospital beds being used, hospital admissions, and the total number of new COVID-19 cases in an area.
We will assess risk metrics for each county in which our facilities are located on a weekly basis to determine the appropriate safety protocols. County-level assessments will be made each Friday to determine protocols for the subsequent week.

title: Face Coverings Field Employees Conducting Field Operations
content:
According to the Center of Disease Control (CDC), face coverings help decrease the spread of COVID-19. If you have any concerns regarding your ability to comply with this directive, please contact with your immediate supervisor as soon as possible.
Follow your RO's policy for wearing face masks.
If required by your RO's policy, always wear face coverings if you are not six feet away from others, avoid contact with people who are sick, and wash your hands often with soap and water or hand sanitizer. A failure to comply with your RO's directive to wear face coverings or adhere to any other established COVID-19 guidance may result in administrative action, up to and including, termination.

title: Tips for Wearing a Cloth Face Mask
content:
- Employees should remove their face covering while driving between assignments.
- Wearing a face covering shows respect for all staff around you and the American public. This personal protective item represents one of the most effective ways to protect each other.
- Wash or sanitize your hands before wearing a mask.
- A mask should cover your nose, mouth, and chin.
- Tie the mask behind your head or use the ear loops and ensure it is snug.
- Avoid touching the mask while wearing it.
- If the mask is touched, wash or sanitize your hands immediately.
- While untying the mask, avoid touching the front of the mask.
- Wash your hands immediately after removing.
- Regularly launder your reusable cloth face mask. You can also launder it with your other clothes. Never wash or reuse a disposable face mask.

title: Mask Precautions
content:
- Do not put masks on anyone who has trouble breathing, is unconscious, or otherwise unable to remove the mask without assistance.
- Do not use face masks as a substitute for social distancing.
For the latest updates on the COVID-19 pandemic, check the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention website and MayoClinic.org.Driving
- Never pick up hitchhikers in your vehicle.
- Watch for erratic movements of other cars. Drive defensively, yielding to other cars to avoid accidents.
- Check your directions and locations before starting out. If you need to look at them again, pull off the road, into a parking lot and stop, while reviewing directions. Only use hands- free devices for maps and directions while driving.
- Observe speed limits.
- It is mandatory to always wear a seat belt, even when pulled to the side of the road.
- Look around and make sure it is safe before exiting your vehicle.
- Keep your doors locked.
- Watch for children, jaywalkers, and pedestrians.
- Keep your vehicle in good operating condition with emphasis on brakes, lights, tires, wiper blades, and belts.
- Park in well-lit parking places at night.
- As you walk towards your vehicle, scan beneath the vehicle for persons waiting to charge out at your ankles. Check the back seat and floor for hidden persons before entering your vehicle.
- If your vehicle stalls, stay inside and hang a brightly colored cloth out the window. If someone stops to assist you, stay in the vehicle, and ask the person to phone the police for help.
- If you are being followed, do not drive directly home. Drive to the nearest police or fire station, hospital, or another public place. Do not exit your vehicle until it is visually safe.
- Have your vehicle keys ready before you reach your car. Do not open your purse or distract yourself when walking to your vehicle.
- Maintain a safe distance from the vehicle ahead of you. Don't tailgate.
- Cell phones and other handheld devices are not to be used while driving*. Do not text*, while driving, when the vehicle is in motion you must pay 100% attention to the road.
- Check for other vehicles before backing, turning, or entering an intersection.
- Do not carry valuables in your car; keep your car locked when parked.
- In rural / wooded areas watch for deer, moose and other animals that may be in the road.
- When refueling your vehicle, be alert for theft or carjacking, and avoid any\
    action that could cause a spark and ignite fumes from the fuel
- Be alert to brake lights or turn signals beyond the vehicle ahead of you. Anticipate when others will slow down.
- When stopping, leave space between you and the vehicle ahead of you. Should another vehicle rear-end you, this may protect you from hitting the car in front of you.
- Drivers who use a motorcycle to conduct Census business, are required to wear a helmet,\
    regardless of local or state laws.

title: Intersection Safety Tips for Drivers
content:
Accidents at intersections accounted for most of all work-related accidents reported by Census employees.
When approaching an intersection:
- Enter the correct lane for your intended action well in advance of reaching an intersection. Be sure to signal before changing lanes.
- Watch for other vehicles changing lanes abruptly. Sideswipe collisions are common around intersections.
- Be alert to brake lights or turn signals beyond the vehicle ahead of you. Anticipate when others will slow down.
- After checking to your left when turning right, always look ahead and right before accelerating.
- Vehicles ahead of you should stop for pedestrians crossing the street. Watch for pedestrians in all directions before making a turn at an intersection. Also, keep an eye out for cyclists going straight through the intersection, either on your right or on the sidewalk.
- Don\'t tailgate. Tailgating behind large trucks is especially hazardous. When stopping, leave a space between you and the vehicle in front of you.
When crossing an intersection:
- Watch for cross-traffic. Running a red light, intentionally or not, is a leading cause of intersection crashes.
- Be alert to traffic from the opposite direction turning across your lane in an intersection. Do not race a yellow light. Do not assume you are safe crossing on a yellow light.
- Always stop behind the marked stop line or crosswalk. Keep your wheels straight and your foot on the brake while you wait.
- Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side. Do not change lanes while driving through the intersection. If you are not in the correct lane before entering the intersection, change lanes after you have cleared the intersection.
- Treat a non-functional traffic signal as an all-way stop.

title: Trespassing
content: While Census Bureau employees do have authority to enter a property marked "no trespassing" when conducting official business under Title 13, United State Code, once a property owner asks a field employee to leave the premises, he/she should leave immediately employees **must use good judgment**. If the situation does not seem to be safe, contact your supervisor before attempting to enter the property.

title: Accidents and Injuries
content:
## Introduction
All accidents and injuries referred to in this chapter are related to those occurring while employees are on official duty and acting within the scope of their employment. Employees are responsible for the prompt reporting of accidents and incidents to their supervisor, the Workers Compensation Specialist (WCS) (1-800-819-4215) and the Special Census Supervisor at the Regional Office. Every Field employee's New Hire packet should include an 'Are You Hurt' wallet card bearing the WCS number.

title: Employee Rights, Benefits, and Legal Protection
content:
All U.S. Census Bureau employees are covered by the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA), which is administered by the Department of Labor (DOL), Office of Workers' Compensation Program (OWCP). The FECA provides compensation benefits for lost wages and medical expenses of employees for disability due to personal injury or occupational disease sustained while in the performance of duty.
Workers' compensation case management is performed by the Workers' Compensation Specialists (WCS) staff assigned coverage for HQ, Chicago/Los Angeles, Denver, New York/Philadelphia, and Atlanta. These individuals work closely with HQ workers' compensation and safety and property claims staff in the Administrative Customer Services Division (ACSD) in the Safety and Claims Branch (SCB).

title: Legal Action
content:
Public Law 87-258, Title 28 of the Unites States Code, Section 2679, provides that the Attorney General shall defend any civil action brought in any court against an employee of the government for damage to property or for personal injury, including death, resulting from the operation of any motor vehicle by the employee while acting within the scope of his or her employment, that is, performing official government business.
If any legal actions are brought against an employee for any reasons while acting within the scope of their employment, they should advise their supervisor immediately.
If the SC Supervisor becomes aware of any legal actions brought against a Census Bureau employee because of an on-duty accident, notify the RO immediately.

title: Assault Coverage
content: Under federal law, employees are protected against verbal and bodily assaults and attacks. Title 18 of the United States Code prohibits persons from intimidating or assaulting census employees while conducting census activities in the field.

title: Workers Compensation Specialist (WCS)
content:
The WCS is the person responsible for reviewing and handling workers' compensation requests from employees involved in accidents and/or injured while on duty. The WCS can be reached through the "Are You Hurt" hotline at 1-800-819-4215 and select the prompt for their respective region. The employees are given the contact information for the WCS during training.
The SC Supervisor needs to have this information readily available to provide to employees that may have been injured and/or have an accident while on duty in case the employee forgot or misplaced the contact information.

title: What to do in Case of an Accident or Injury
content:
In cases of an accident or injury, the employee will contact SC Supervisor at the SCO and the WCS. The employees are told during training the steps they need to take and who to contact if they are involved in an accident and/or are injured while on duty.
Every Field employee should carry the *Are You Hurt?* wallet card at all times while working for ready reference to injury reporting. Wallet cards are supplied in every new hire kit.
If you suffer an injury while working, regardless of the severity, get emergency treatment from the nearest hospital or physician's office, if required.
Notify a supervisor and WCS as soon as possible and call the **Are You Hurt Workers Comp Hotline: 1-800-819-4215** and select the option for your region.
The WCSs will assist injured workers with all phases of a Workers' Compensation claim. WCSs function as the Supervisors of Records (SOR) for all Field employee workers' compensation claim processing.
When an employee notifies the WCS of a work-related injury, the WCS will authorize immediate medical care when appropriate. The WCS will email the injured employee instructions for registering, electronically completing the OSHA 301 injury report and filing a workers' compensation claim through the Office of Workers' Compensation Programs' ECOMP system.
The SC Supervisor might also receive notice from the employee's immediate supervisor, such as Field Supervisor (FS), that an employee was in an accident or was injured while on duty. If the employee is unable to contact the WCS due to the seriousness of the accident or injury, the SC Supervisor may call the WCS on behalf of the employee.
When the WCS is notified by an employee that an accident/injury occurred, the WCS will email the SC Supervisor with the employee's name, date of injury and brief description of accident.

title: Reporting Assaults or Serious Threat
content:
An assault or serious threat of any kind on Field Representatives (FRs), Field Supervisors (FSs), or other Census employees working with the public is a rare occurrence. However, if SC employees are assaulted or threatened while on duty, they should immediately:
- Notify the local police and fill out a police report.
- Get medical attention, if necessary. Contact the SC Supervisor and the WCS (1-800-819-4215) for ECOMP email instructions for registering, reporting to OSHA, and filing a workers' compensation claim, and other instructions as appropriate.
- Contact their immediate supervisor, who will assist the employee as necessary.
- Complete a BC-1206, Security Incident Report, detailing the incident.
The SC Supervisor will report the assault or threat to the RO Manager immediately by telephone and will confirm the assault or threat on the BC-1206, *Security Incident Report.*

title: Employee Responsibilities
content:
## Insurance
Employees are advised to carry adequate liability insurance when using their personal vehicle on official government business. In addition to liability insurance, employees must carry the necessary amount of insurance for property damage to their own automobile. Except in rare circumstances, employees will not be reimbursed for damage to their automobile. The mileage reimbursement is considered sufficient to cover the cost of insurance as well as operating expenses.

title: Reporting Motor Vehicle Accidents
content:
Employees who suffer a work-related injury while operating their own motor vehicle for official business will:
- Contact the WCS (1-800-819-4215) and the SC Supervisor at the SCO as soon as possible. The WCS will authorize treatment, when appropriate, by faxing form to the medical provider or facility and send email instructions for registering, reporting to OSHA on form -301, and filing workers' compensation claims through the ECOMP system.
- Complete the SF-91, Operator's Report of Motor Vehicle Accident, and SF-94, Statement of Witness.
- Notify their supervisor as soon as possible following an accident.
- Notify and provide to state, county, or municipal authorities such information concerning the accident as required by law.
- Furnish name and address on the request of a law enforcement officer, but employees should NOT write their name on a card or paper for anyone except as required by a law enforcement officer.
- Not sign a statement or express opinions as to the responsibility for the accident, except to their supervisor or a law enforcement officer.
- Complete the SF-91, *Operator's Report of Motor Vehicle Accident*, immediately after the accident, if possible, at the scene of the accident regardless of the extent of damage.
- Have witnesses complete and sign the SF-94, *Statement of Witness*.
- Give the completed Forms SF-91 and SF-94 to their Administrative Specialist in the RO.
- Complete any required accident report forms provided by their own insurance company and follow their advice.

title: Supervisor Responsibility
content:
If an employee receives an accident report, citation, subpoena, summons, tag, or ticket as the result of an accident investigation by state or local police, the SCO Supervisor will immediately notify the RO and forward a copy of the document to them.
Supervisors are responsible for following up with employees to submit the required forms to the SCO or RO Administrative Area. In the field, the FS is responsible for collecting the FRs completed forms and submitting them to the SCO.
The supervisor is also responsible for notifying the WCS and the SCO when an employee returns to work.

title: Special Instructions for Reporting Deaths or Multiple Hospitalizations
content:
Immediately after the death of any employee from a work-related incident or in-patient hospitalization because of a work-related incident, the SCO Supervisor, WCS, or the Region's Administrative Supervisor must report the fatality/multiple hospitalization to the Census Headquarters Safety & Claims Branch (SCB) at (301) 763-3711.
Provide the following information:
- Location of the incident.
- Date and time of the incident.
- Date and time you received notification
- Number of fatalities or hospitalized employees.
- Name of any deceased or injured employees.
- Decedents or injured employees job title.
- Decedents or injured employees work status at the time of death.
- Contact person(s) name and their phone number.
- A brief description of the incident.
- Information on next kin, if available.
The SCB will notify the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), the Department of Commerce (DOC) and the Office of Workers' Compensation Programs (OWCP) within 8 hours of a fatality, and within 24 hours of a work-related overnight hospitalization
WCS will also be responsible for completing Form CA-6, *Official Supervisor's Report of Employee Death,* if needed for a workers' compensation claim for a deceased employee.

title: Penalties
content:
Supervisors may be fined not more than \$500 or imprisoned for not more than one year, or both, if convicted of:
- Willfully failing, neglecting, or refusing to make a report of any of the proceeding.
- Knowingly filing a false report.
- Inducing, compelling, or directing an injured employee to forego filing of any claims for compensation or other benefits provided for under the *Federal Employee's Compensation Act*, extension, or application of it.
- Willfully retaining any notice, report, claim, or paper which is required to be filed under the *Federal Employee's Compensation Act*, extension, application, or other regulations issued under it.

title: Submission of forms
content:
All reports of accidents and injuries are to be reported to the WCS as soon as possible, through the Are You Hurt hotline at 800/819-4516. All reports of on-the-job accidents and injuries to OSHA and OWCP are processed electronically through the Employee Compensation Operations and Management Portal (ECOMP).
The WCS will provide guidance to the injured employee on the type of claim forms to use, and benefits to which they may be entitled. The WCS will send an email to the injured employee with step-by-step instructions on how to register an account in the ECOMP, and report the accident on the OSHA-301, and file a claim for workers' compensation benefits with OWCP, if they choose, through the ECOMP system.
In the rare event the injured employee does not have access to Internet to electronically register, report, and file, on a case-by-case basis the WCS will coordinate and assist the injured employee to facilitate the reporting to OSHA and filing of claim form with OWCP through ECOMP.

title: Personal Property Claims
content:
Employees are encouraged to carry private insurance against damage or loss of their personal property.
Claims for loss or damage to personal property (property belonging to an individual) are to be prepared on a CD-224, Employee Claim for Loss Of or Damage to Personal Property and CD-137, Report of Incident, Injury, Illness, Motor Vehicle Accident, Property Damage, or Fatality submitted to the SCO along with a copy of supporting evidence and appropriate accident forms (if not already submitted). Claims for property loss/damage and claims for on-the-job injury are processed by two separate HQ offices and employees filing both types of claims must file duplicate copies of forms and evidence to support each claim.

title: Conditions Required for Allowable Claim
content:
There are five conditions that employees must meet to receive reimbursement for loss of, or damage to, their personal property:
- The loss or damage to their personal property must have resulted from their official census duty.
- They file a claim within two years after the incident occurs.
- The loss or damage was not caused, wholly or partly, by the employee's negligence or wrongful act.
- The loss or damage is not otherwise covered by insurance.
- Witnesses can verify the loss or damage, or you have other evidence such as a receipt or similar document which proves the value of the property.
- It was reasonable for you to have the property on your person at the time of the loss or damage.

title: Allowable Claims
content:
The following types of claims are allowable:
- Claims for losses or damages due to unpredictable behavior of animals.
- Claims for losses of property used for the benefit of the government at the direction or with approval of superior authority.
- Claims for losses or damages as a direct result of extraordinary risks to which the employee or the property has necessarily been subjected in the performance of official duties.
- Claims for loss of or damage to personal property when employees are forced to evacuate transportation facilities while traveling in the course of their duties.
- Claims for theft or burglary of employee's property when there is a clearly established positive evidence of the existence of the theft or burglary and that all reasonable and practicable protection and security measures were taken, and that the item involved was incident to the service of the employee. The employee shall furnish satisfactory proof that such measures were taken. If a police report is filed, it should be submitted with claim.

title: Items not reimbursed
content:
The following types of claims ordinarily will not be payable:
- Theft of items whose prior existence cannot be proven.
- Theft of articles of excessive value or those that can easily be stolen.
- Loss of currency or intangible property unless payable under other conditions.
- Loss or damage to motor vehicles.
- Loss or damage that is covered by insurance.
- Loss or damage to tattered or unserviceable property.
- Loss or damage to property that is owned by the U.S. and for which they are not financially responsible.
- Loss or damage to property that they normally use for their own private business or profit.
- Repair estimate fees for damaged property which the SC Supervisor has not approved in advance of their obtaining the estimate.
- Property that is acquired, possessed, or transported in violation of the law.

title: Providing evidence
content: Provide all appropriate supporting documentation as evidence to support their claim. If they cannot provide the proper evidence, they should prepare a statement indicating why supporting documentation is unavailable or is impractical to obtain.

title: List of supporting documentation
content:
These items are considered appropriate supporting documentation:
- A statement from one or more witnesses which gives details of the incident.
- A statement that the property has been recovered or replaced in kind.
- A detailed written estimate of the repair cost that is prepared by a person or company licensed to make such repairs (*If a fee is charged for the estimate, they must **first** obtain approval from the SC Supervisor*).
- Itemized repair bill and/or receipt for repairing damaged property.
- Receipts or similar documents proving the value or cost of the original property.
- A statement of insurance coverage, including copies of claim papers if they made a claim through their insurance company.
- Power of attorney, or other acceptable evidence of authority, must support any claim filed by an agent or survivor.
- Written justification establishing a claimant's right to have the property on-person, or located at the place of work, when lost or damaged.
- Copy of a police report, if applicable.

title: Computation of Awards
content:
The amount awarded on any item of property will be based upon its estimated fair market value at the time and place of loss. The amount payable for property loss or damage beyond economical repair is found by determining its depreciated value immediately before loss or damage, less any salvage value.
If the cost of repair is less than the depreciated value, it will be repaired and only the cost of the repair allowed.
Claims will be payable only for such types and quantities of personal property, the possession of which shall be determined to have been reasonable, useful, or proper under the circumstances at the time of loss or damage. And, taking into consideration the hour of the day and the locality where the loss occurred, and any other factors pertinent to the determination.

title: Recovery From Third Parties
content: If employees have submitted a claim to their insurance company, a copy of such claim(s) should be included with the CD-224.

title: Third Party Claims for Loss of Property or Personal Injury or Death (Tort Claims)
content:
In any case of damage to, or loss of, property or of personal injury or death in which there is any question of negligence or wrongful act on the part of Census employees, the SCO Supervisor must:
- Notify the RO Manager immediately.
- Submit the SF-95 and attachments to the RO.
- Send the SF-95, *Claim for Damage, Injury, Or Death*, to the claimant(s).
- Inform the claimant to attach any additional statements of support evidence which might be pertinent to a proper adjudication of the claim filed on the SF-95.
- Get a statement from the employee involved, CD-137.
The completed SF-95 and attachments should be submitted as soon as practicable to expedite settlement, although claims may be submitted no later than two years after the date of the injury or damage.
