title: Office Setup
content:
## Acquiring Office Space
## Introduction
The governmental unit (GU) is required to make the arrangements for acquiring the Special Census Office (SCO) space. The proposed SCO space is inspected and be approved by the Regional Office (RO). The RO provides the Special Census Supervisor (SCS) with the keys to the SCO and briefs him or her on any necessary information regarding the space.
Depending on RO guidance, some activities in approving the space for the Special Census (SC) might be performed by the SCS. The RO provides guidance to the SCS on office space requirements prior to reviewing the proposed office space and/or inspecting the office space.
Office Space Requirements
The SCS or RO manager and the GU official discuss the SCO space requirements during the initial meeting. The office space needed depends on the workload of the SC. The RO provides guidance to the GU related to the space needed to conduct the SC.
Areas of consideration about the office space include:
- Can the office accommodate the number of planned staff to be hired for the SC?
- Is the office space open or is it divided, for example, into multiple office spaces? It is preferable to have an open room as opposed to divided space.
- Does the office space have parking? Office space should have parking space, as field staff may visit the office regularly to pick up and drop off field work.
- Is the office space available during and after normal work hours? How many days a week and how many hours each day?
- Does the office space comply with the American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements and the National Institute for Occupation Safety and Health requirements?
- Is the office space in proximity to police departments or local law enforcement agencies? The Census Bureau prefers having office space away from law enforcement buildings to assure people the Census Bureau is not associated with any police department or law enforcement organization.
- Who is performing the office cleaning/maintenance work? The GU is responsible for making the arrangements for the office custodial work. In addition, the custodial staff need to be sworn using the Special Sworn Status form. Custodial work needs to be done during the SCO's business hours. These requirements should be discussed with the GU during the initial meeting.
- If the office space is shared with other non-Special Census office staff in the same building/area, how will this affect the SC operation; if so, how?
- Is there a potential access problem by non-SC personnel?
- Is there noise from other offices?
- Will others be able to hear SC employees?
- If the office requires repairs or cleaning, will it be done in time for the planned opening of the office space? Who is responsible for these items?
- Is office lightning adequate?
- Do windows need to be covered?
- Are the numbers of restrooms adequate for the number of people planned to be hired for the SC? Are the restrooms sanitary?
- Can testing and/or training be conducted in the office space?
- Is the general area where the office is located safe/secure?

title: Opening for Business
content:
One of the office space requirements is that access to the office space must be provided during normal hours of operation. Each SCO is required to have someone at the office Monday through Friday during specified hours, usually 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or as instructed by the RO. If an SCO cannot meet this requirement, the SCS must contact the RO.
During peak SC operations, double shifts may be necessary. These shifts typically overlap by 15 minutes (for example, a shift would begin at 4:15 p.m. to overlap with a shift ending at 4:30 p.m.) and last if needed (that is, at the SCS's discretion).
The SCS is responsible for notifying the GU or RO, if necessary, when the office will remain open later than normal hours. This notification may be necessary, for example, if additional heat or air conditioning services need to be obtained.

title: Office Areas Set-up
content:
## Setting Up Work Areas
The SCS might be provided with a general floor plan of the SCO prior to opening the SCO that can be used to plan the office work areas, and the positioning of furniture and equipment. The space should be configured to optimize the layout of the office and to support areas within the SCO. How the space is used during the SC may change depending on the needs of the operations.
It is the SCSs responsibility to make several 8½ x 11 copies of the floor plan, draw evacuation routes in red, and post copies on the walls next to the banks of desks and doors within the first week of opening.
The office setup may vary from RO to RO and from SC to SC because the office setup depends on the workload size and the space made available by the GU. The guidelines that follow are recommendations for how to setup the office space. The RO has discretion as to how to set up the SCO office space.
The SCO functional areas on the floor plan include:
- Administration
- Recruiting (optional)
- Field operations---production
- Field operations---quality assurance
The SCO support areas that should be created on the floor plan and as space allows may include:
- SCSs office or space
- Multipurpose room
- Storage room
- Sensitive information disposal bin
- Break area
- Entrance/reception area

title: Administration Area
content:
The Administration area should include space for:
- Clerk spaces
- Computers
- Mail receipt
- Supply storage
- Locked filing cabinets for personnel and payroll records

title: Recruiting Area (optional)
content:
If the GU implemented a good recruiting plan that provided sufficient applicants for the SC, then a Recruiting area is optional. However, in some SCs the SCS may need to assist the GU in their recruiting efforts. In this case, the SCS may consider creating a separate recruiting area for these activities.
The Recruiting area should include space for the:
- Clerk spaces
- Applicant file storage

title: Field Operations Area-- Production and Quality Assurance
content:
The Field Operations area should be divided into the production and quality assurance areas. These areas need to be close because the work from the production area feeds into the work of the quality assurance area.
The Field Operations area should include space for:
- Managers (FMs) space, if applicable.
- Clerk spaces for checking work in and out to the field.
- Map storage.
- Space for incoming and outgoing Field Supervisor work.

title: Multipurpose Room
content: Each SCO should have a multipurpose room. This room has chairs and folding tables, which staff can move around to create work areas to use for a variety of activities. This room can be used for assignment preparation and distribution, testing, or training.

title: Box for Title 13 and PII Materials Needing Disposal
content:
The SCS also needs to set up a locked box where staff can dispose of sensitive information that needs to be properly destroyed. Sensitive information includes documents or other materials that may contain:
- Title 5 data -- Personnel and other Privacy Act protected information.
- Title 13 -- Confidential SC collected information.
- Any other information such as budget or financial information that is handled in the SCO.
This box needs to be marked as Title 13 and PII Document Disposal Box. This box must be locked and always safeguarded. The SCS is responsible for ensuring that office staff know how to properly handle sensitive information and know where to dispose of sensitive materials that need to be destroyed. If in doubt, the staff should assume the material contains sensitive information.
All paperwork that contains sensitive information needs to be disposed of properly. At the end of the SC, the materials in this box will be packed and shipped out of the office, along all other enumeration materials, to be properly destroyed at the Regional Office. See Chapter 18 for more information about packing these sensitive materials for proper disposal.

title: Optimizing the SCO Space for Operations
content:
The space should be optimized to make sure the office operations flow smoothly. Some considerations for optimizing the space follow:
- The entry/reception area should be access controlled. Only authorized SC employees are allowed into the office.
- The receiving and outgoing bins should be placed as close to the entrance as possible. During operations, FSs drop off work completed in the field and pick up work they need to complete or assign to Field Representatives (FRs).
- Organize the completed field work by FSA and store it in a convenient location in the SCO where it can be locked. Keep the boxes from the field materials sent the office as these can be used as storage bins and later used to ship the materials for processing.
- The multipurpose room, if one is available, should be located away from the field operation areas, so it does not disrupt SC operations.
- The administrative area should also be located away from the field operations area. It is also important that this area has locking file cabinets for employee folders and payroll. See Topic 4 for more information on furniture requirements.
See []{.mark}Figure 11 for an SCO space mock-up and Figure 12 for an SCO workflow of the most frequently performed activities in the office.

title: Other Office Space Use Guidance
content:
All office space management issues are the responsibility of the GU. The GU is responsible for interpreting and enforcing leases, if there is one, and resolving any problems related to the use of the office space.
The SCS is responsible for the overall control of the telephone and enforcement of the rules governing its use, for example, that telephones are used only for business.
With guidance from the RO, the SCS must ensure that SCO staff members follow all guidelines related to the proper use of the office space. A simple example is ensuring that the front door (or any other entrance to the office space) is secured/locked when the SCO is not in use.
Sometimes the office spaces may contain restrictions that SCO staff members need to be aware of so that they do not violate the office space use guideline. For example, asking for a change in janitorial services or asking the building manager to run the heat or air conditioner on the weekend may affect a lease. When requesting any changes related to the use of the property or related services, the SCS (with approval/funding from the RO manager) must first check with the GU and the RO to determine if it is within the scope of office space use.
The SCS is responsible for reporting problems related to office space requirements to the GU and the RO or taking appropriate action to resolve issues when necessary. The SCS must keep a log of property management problems encountered. The RO may periodically ask for updates related to problems with the office space. An example of this log is shown on [167](#SCOProblemLog). The RO may modify this log as necessary.

title: Furniture, Equipment, Bulk Items, and Office Supplies
content:
## Introduction
The furniture, office equipment, and locking file cabinets provided by the GU must be in the office prior to the opening of the SCO. Contact the GU and the RO if the items above are not in the office by the time the SCO is scheduled to open. The RO informs the SCS when the items from the RO or NPC are scheduled to arrive at the SCO.

title: Telecommunications Equipment
content:
The number of telephones required for the special census office depends on the size of the special census and the number of authorized office and field staff. Telephones must be non-cellular and connected to direct lines.
Because of the Census Bureau's privacy and confidentiality requirements, the lines cannot be routed through a switchboard or be part of the governmental unit's telephone network. If telephone lines must be installed, please check with the local telephone company regarding their installation timeline(s). Be aware that there can be a significant time from the request date until installation.

title: Office Furniture
content: The Census Bureau attempts to minimize the amount of time and money a jurisdiction must spend to equip a special census office. Office furniture requirements are based on the need for simple work surfaces and the need to secure personally identifiable information protected under Title 13 of the U.S. Code.

title: Workstations
content: At a minimum, each workstation should consist of a table and a chair. Desks are not necessary but can be provided for the special census supervisor and office clerks if they are available. Sufficient electrical outlets near each workstation are also required to support computers and a printer. Field staff will come into the special census office to meet with their supervisors and drop off work. Tables and chairs to use while reviewing materials are sufficient for these staff.

title: Locking File Cabinets
content: Locking vertical or lateral file cabinets are required to secure the Title 13 and personally identifiable information materials. Legal size cabinets are required to accommodate the oversized address registers and maps. The number of cabinets required is specified in the initial letter from the Census Bureau's regional director.

title: Information Technology (IT) Equipment
content: For this decade, the Census Bureau is requiring that GUs provide their own equipment and support. This allows for the GUs to use equipment they already possess as opposed to procuring it from the Census Bureau. This will decrease the overall cost to the GU. GUs should provide, at a minimum, computers (laptops or desktops), monitors if appropriate, printers, and barcode scanners. Detailed IT requirements will be provided to the GU through the Memorandum of Agreement process.

title: Shipment of Bulk Office Supplies, Training and Data Collection Materials
content: The Census Bureau, through NPC, ships office and bulk supplies such as paper, pens, pencils, manuals, training guides, workbooks, etc. to the SCO. The NPC also assembles and ships the Address Registers (AR), including map envelopes, to the SCOs.

title: Tips for Managing Inventory and Storage
content:
Some suggestions for handling materials shipped to the SCO from the NPC or RO:
- Inventory all materials as they arrive. Do not assume that a shipment of materials is complete.
- Do not assume that a shipment contains materials for just one operation. You may receive materials for several operations at once, for example, materials for housing unit (HU) enumeration, group quarters (GQ) enumeration, and transitory location (TL) enumeration. Be sure to inventory what you receive.
- It is important to know where all materials are stored in the SCO. Organize and store your materials logically in the SCO, such as by FSA/FR in Case ID order.
Plan your workspace so you have or can easily set up a materials staging area. A lot of materials will be going out of and returning to the SCO simultaneously. It is critical that the materials staging area is always organized and neat.

title: Receipt of Office Supplies
content:
The RO and/or Headquarters sends, through NPC, office supplies to the SCO. The quantity of office supplies depends on the workload for the SCO.
The office supplies for field and office staff are:
- Clips, Paper, No 1, 1/8"
- Erasers
- Pens, black
- Pencils, red
- Electric pencil sharpener
    The SCO also receives supplies for the office such as:
- Staplers and staples
- Staple removers
- Shear scissors
- Filament Strapping tape for boxes, 2x60 yard
- Tape dispenser
- Transparent tape, ¾ side, 36 yd, 1 core
- Telephone message pad
- Messenger envelopes, large
- Rubber bands, size 33
- Stapler remover
- Packing knives
- Markers, black
- Marking pens, fine tip, black
- Labels, 2x4, 10 labels per sheet
- Label, 8.5x11, 2-slit back
- Memo pads, 3x5, white
- Paper, Letterhead (RO provides)
- Paper, copying, 8 ½ x 11
- Paper, copying, 8 ½ x 14
- Carton, 18x12.5x 6, 25 count bundles
- Flashlights
- Reflective Vests
Verify that the materials expected to be shipped to the SCO are received in the office. Refer all problems regarding supplies or shipping arrangements to the RO.
The SCS should inform the RO if additional supplies are needed. The RO initiates the resupply order with the NPC. The NPC sends the supplies directly to the SCO.
It is critical that the SCS or designee monitor the consumption of office supplies carefully to ensure timely reordering and replenishment. The SCO cannot afford to wait until the office has run out of needed supplies.

title: Bulk Supplies
content:
The bulk supplies include the following materials:
- Training guides, manuals, job aids, and workbooks for field staff,
- Address registers for the SC Area.
- Questionnaires (housing unit, group quarters, and transitory locations, and reinterview).
- Other field operation specific Special Census forms for GQ, TL, and HU.
- Other field operations support materials and administrative forms, such as:
- SC-ID, Language Identification Card
- SC-CN(E/S), Confidentiality Notice
- SC-NV(E/S), Notice of Visit
- SC-IS, Information Sheet
- SC-225, INFO-COMM
- SC-308, Daily Pay and Work Record
- SC-282, Documentation of Conduct and /or Performance Problems
- SC-336.1, Reassignment Worksheet
- SF-91, Motor Vehicle Accident Report
- SF-94, Statement of Witness
- CD-224 Employee Claim for Loss or Damage to Personal Property

title: Training Materials
content:
Depending on the RO, many materials delivered to the SCO may be packaged already as training kits. These packages contain materials that are grouped for specific purposes. For example, training packages can include:
- FS and FR supplies
- Training materials for trainers
- Training materials for trainees.
For those ROs that will have the SCO assemble the training packages, refer to each of the operational training guides to determine the contents and quantities of the training packages. Each training guide includes a table with the specific materials that need to be included in the training package.

title: Organizing Bulk Supplies
content:
When bulk supplies are received, the SCO staff check them against the shipping list, unload the cartons, and store them in the office designated for bulk storage. A bulk supply list is provided for each SCO once the Memorandum of Acceptance MOA is signed.
In storing bulk supplies, staff should:
- Ensure that all exits, and fire extinguishers are readily accessible and not obstructed
- Ensure the contents of all cartons are labeled on the outside and stored so the labels are visible
- Stack all similar materials together. For example, stack cartons of questionnaires together in one place and cartons of training packages in another
- Leave 36-inch walkways between stacks of different materials
- Keep the supply storage area neat and orderly and free of litter and empty cartons
Many supply shortages in the SCO result from incorrectly sorted and stored boxes. Be sure all boxes are opened and stored in their proper places.
Keep in mind that bulk supplies can be overwhelming. For example, the SCO may receive numerous training materials. These materials must be stored, and the SCS and other office staff need to know where each item is located.

title: Managing SCO Materials
content:
The SCS is ultimately responsible for the check-in, control, storage, and distribution of SCO materials and supplies. All materials must be properly inventoried, organized, and neatly stored for efficient control and distribution.
If any materials have not been received by their scheduled delivery date, the SCS should inform the RO after checking that sufficient time has been allowed for delivery and the materials have not been misplaced.

title: Geography
content: A special census is a basic enumeration of population, housing units, group quarters and transitory locations that the U.S. Census Bureau conducts at the request of a governmental unit. The success of a Special Census (SC) depends on the collection of accurate living quarters (LQ) data, the population associated with those LQs and the further association of these data to the correct geographic area.

title: Introduction
content:
## The Importance of Geography
Geography is crucial to both census data collection and data tabulation for several reasons:
- Geography provides the framework for detailed population and housing information at the local geographic level, and more specifically, for the SC area.
- It enables the Census Bureau to determine where living quarters (LQ) are located so they are tabulated in the correct jurisdiction.
- Specific geographic entities ensure that canvassing and enumeration procedures are systematically conducted.
- Specific geographic units help to ensure that LQs and the associated residents are consistently identified and enumerated at the correct location.
- The SC is organized by geographic areas.
- The SC outcome affects the sponsoring governmental unit (GU), including possible state and federal funding.

title: Full Special Census vs. Partial Special Census
content:
An SC can be conducted for an entire GU (a full SC) or for part of a GU (a partial SC). A full SC is usually sponsored by a county, city, village, town, or other legally functioning unit of government.
A partial SC is conducted for only a selected area of a GU, usually in states where the results of a partial SC are recognized by the state for funding or planning purposes. Partial SCs are usually requested for a specific area or areas that have been annexed by a jurisdiction since the most recent Decennial census or since the last SC, whichever is more recent. A partial SC may also be requested for areas with newly built HUs or group quarters (GQs).
Regardless of whether an SC is a full or partial SC, SC data are collected and tabulated by census geography.

title: Types of Census Geography
content:
## Special Census Geography Hierarchy
The basic concept of census geography is that it is directly related to the field positions established for either collecting the data or supervising the data collection. These staff work in the field and cover specific geographic areas.
The area that a Field Manager (FM) covers is called a Field Manager Area (FMA). Each FMA is broken down into several smaller areas called Field Supervisor Areas (FSAs). Each FSA is covered by a Field Supervisor (FS) working for the FM. One FM can typically manage up to eight FSAs, with each FSA containing approximately 1,200 HUs.
Each FSA is further divided into Assignment Areas (AAs) that Field Representatives (FRs) work. Each FSA contains approximately 16 AAs. Each AA contains approximately 75 HUs.
Each SC includes all types of census geography even though the specific position associated with the geography type may not be authorized for every SC. The positions authorized depend on the size of the SC. For a smaller SC, an FM position may not be authorized because there is an insufficient number of field staff to require this supervisory position.
An overview of each SC geography and the approximate number of staff associated with each of the supervisory positions is provided in this topic.

title: Special Census Area (SCA)
content: The Special Census Area (SCA) is the entire geographic area included in the SC. The SCA represents the geographic extent of the area to be enumerated.

title: Field Manager Area (FMA)
content: The territory covered by an FM, reporting to the Special Census Supervisor (SCS). For a given SC program, there may not be an FM. Only the larger SCs are authorized FM positions. An FMA is comprised of a group of eight FSAs, on average. An FMA contains approximately 9,600 HUs.

title: Field Supervisor Area (FSA)
content: The territory covered by an FS, reporting to an FM. Each FSA is comprised of approximately 16 Assignment Areas, with approximately eight FRs reporting to the FS. An FSA contains approximately 1,200 HUs.

title: Assignment Area (AA)
content: An AA is the geographic area that makes up an assignment intended for one FR. An AA is comprised of one or more blocks. For the SC program, an AA is approximately 75 HUs.

title: Block
content: The block is the smallest geographic area for data collection.

title: Special Census Maps
content:
## Special Census Maps Overview
There are two general categories of maps used for the SC. The first category includes the maps that the SC sponsor receives and reviews prior to the start of their SC. The second category includes the operational maps used by Census Bureau staff for data collection.

title: Sponsor Maps Overview
content: The SC Sponsor maps are large format maps reviewed by the GU prior to the start of the SC. Sponsor maps include the Boundary and Annexation Survey (BAS) map and the Verification map. Each of these maps may be viewed by the GU in either paper or digital format.

title: Boundary and Annexation Survey Map
content:
The Census Bureau conducts the BAS annually to collect information about selected legally defined geographic areas as of January 1 of each year. The BAS is used to update information about the legal boundaries and names of all GUs in the United States.
For each SC, the BAS helps ensure the SC boundaries are accurately represented for SC data collection and subsequent tabulation. The Census Bureau will send a current BAS map, or shapefiles if requested, to the BAS contact for the SC GU. This official may be the Highest Elected Official or another government official, such as a city administrator or manager, or a Geographic Information System staff member. The BAS contact for every GU is maintained in the Geographic Program Participant database. Field Division's geography staff can assist SC staff in determining the BAS contact on record.
The BAS map and shapefiles show the legal boundaries the Census Bureau has on record for the requesting GU. The GU reviews their legal boundaries and may provide boundary changes to these maps. Updates made on the BAS maps are reflected on the Verification map (see Figure 13).

title: Special Census Verification Map
content:
After a GU has certified their legal boundaries on the BAS map, the Census Bureau produces and sends the GU an SC Verification Map or shapefiles that reflect the changes they submitted. The Verification map and shapefiles are produced for both full and partial SC requests.
The verification map is based on the area included in the Special Census Area and highlights the census blocks within that area. The GU again verifies and confirms the enumeration area and legal boundaries are correct or provide any update as necessary.
The full extent of the GU may not be included in the verification map. If a boundary change was provided that is not included or near the special census area, it may not be visible.
Figure 13. Example of a Special Census Verification Map.
![](/images/imports/1/image1_ddc1b69f.png){width="6.5in" height="5.7281791338582675in"}

title: Operational Maps Overview
content:
Operational maps are used for assignment management and data collection. The operational map category can be further subdivided into two categories:
The operational maps, including the SCA Map, are for internal use only and should not be shared with the GU sponsoring the SC.
- Large format maps (36 x 32) are plotted in color and include:
- Special Census Area (SCA) with Field Manager Area (FMA) map
- Field Manager Area (FMA) with Field Supervisor Area (FSA) map
- Field Supervisor Area (FSA) with Assignment Area (AA) map
- Small format maps (11 x 17) are printed in black and white and include:
- AA Locator maps
- AA maps
- Block maps

title: Large Format Maps Overview
content:
Large format color maps are used by the SC supervisors to plan, manage, and control work assignments for field staff.
The National Processing Center (NPC) will plot two copies of each large format map and then ship them to the Special Census Office (SCO). Both copies of the SCA maps are retained in the SCO. Retain one copy of each subsequent supervisory map type (FMA and FSA) in the SCO. Provide the second map copy to the appropriate FM.

title: Special Census Area with Field Manager Area (FMA) Map
content:
The SCA with FMA large format map shows each FMA within the SCA. This map is only available if an SC requires more than one FM to manage the field workload. The SCS may wish to annotate each FMs name on the map under the FMA Number, which may be helpful when reviewing production reports generated from MOJO.
It may also be helpful to annotate the SCA Map with areas of new housing developments, areas of large GQs locations such as college dormitories, or other areas of general interest that may impact the data collection process.
For partial SCs, the blocks to be enumerated are highlighted on this map.

title: Field Manager Area with Field Supervisor Area (FSA) Map
content:
The FMA with Field Supervisor Area (FSA) large format map shows and labels within the subject FSA. The FM uses this map to determine the geographic area within each of their FS boundaries. The FM may wish to annotate each FS's name on the map under their area.
See []{.mark}Figure 14 for an example of an FMA with FSAs map.
**Field Supervisor Area with Assignment Area (AA) Map**
The FSA with Assignment Area (AA) large format map shows and labels the AAs within the subject FSA. This map is used to determine FR assignments. The SCO makes initial AA assignments to the FS. The FS then assigns AAs to the FRs. As a rule, FRs are usually assigned the AA in which they live, and subsequent AAs closest to their home locations. Efficient assignments minimize the time and travel required by field staff and helps to contain costs to the sponsoring government.
The FS should pinpoint the home location of each FR on their copy of the AA Map. This will aid in the review and approval of payroll submissions and mileage claims by the field staff, to determine whether the claims submitted are reasonable for work completed.
Figure 14. Example of a Special Census -- FMA with FSAs Map.
![Image showing an example of a Special Census FMA with FSAs map. The map includes a legend and areas highlighted in colors.](/images/imports/1/image1_ddc1b69f.png){width="6.351932414698163in" height="6.509166666666666in"}

title: Small Format Maps Overview
content:
The small format (11x17) maps include the AA Locator Map, the AA Map, and the Block Map. These black and white maps are used by FRs for data collection purposes in the field.
The NPC print the maps and insert them into a map pouch in the back of the corresponding Address Register. The address registers are then sent to the appropriate Special Census Office.
Each AA contains its own set of maps, an AA Locator Map, an AA Map, and a Block map for each block in the AA. A single separate small format map legend is included in the map pouch with the maps.
The sections below provide a general overview of each small format map type. Refer to Chapter 3 of the SC-1202, Field Representative Manual for detailed information on each of the operational maps.

title: AA Locator Map
content:
The AA Locator map shows where the AA is located within the general vicinity of the FSA.
The AA is highlighted on the map. The map shows neighboring streets and other nearby geographic features.
The AA Locator map is used to locate the AA on the ground and to plan an efficient route of travel through the AA. Updates should not be made on the AA Locator map.
See Figure 15 for an example of this map.

title: AA Map
content:
The AA map shows the geographic area of the AA bounded on all sides by visible features, such as streets or roads, railroads, or rivers; or by nonvisible features, such as county, city, or property boundaries. The map shows all the blocks in the AA. An AA is identified with a six-digit number on the map, for example, 005001.
The FRs use the AA map to locate the blocks within their assigned AA. Updates should not be made on the AA map.
See Figure 16 for an example of an AA map.
Figure 15. Example of a Special Census Assignment (AA) area Locator Map.
![Image showing an example of a Special Census Assignment Area (AA) Locator map, where the AA appear in the context of a larger map. This map is used to find an AA.](/images/imports/1/image1_ddc1b69f.png){width="5.207517497812773in" height="8.297200349956256in"}
Figure 16.Example of a Special Census Assignment Area map.
![Image is an example of the Special Census Assignment Area (AA) map, where the assignment area map fills the page. This map is used to see more detail about the AA.](/images/imports/1/image1_ddc1b69f.png){width="5.291780402449694in" height="8.430423228346458in"}

title: Block Map
content:
This map shows the boundaries and features of a specific block where the FR conducts listing and enumeration activities. The block map also shows map spots and map spot numbers for known HUs within the block boundaries.
**Important:** Although most block maps are comprised of a single parent map sheet, a block may be multi-sheeted. There are three types of map sheets: parent sheet, inset sheet, and index sheet. These sheets help to show more detailed areas that cannot be shown clearly on the block map. Map spot distribution and density affects the display of map spots and their labels. Each block is covered by one or more parent map sheets at a single scale. Inset map sheets at larger scales are created as required for areas with high map spot density that cannot clearly be shown on the parent map sheet. An index map sheet showing the sheet configuration is created for all blocks requiring more than one parent map sheet. The type of map sheet is identified in the map margin. FRs do not make updates on the block maps.
After the FR completes canvassing a block, in addition to circling the block number on the SC-114, Block Listing, they should also circle the block number on the map. This helps them to track which blocks they have completed canvassing.

title: Map Spots and Map Spot Numbers
content:
Map spots for HUs are shown on the SC block maps, if they exist, along with an accompanying map spot number. The map spot number is considered part of the geographic code for the LQ. The map spot number is also displayed in Column 10, Map Spot No., on the SC-920, Address List Page. Areas of newer HU development (after the most recent Decennial census) may not have maps spots.
Map spots and their map spot numbers on the maps, when used in conjunction with the address register, can help FRs locate existing HUs during canvassing. Map spots can be especially useful when the house number and street name listed in the address register are not complete. The SC Program does not include map spotting in the canvassing procedures. Consequently, FRs do not add map spots to the block maps nor update existing map spot locations.

title: Map Spots
content:
A map spot is a symbol showing the location of a structure containing one or more LQs.

title: Map Spot Number
content:
A map spot number is a number assigned to each structure containing HUs and GQs in the AA. The map spot number is printed next to the map spot. Map spots representing multi-unit structures will have a map spot number, followed by the number of HUs at the structure in parentheses.

title: Receiving and Preparing Assignments for the Field
content:
## Introduction
This chapter is mainly for office clerks. The purpose of this chapter is to provide the instructions for confirming receipt of and checking in Address Registers from the National Processing Center (NPC), reviewing the contents of the Address Registers for accuracy, and for preparing Address Registers for check-out to the Field Supervisors (FSs).
The NPC prints the contents of the Address Registers, assembles the map envelopes, and ships the Address Registers to the Special Census Office (SCO). This chapter explains how the materials are processed in the SCO and sent to the field.

title: Check-in Materials From NPC
content:
## Overview
The NPC ships assembled Address Registers to the SCO. Upon receipt of the Address Registers at the SCO, the clerks are responsible for opening and unpacking the boxes and checking Address Registers and map envelopes received from NPC into MOJO.

title: Receipt of Address Registers from the NPC
content:
The NPC ships assembled Address Registers to the SCO. Upon receipt of the Address Registers, the clerks:
- Open, unpack, and sort the boxes of Address Registers.
- Check-in Address Registers and map envelopes received from NPC.
- Determine if any Address Registers are missing.

title: Step 1: Open and Unpack Boxes of Address Registers
content:
Carefully open the boxes of Address Registers and sort the Address Registers by Field Supervisor Area (FSA). For each FSA, sort the Address Registers in ascending order by Assignment Area (AA).
Some AAs may consist of more than one Address Register, depending on the number of housing units (HU) in the AA. If an AA requires multiple Address Registers, then each Address Register for the AA will have a label indicating Register \_\_ of \_\_ that will be affixed to the top right corner of the Address Register's front cover. If an AA contains more than one Address Register, all Address Registers for the AA will be strapped together for shipment. Be sure to keep all Address Registers for an AA together. If the number of Address Registers received do not match the number of Address Registers indicated on the label, then immediately notify the SCO manager.
Do not discard the Address Register shipping boxes. Use the shipping boxes to transport training materials to the training site and to ship Address Registers and materials to the NPC at the end of the SC.
Make sure there is a map envelope included for each AA. If there are multiple Address Registers for an AA, the map envelope will be in the back of the first Address Register for the AA.
Using the packing list, cross off AAs as you confirm each AA was received.
If Address Registers are missing, search the SCO for the missing Address Registers. Inform the Special Census Supervisor (SCS) if the missing materials cannot be found in the SCO.
If any map envelopes are missing from the Address Registers, notify the SCS immediately, so the RO can be contacted to notify NPC.
**Step 2: Check-in Address Registers and map envelopes received from NPC**
Every Address Register and map envelope received from NPC must be checked in to MOJO individually before Address Registers can be checked out to field staff. Some AAs may contain more than one Address Register, but only one Address Register for the AA needs to be checked into MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for steps to check-in Address Registers and map envelopes received from NPC.
**Step 3: Check MOJO to determine if there are any AAs that were not received from NPC**
Sort and filter the Case Search table in MOJO to determine if any AAs were not received from NPC. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for instructions on sorting and filtering the Case Search table in MOJO.
If Address Registers or map envelopes are missing, review the packing slip from the NPC shipment to determine if the Address Registers and map envelopes were included in the box. Search the SCO for the missing Address Registers and map envelopes. Inform the SCS if the missing materials cannot be found in the SCO.
If the missing materials were not included in the shipment(s) from NPC, then contact the SCS. The SCS contacts the Regional Office (RO) to communicate the issue. The RO contacts NPC to inform them of the missing materials so they can be assembled and shipped to the SCO again.
If all Address Registers and map envelopes were received and checked into MOJO, then proceed to Topic 3 to confirm the contents of the Address Registers.

title: Confirm Contents of Address Registers
content:
## Overview
After checking in the Address Registers and map envelopes from NPC, the clerks verify the contents of a sample of Address Registers to confirm the contents are accurate, in the correct order, and have the correct quantities.

title: Confirming Contents of Address Registers
content:
Print Form SC-336, Assignment Directory, from MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for instructions on printing Form SC-336, Assignment Directory. This report provides a listing, in numerical order, of every AA in each FSA within the SCO.
Form SC-336, Assignment Directory is printed from MOJO and is used by clerks in the office to track the review of the contents in the Address Registers for each AA in the SCO. Organize the Address Registers in the same order the assignment areas are presented on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory, prior to confirming contents of the Address Registers.
The SC-336, Assignment Directory, contains the following information:
**Column (1), SCO** used by the clerks to track review of the contents in the Address Register for each AA in the SCO.
**Column (2), Date Assigned** -- the date the AA was assigned to the FS.
**Column (3), AA** -- the Assignment Area number.
**Column (4), Employee Name** -- the last name, first name, and middle initial of the employee to whom the AA is assigned.
**Column (5), Employee ID** -- the Employee ID of the employee to whom the AA is assigned.
**Column (6), HUs** -- the number of housing units in the AA.
**Column (7), State** -- the state code and abbreviation.
**Column (8), County** -- the county code and name.
**Column (9), FS** -- used by the FS to indicate the AA has been assigned to a FR.
An Address Register is a legal size (8 ½ inch X 14 inch) binder that opens from right to left. Address Register contents are listed in the order in which they appear in the Address Register from front to back. The following table provides a brief description of each item in the Address Register.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Form                                     Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Quantity
  ---------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ --------------
  SC-101A.1, Special Notice Page           This form is a reminder that all information in the Address Register is confidential, and all entries made need to be clear and legible                                                                                                                            1
  SC-940, Address Register Cover Page      This form is used to track assignment information and indicate work progress.                                                                                                                                                                                      1
  SC-114, Block List Page                  This form lists the Block Number of each block within the Assignment Area                                                                                                                                                                                          1
  SC-920, Address List Page                These pages list all known housing unit (HU) addresses, Group Quarters (GQs), and Transitory Locations (TLs) in the AA                                                                                                                                             Varies by AA
  SC-921, Add Page                         FRs use this page to list housing units (HUs), Group Quarters (GQs), and Transitory Locations (TLs) found during their work that are not listed on Form SC-920, Address List Page                                                                                  8
  SC-901, Notes Page                       FRs use this form to enter any relevant notes about addresses.                                                                                                                                                                                                     1
  SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record   This form is used by Quality Control Field Supervisors while performing dependent quality checks on the completed assignment                                                                                                                                       1
  Map Envelope                             Contains an AA Locator map, AA map, Block map(s), Map Legend, and possibly an Index map and an Inset map (depending on the assignment). If there are multiple Address Registers for an AA, then the map envelope will be included in the first Address Register.   1
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Open each Address Register and confirm the order and quantities of the pages match the expected contents in Table 12.1. Be sure to check contents of the Address Registers based on the order the AAs appear on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory.
The clerks check a sample of Address Registers for each FSA To ensure that the Address Registers are accurate.
For Address Registers, clerks:
- Conduct a content check for each of the first three AAs in each FSA (some AAs may contain more than one Address Register) listed on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory
If all three AAs for the FSA pass the content check, continue reviewing each Address Register in the FSA to make sure the same AA number is printed on the forms.
If any one of the first three AAs for the FSA fail the content check, immediately notify the SCS. The SCS contacts the RO to communicate the issue. The RO contacts NPC to inform them of the error and works with NPC to ensure the materials are corrected and resent to the SCO. Place the Address Register(s) that failed the content check aside.
- For the remaining Address Registers in the FSA, check to ensure that the AA number printed on the following forms match the label on the front of the Address Register(s):
- Form SC-940, Address Cover Page
- Form SC- 114, Block List
- Form SC-920, Address List Page(s)
- Form SC-921, Add Pages
- Form SC-901, Notes Page
- Form SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record
- Map envelope (at a minimum, there must be one AA Locator Map, an AA Map, and a Block map for each block in the AA)
Using Form SC-336, Assignment Directory, write a check mark in the left side of Column 1, SCO, if the Address Register passed the content check of AA number check.
Using Form SC-336, Assignment Directory, write a X in the left side of Column 1, SCO, to identify there is an issue with the Address Register(s). Place the Address Register(s) that failed the content check or AA number check aside.

title: Prepare Address Registers for Check-out
content:
## Overview
Prior to checking out Address Registers to the FS, clerks:
- Update the SC-920, Address List Page(s) to identify housing units that self-responded.
- Write X in Column 3, Special Situations and Column 4, Action Code, on the SC-920, Address List Page.
- Update the SC-920, Address List Page(s) to identify dangerous addresses.
- Write PC in Column 3, Special Situations to indicate Proceed with Caution for a dangerous address and leave Column, 4, Action Code blank.
- Write X in Column 3, Special Situations to indicate Cease Contact for a dangerous address and Column 4, Action Code.
- Locate the supply of messenger envelopes from the SCO materials supply.
- Print labels for housing units on the SC-920, Address List page(s).
- Affix the labels for the housing units on the SC-920, Address List Page(s) to blank SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, keeping the questionnaires in the same order as the addresses appear on the SC-920 Address List Page(s).
The SCO is provided with both blank questionnaires and questionnaires with a pre-printed barcode ID/Case ID. The blank Forms SC-Q, Special Questionnaire, are used for known addresses on Form SC-920, Address List Page. As part of the preparing Address Registers for check-out, clerks print labels for known addresses that require an interview and affix the label to a blank questionnaire.
Questionnaires with a pre-printed barcode ID/Case ID are mainly used by field staff when conducting an interview at a new housing unit.

title: Preparing Address Registers
content:
Prepare Address Register(s) for one AA at a time, working in order as the AAs are listed on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory. Complete all preparation steps for an AA before continuing with the next AA listed on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory. As preparation steps for each AA are complete, place a checkmark in the right side of Column 1, SCO, on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory.
Continue preparing Address Registers until all AAs in the FSA have been prepared. Then continue with the next FSA until all registers in each FSA have been prepared. Keep the Address Registers organized by FSA.

title: Step 1: Update the SC-920, Address List Page(s) for Addresses that Do Not Require an Interview
content:
The Address Registers were printed and assembled prior to the self-response phase. As a result, Form SC-920, Address List Page(s) for each AA need to be updated to indicate that FRs do not need to make contact or interview at housing units that self-responded and addresses that are dangerous with a cease contact classification. The SC-920, Address List Page(s), also need to be updated to identify addresses that are dangerous with a proceed with caution classification.
The SC- 300 Self-Response/Dangerous Address Report in MOJO contains a list of the addresses that self-responded or are identified as dangerous. To update Form SC-920, Address List Page(s) the clerks:
- Review the SC-300 report in MOJO. Refer to the MOJO user guide for steps to view and print SC-300 report from MOJO.
- Update the SC-920, Address List Page(s) to identify housing units that self-responded.
- Write X in Column 3, Special Situations and Column 4, Action Code, on the SC-920, Address List Page.
- Update the SC-920, Address List Page(s) to identify dangerous addresses.
- Write PC in Column 3, Special Situations to indicate Proceed with Caution for a dangerous address and leave Column, 4, Action Code blank.
- Write X in Column 3, Special Situations and Column 4, Action Code, to indicate Cease Contact for a dangerous address.

title: Step 2: Locate Supply of Messenger Envelopes
content: Locate the supply of messenger envelopes from the SCO supply of materials. Use one messenger envelope per AA.

title: Step 3: Print Labels for Housing Units on the SC-920, Address List Page(s)
content: Before printing labels ensure the sheet of labels is properly installed in the printer. Labels only print for addresses that require an interview. If a self-response was received for an address or if an address is dangerous with a classification of Cease Contact, then labels will not print for those specific addresses. As labels are printed, make sure the printed text on the label is legible. If the printed labels are not legible, properly dispose of the illegible labels and reprint the labels. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for steps to print labels for housing units listed on Form SC-920, Address List Page(s).

title: Step 4: Affix Labels to blank SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires for Housing Units on the SC-920, Address List Page(s)
content:
After the AA labels are printed, clerks:
- Retrieve a stack of blank Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, from the SCO materials supply.
- Working in order of addresses as they appear on the SC-920, Address List Pages(s), carefully peel off the corresponding housing unit label and carefully affix it to the Apply Label Here section on the front page of a blank Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. Labels should only be printed and affixed to a blank Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire for addresses on Form SC-920, Address List Page if column 4, Action Code, is blank. Make sure the label is completely within the label box. Continue this process until all address labels for the entire AA have been placed on questionnaires. Be sure to keep labeled SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires in the same order as the housing units appear on the SC-920, Address List Page(s).
- To ensure that each listed address requiring an interview has a labeled SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, match each labeled questionnaire to its corresponding Special Census address on the Form SC-920, Address List Page(s)*,* in the AA address register. All addresses with a blank Column 4, Action Code, require an interview and should have a labeled questionnaire. Immediately notify the FM or SCS if any addresses requiring an interview on Form SC-920, Address List Page(s) do not have a barcode ID label. Keep Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire(s) in the same order as they appear on Form SC-920, Address List Page(s).
After confirming that every address in the AA that requires an interview has a corresponding labeled questionnaire, place all labeled questionnaires in the 12 by 16 messenger envelope. Refer to Form SC-336, Assignment Directory, to obtain the AA numbers. Write the AA number in legible, large print using a black ink ballpoint pen on the outside of the 12 by 16 messenger envelope.
Place the stuffed 12 by 16 messenger envelope inside the front cover page of the Address Register and place a rubber band around the Address Register with the questionnaires. If there are multiple Address Registers for an AA, place the stuffed 12 x 16 messenger envelope inside the front cover of the first Address Register for the AA.

title: Step 5: Fill out Form SC-940, Address Register Cover Page
content: On Form SC-940, Address Register Cover Page, in Section 1, Assignment Information, under row (a) FS, enter the Name, Employee ID, and Telephone Number of the FS to which the AA will be assigned.

title: Print and Prepare Forms for Field Supervisors
content:
## Overview
Prior to checking out AAs to Field Supervisors, clerks are responsible for gathering the materials to be provided to the FSs along with their AA Address Registers. Clerks are responsible for gathering the:
- Form SC-20, Field Supervisor Management Record
- Form SC-1019C, Employee Listing by FSA

title: Step 1: Locate Form SC-20, Field Supervisor's Management Record
content:
Locate the SC-20, Field Supervisor Management Record in the SCO materials supply. Clerks:
- Write the Field Supervisor's Name, SCID number, and FSA number in the top right corner of the SC-20, Field Supervisor Management Record.
- Make a copy of the completed Form SC-20, Field Supervisor's Management Record to keep in the SCO.
- Write each AA number in Section 1, Assignment Information, in the space provided. The AAs must be written in the order they appear on Form SC-336, Assignment Directory.

title: Step 2: Print Form SC-1019C, Employee Listing by FSA from MOJO
content:
Print Form SC-1019, Employee Listing by SCID and FSA, from MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for printing procedures. This report provides a list of all employees in the FSA. FSs use this list to contact FRs on their team and when making reassignments in the field.
Form SC-20, Field Supervisor's Management Record, and Form SC-1019, Employee Listing by SCID and FSA, must be provided to the FS along with the Address Registers for their FSA. Keep these two forms with the Address Registers for the FSA.

title: Check-out Address Registers
content:
## Overview
Clerks use MOJO to check-out the Address Register and select the FS to whom the AA is being assigned. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for procedures on assigning and checking out AAs. All Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, associated with the AA, need to be checked out separately from the Address Register.
After the assignment areas are assigned to an FS in MOJO, the clerks:
- Print a new Form SC-336, Assignment Directory showing that the Address Registers are assigned and checked out to the FS.
- Place Form SC-336, Assignment Directory with the materials that are provided to the FSs along with Address Registers.
Below is a list of the contents that go out with each assignment to the FS:
- Address Register
- Map pouch with the associated maps
- SC-Q labeled questionnaires
- SC-336, HU Assignment Directory, showing all assignments made to the FS
- SC-20, Field Supervisor's Management Record
- SC-1019, Employee Listing by SCID and FSA

title: Initial Reassignment of Address Registers to Field Representatives
content:
FSs assign AAs to the FRs after classroom training. The FSs update Form SC-336.1, Reassignment Worksheet, with the name of the FR to which the AA was reassigned. The FS writes the:
- SCID, Date, FSA Number, and Page \_ of \_ in the Header section.
- AA number in Column 1, AA.
- Name of Employee who was previously assigned the AA (which is the FS) in Column 3, From: Employee Name.
- Name of the employee to whom the AA was reassigned (which is the FR) in Column 4, To: Employee Name.
- Employee ID to whom the AA was reassigned in Column 5, To Employee ID.
When the updated Form SC-336.1, Reassignment Worksheet, is returned to the office, the clerks update MOJO to reflect the new reassignment. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for procedures on assigning AAs. It is important to keep MOJO updated as reassignments are made in the field.

title: Subsequent Reassignments of Address Registers to Field Representatives
content: As AAs need to be reassigned during the SC, FSs use Form 336.1, Reassignment Worksheet to document the reassignments. The FSs send the Form 336.1, Reassignment Worksheet to the SCO as reassignments are made. When a Form 336.1, Reassignment Worksheet arrives in the office, the clerks update MOJO to reflect the new reassignment. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for procedures on reassigning AAs.

title: Conducting Telephone Interviews
content:
Clerks may need to conduct telephone interviews during the SC. The production clerk may conduct production telephone interviews for production. The production clerk conducts a production telephone interview when a FR is unable to make contact at a housing unit. The FR leaves Form SC-NV(E/S), Notice of Visit, which provides the SCO phone number so the respondent can complete the interview over the telephone.
The Quality Control (QC) clerk will conduct telephone reinterviews in instances when a telephone number is available. During telephone reinterview, a QC clerk may only complete Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire and they may also need to complete a full telephone interview using Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, based on responses provided during reinterview.
Sometimes an interview will need to be conducted in Spanish. In these instances, the cases should be reassigned to a Spanish speaking person. When this occurs, a Spanish version of the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, must be used. Also, a Spanish version of the label must be printed and affixed to the Spanish questionnaire before the questionnaire is checked in.

title: Production Clerks Conducting a Telephone Interview Using Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire
content:
When a phone call is received in the SCO and the caller refers to Form SC-NV(E/S) Notice of Visit for a SC, the production clerk must first ask the caller for their phone number in case the call becomes disconnected. The production clerk must also ask the caller to provide the following information, which is located on the bottom of the Notice of Visit:
- Case ID
- Line Number
- Which box is checked, SC-920, Address List Page or SC-921, Add Page
After receiving the requested information, the production clerk must use an unlabeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, to complete the telephone interview. The clerk hand writes the Case ID in the label section of an unlabeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. All entries on Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, must be made using a black ink ballpoint pen. Refer to Form SC-50.1, Special Census Office Job Aids for details on conducting a production telephone interview.
When the telephone interview is complete, the production clerk prints a label from MOJO that matches the Case ID the respondent provided from Form SC-NV(E/S) Notice of Visit. The production clerk affixes the label to the unlabeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. If a Spanish questionnaire is used, then a Spanish label must be printed and affixed to the completed Spanish questionnaire before the questionnaire is checked in.
During a telephone interview, if the caller refuses to answer questions, the production clerk records an Outcome Code of RE, Refusal in the Record of Contact section.
The production clerk completes the last page of the questionnaire. Refer to SC-50.1, Special Census Office Job Aids for instructions on completing the last page of the questionnaire.
The production clerk follows procedures in Chapter 13, to check-in Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire.
After the production clerk completes a telephone interview for a housing unit where the FR left Form SC-NV(E/S), they must notify the FM that the interview was conducted. The production clerk must provide the FM with the Case ID associated with the interview, the address, form number from Form SC-NV(E/S), Notice of Visit, line number from Form SC-NV(E/S), Notice of Visit, and the date when the interview was conducted. The FM must notify the FS, who then notifies the FR that the interview was completed via telephone at the SCO. The FR will be instructed to write a large X on each page of the questionnaire. When the questionnaire marked with a large X arrives at the SCO, the questionnaire should be held until confirmation of the version completed by the production clerk has been checked in to MOJO. Once confirmed, these questionnaires are boxed up and sent to the RO. The RO will destroy once them have received confirmation from NPC that all forms are scanned.
It is possible for the FR to complete Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, in a similar timeframe as when the production clerk completed the telephone interview. The system will notify the user, during check-in, if the questionnaire has already been checked in. If this happens, the production clerks must locate the initial version of the questionnaire and compare it to the subsequent version.
If the questionnaire completed the production clerk via telephone and the subsequent version of the questionnaires completed by the FR do not match, then refer both questionnaires to the SCS for guidance. If the SCS determines the version completed by the FR should be kept, then he or she checks the REP bin box in item E, Interview Outcome Code, in the Interview Summary on the questionnaire completed by the FR and the clerks checks in the questionnaire.
For the other form not accepted (but still needed since there is partial information), the SCO will cross out the barcode label and put the form in the box. For forms with duplicate barcode IDs, MOJO assumes one form only. So, if there\'s a duplicate that gets crossed out, it doesn\'t exist to MOJO. The SCO can put the form in any box they\'d like without scanning it into the system. Once the form arrives at NPC, NPC will affix an ATAC label over the crossed-out label so the form can be image scanned.

title: Replacement Materials
content:
In the event Address Registers and various questionnaires become lost, missing, or stolen, following these steps to request replacement materials.
*Address Registers*: NPC will need to print the entire register and overnight it to the SCO (including maps) and send the replacement register through Kiteworks to avoid delays. Address labels will be printed in the SCO from MOJO. If questionnaires were checked in, the clerk will place a check mark in column 3 on the SC-920 so the FR does not conduct another interview. The clerk must also transcribe address updates on SC-921 address list page. Recreate Add Page(s) based on SC-Qs for added housing units that have been received in the office and checked in. Follow initial preparation procedures to mark addresses that self-responded and mark cease contact and proceed with caution addresses that are dangerous. Check INFO COMMS to see if any GQ/TLs were added to the Add Page and make sure they are on the replacement materials.
*DQC Register*: NPC will need to reprint if lost during or after DQC. Office clerks needs to recreate the Add Pages in the SCO by looking at the checked in questionnaires. The clerks need to transcribe the adds on the Add Pages (based on checked in questionnaires). The HU status will need to be transcribed as well.
**SC-Q Production Questionnaire:** The office clerk prepares a questionnaire with a label and sends it to the FR.
**SC-RQ:** Follow same process as preparing for RI. Copy information from the production form onto the RI form.
**SC-20:** If replacing, the clerk lists all AAs, but writes a large X in section 1 when the AA is complete. If an AA is not complete, the clerk writes in assignment information, based on data in MOJO.
This page intentionally left blank.

title: Receiving Production Assignments from the Field
content:
The activities clerks perform as completed work from the field is returned to the Special Census Office (SCO) is the focus of this chapter. The clerks check work in to MOJO as it arrives to the SCO after production work is complete.
Clerks review Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire(s) and Address Registers for completeness and accuracy. If a Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire contains errors, the clerks attempt to resolve the issue in the office. If unable to resolve error in the office, Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire must be placed in Supplemental Reinterview. If Address Registers contain errors, clerks prepare Form SC-320, Error List, to go out with the Address Register during the Dependent Quality Check (DQC), and the Quality Control (QC) Field Supervisor (FS) corrects the documented errors while performing DQC.

title: Introduction
content:
Every completed Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, and Address Register is checked into MOJO after work is completed in the field. Every Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, and Address Register flows through several quality checks before they are sent to the National Processing Center (NPC) at the end of the operation.
The Special Census Supervisor (SCS) monitors workflow in the SCO to ensure that:
- Materials received from the field are sorted and routed to the appropriate areas of the SCO for various processing activities
- Completed Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, Forms SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, and Address Registers are promptly checked in to MOJO as they arrive in the office from the field
- Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire is prepared for Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, when selected for Reinterview
- Payroll forms, personnel forms, and other administrative forms are promptly processed
- Office reviews of completed Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaires, and Address Registers are promptly conducted
- Form SC-225, INFO-COMM containing information about added Group Quarters (GQs) and Transitory Locations (TLs), dangerous addresses, describing problems, procedural questions, safety concerns, supply requests, and other work-related issues are reviewed and resolved

title: Receiving and Sorting Production Work
content:
## Overview
Assignment Area (AA) materials are returned to the SCO on a flow basis as work is completed. Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires and Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaires are returned as interviews are completed. The Address Registers are returned after the entire AA has been completed.

title: Receiving and Sorting Area in the SCO
content:
The SCS and clerks organize work areas to receive and sort Special Census (SC) materials received from the field daily. The SCO staff use IN and OUT bin boxes for receiving and sorting materials. Separate IN and OUT bin boxes are needed for Form SC-Q Special Census Questionnaires, the Address Registers, and all other forms received in the office.
The SCO staff must always keep the receiving area neat and orderly by ensuring that incoming materials are placed in the appropriate bin boxes.
Most of the previous day's completed work from the field arrives in the morning; however, work may arrive in the SCO anytime throughout the day. The SCO may also receive group quarters and transitory location enumeration materials to check-in to MOJO. Refer to Group Quarters Enumeration and Transitory Locations Advance Contact (TLAC) and Enumeration at Transitory Locations (ETL) for the instructions to check-in the GQ and TL enumeration materials to MOJO.
It is recommended that at least one clerk should be in the SCO during the entire work shift. The materials received from the field contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Title 13 information and the SCO is responsible for ensuring that this information is distributed as quickly as possible and checked in to MOJO.

title: Reminders about Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire
content:
As Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires and Form SC-CQ, Special Census Questionnaires flow through the office, ensure that staff are aware of how to handle these materials.
- Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires tend to stick together because of static electricity. Be sure they are separated. This is especially important when the Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, are being checked into MOJO, because every Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, must be accounted for.
- If there are more than six people living in a housing unit, the Field Representative (FR) uses Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, to collect data for the additional persons. The FR is instructed to keep all continuation questionnaires together for housing units (HU) by placing Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire(s), inside the parent Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. Clerks must keep the SC-Q, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire(s), with the parent Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, throughout all office processes.
- Unlabeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, for added HUs do not need to be processed separately. They can be mixed with labeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires.
- Clerks must use a black ink ballpoint pen when marking questionnaires. Also, for Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, selected for Reinterview, clerks use a red pencil to write the letters RI on the Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, to indicate it was selected for reinterview. See Topic 3 for the instructions to check-in SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires and Reinterview selection.
- There is the potential to receive BOTH an English SC-Q and a Spanish SC-Q for a HU. Assuming the Spanish version is accepted, the office needs to print a Spanish label and then check-in ONLY the Spanish SC-Q. The English SC-Q must be placed in a destroy bin.

title: Overview of Production Check-In
Check-in Questionnaires
content: Production work is checked into MOJO as it arrives in the SCO. Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires and Address Registers are checked in to MOJO one at a time.

title: Check In Questionnaires and Continuation Questionnaires
content:
Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires and Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaires, are returned to the SCO as interviews are completed. Clerks check each Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, into MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for instructions on checking in Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires(s).
If an interview is conducted in Spanish, then a Spanish version of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, will be returned to the SCO, along with the corresponding English version of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. The English version of Form, SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, will be placed inside of the Spanish version. When a Spanish version of the questionnaire is used, then a Spanish label must be printed and affixed to the Spanish version of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, **[before]{.underline}** it is checked in. The corresponding English version of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, will have a large X on the front page. The corresponding English version must be placed in a destroy bin and not be checked in to MOJO.
The following data from the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, are scanned or keyed into MOJO upon check-in.
- Barcode ID label on front cover -- scanned or keyed.
![Image showing the location of the barcode ID on the front cover.](/images/imports/1/image21_579c69a3.png){width="3.8020833333333335in" height="1.9791666666666667in"}
- Name of FR who completed the interview -- keyed from the Certification section.
![Image showing the certification section of the SC-Q with the Field Representative\'s Signature field name highlighted.](/images/imports/1/image22_03d1e178.png){width="6.5in" height="1.28125in"}
- Key the following from the Interview Summary section of the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire.
![Image of the Interview Summary section of the SC-Q with items A, C, D, E, and F highlighted.](/images/imports/1/image23_c942c0bb.png){width="6.5in" height="2.5034722222222223in"}
- Unit Status-- keyed from Item A .
- Number of People listed on questionnaire(s) -- keyed from Item C.
- POP Count is 7 or more -- the system prompts for the SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire(s). The clerk follows the system prompts to check these in.
- Language code -- keyed from Item D.
- Interview Outcome Code -- keyed from Item E.
- **Usual Home Elsewhere (UHE)** -- This option is marked when the respondent lives in a usual home elsewhere on the Special Census Day. 
- **Refusal (RE)** -- This option is marked when the FR is instructed by the FS to mark the outcome code as a refusal when a case is determined to be a refusal versus having another FR work the address. 
- **Replacement (REP)** -- This option is only marked by office staff in the SCO for a replacement questionnaire. 
- **Movers (MOV)** -- This option is marked for address with movers. 
- **Closeout (CO)** -- This option is used at the end of the operation to close the remaining cases. The FS instructs the FR when to make this option. Also used when an FR has visited the address the maximum six times and wasn't able to make contact. 
- Number of Continuation Questionnaires -- keyed from Item F.
If the questionnaire is for an added housing unit, the clerks also enter the following information into MOJO:
![Image of the SC-Q that shows highlighted fields where the clerk gets the information they key into MOJO for an added housing unit. The fields SCID, State, County, AA, Tract Block are highlighted, as is the Added Unit Address or Address Changes section.](/images/imports/1/image24_fc304064.png){width="6.5in" height="4.05in"}
- SCID, State, County, Tract, Block, and AA from the header section of the questionnaire
- The complete address which includes the house number, street name, unit designation (if present), and ZIP Code; or street name, unit designation (if present), location description, and ZIP Code
- If there are Forms SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, then MOJO prompts the clerk to check-in each Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, associated with the parent Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire.
- As Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, are checked-in, MOJO randomly selects cases for Reinterview. If a case is selected for RI, the clerk writes the letters RI in red pencil on the upper-right corner of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. The clerk sets the case aside so the information can be transcribed to the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. While MOJO selects cases for RI upon check-in of the SC-Q from production, the SC-RQ can be printed after check-in.
- Place Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires that are not selected for Reinterview in office review. See Topic 6 for more information on questionnaire office review.

title: Preparing the Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
content:
Preparing Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, should be completed in the afternoon when most or all the Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, have been checked into MOJO. Clerks conduct Reinterview in the SCO if a respondent telephone number is available. Reinterview FRs also conduct RI in the field. Production clerks prepare Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, for Reinterview. QC clerks conduct the Reinterview in the office if a telephone number is available. QC clerks have three attempts to conduct the telephone Reinterview. If the QC clerks are unable to complete the telephone Reinterview in three attempts, then the Reinterview will be assigned to a RI FR. Reinterview FRs conduct reinterview in the field, if a QC clerk is unable to complete the telephone Reinterview in three attempts or if a telephone number is not available.
It is important that the clerk who prepares Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, is not the same clerk that may conduct the Reinterview over the telephone.
Reinterview is an independent check of the contents of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. For this reason, the clerk that makes the telephone call for the Reinterview should not have prior knowledge of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, responses.
At the end of the day, the clerks:
- Print Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, from MOJO for Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, that were selected for Reinterview for the day. Form SC-RQ, Special Census Questionnaire, contains a printed barcode ID. Refer to the SC- 445, User Guide for the MOJO for the instructions on how to print Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
- Print the appropriate English or Spanish version of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, to match the version used for the production interview. MOJO provides an indicator of whether the production interview was conducted in English or Spanish on the screen used to print Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
- For known addresses (SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires with a label), check MOJO to determine if the address is a known dangerous address flagged as proceed with caution. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for the instructions on determining whether an address is flagged as proceed with caution by reviewing information on the screen for printing the SC-RQ.
