- If the address is dangerous and flagged as proceed with caution, then add a note in the Notes section on the bottom of the back of the corresponding Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. Include the reason the address is dangerous and a note to inform the FR to proceed with caution when approaching the address.
- Dangerous addresses that are cease contact and new dangerous addresses added will not be eligible for RI, since they are coded as cannot work during production.
- Transcribe items R1, R2, R3, and R4 in the Respondent Information from Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire onto the corresponding SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire Original Respondent's Information section.
- Item R1, First and Last Name to OR1, Original Respondent's Name.
- Item R1 (Address of proxy) to OR4, Address -- Address of Neighbor or Proxy.
- Item R2 to OR2, Telephone number.
- Item R3 to OR3, Original respondent type.
- OR4, Address -- Neighbor or Proxy only, is left blank if R3 is marked Live or stay in this \[house/apartment/mobile home\] on the Special Census Date or Move into this \[house/apartment/mobile home\] after the Special Census Date.
- If not live of stay in this \[house/apartment/mobile home\] is checked in R3, then the clerk enters the Address of proxy from R1 and telephone number from R2, into OR2 in the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
Refer to Figure 21 for an example of the completed Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
Figure 21. Example showing how information is transcribed from the SC-Q to the SC-RQ when a respondent lived at the address on Special Census Day.
![Diagram Description automatically generated with medium confidence](/images/imports/1/image25_d6b8e9d0.png){width="6.5in" height="6.572222222222222in"}

title: Preparing Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
content:
Refer to Figure 22 for an example of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
Figure 22. Example showing how information is transcribed from the SC-Q to the SC-RQ when a respondent did not live at the address on Special Census Day.
![A picture containing table Description automatically generated](/images/imports/1/image26_a5811922.png){width="6.5in" height="6.172916666666667in"}
After transcribing Forms SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires for the day, the clerks place the original Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires selected for Reinterview in office review. Follow procedures in Section 1, Questionnaire Review in Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials.
After office review is completed, the original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, is placed in a secured temporary bin box in the Reinterview area until the corresponding Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire is completed.
When Form SC-RQ, Special Census Questionnaire is completed and returned to the office, the clerk compares the original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire to the completed SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire to determine whether the Field Representative followed the Special Census procedures. Refer to [Chapter 16: Quality Control Operations](#quality-control-operations) for information on Matching Review.

title: Check-in Address Register
content:
## Overview
Address Registers are returned to the SCO after all listing for an Assignment Area (AA) is complete. As AAs arrive in the SCO, the Clerks check-in each Address Register and conduct a quality check of the completed work.

title: Check-in Address Register
content:
Clerks check-in Address Registers through MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for instructions on checking in Address Registers. The clerks:
- Retrieve Address Registers from the *IN* bin.
- Scan the barcode ID from the cover of the Address Register into MOJO.
![Image showing the barcode and other information at the top of the Address Register including AA Number, SCID, State, Tract, County, barcode graphic, and barcode number. ](/images/imports/1/image27_42269d63.png){width="5.548780621172353in" height="2.9651290463692037in"}
- Select/confirm the name of the Field Representative that completed the Address Register.
![Image showing that the clerk gets the FR name from row (b) of the Address Register Cover Page.](/images/imports/1/image28_1536f011.png){width="6.5in" height="2.811111111111111in"}
- Enter the number of lines used on Form SC-921, Add Page into MOJO.
![Image showing that the clerk can find the numbers of lines on the SC-921 by looking for the last night number. In this example, the last line that has an address on it is line 9.](/images/imports/1/image29_b1be7c48.png){width="6.5in" height="2.857638888888889in"}
- Draw a line, using red pencil, under the last address added for Form SC-921, Add Page, during production.
- If there are no adds on Form SC-921, Add Page, then write *NO ADDS* in red pencil in the first row of Form SC-921, Add Page.
- Conduct an Office Review of the Address Register, following procedures in Section 2, Address Register Review in Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, prior to preparing the Address Register for DQC.
- Prepare the Address Register for DQC. Refer to [Chapter 16: Quality Control Operations](#quality-control-operations) for steps to prepare the Address Register for DQC.

title: Erroneous Adds
content: Addresses added in error are referred to as erroneous adds. If an address was added in error, it can be deleted in MOJO. Refer to SC-445 User Guide for the MOJO for instructions on deleting an erroneous add.

title: Check-in Other Forms
content:
## Overview
Other forms are returned to the SCO throughout the operation. These forms include:
- Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist
- Form SC-225, INFO-COMM
- Form SC-308, Daily Pay and Work Record
- Miscellaneous items, such as notes or letters
The items should be sorted as they arrive in the SCO and routed to the appropriate area for processing or resolution.

title: Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist
content:
Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, is used by the Field Supervisor (FS) during Field Representative observations to determine whether the Field Representatives are performing the work according to the Special Census procedures. Refer to [Chapter 16, Topic 2](#initial-observations) for more information about the observation checklist and its uses.
The Field Supervisor conducts an observation for each Field Representative and completes Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, within the first week of the operation. The SCO should expect Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, for every Field Representative to arrive in the SCO within the first two weeks of the operation.
Clerks in the SCO enter data from Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, into MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for instructions on entering data from Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, into MOJO.
The clerks:
- Retrieve Forms SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, from the IN bin.
- Ensure that items 1 through 9 in the top section of Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist are completed. If any information is missing, prepare Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, and send it back to the FS for resolution.
![Image showing the fields the FS enters when doing an observation: 4. Observer ID, 5. Date, 9. Task, and the recommendation outcome in Section II.](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.5in" height="2.5708333333333333in"}
- Enter the result from Section II - Recommendation of Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, into MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for instructions on entering observation results.
![Image showing Section II of the Special Census Observation Checklist, with the Continue assigning work, Additional observation, and Consult manager boxes highlighted to indicate that the FS must select one of these boxes after completing an observation.](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.458333333333333in" height="1.3645833333333333in"}

title: INFO-COMMs Review
content:
Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, is completed in the field for several reasons, including when GQs and TLs are added to Form SC-921, Add Page, and when dangerous addresses are identified. Some issues documented on Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, require resolution by the Special Census Supervisor. Some examples of issues to resolve include requesting additional enumeration materials, requesting guidance, or informing the Special Census Supervisor about performance or conduct issues, and requesting guidance for issues related to field activities.
Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, contains three copies. The original or top copy is sent to the SCO. Copies 1 and 2 remain with the initial receiver and sender, respectively.
A common issue encountered in the field is gaining access to multi-unit buildings or gated communities that deny access to Special Census Field Representatives. The Special Census Supervisor can request the RO send a letter to a building manager or administrator to request access to a building or community. A sample of this letter is in []{.mark}Appendix E. Consult the RO for guidance on how to manage access issues.
When a new GQ or TL is found during listing, the FR completes Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, by checking the Added GQ/TL/TNSOL box, writes the address, name of the GQ or TL, contact person name and phone number, and the Add Page line number for the listing. The FRs provide Form SC_225, INFO-COMM, to the FS during their scheduled meeting. The FS calls the office to report the information for the new GQ or TL. New GQs and TLs need to be added to MOJO immediately to ensure they are added to the workload and completed by the end of the operation. Refer to Form SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for procedure to enter a new GQ or TL into MOJO. Additionally, the Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, containing the information that was called into the office about the new GQ or TL will be sent to the SCO. Upon receipt of Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, in the office, clerks must verify that the information on Form SC-225, INFO-COMM was correctly entered into MOJO.
Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, is also used to report dangerous addresses encountered in the field. In situations where Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, is submitted due to a dangerous address, the form will be placed inside the respective Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. When Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, is used to report a dangerous address, the SCO must communicate, to the RO, the address, and the reason it is dangerous. The RO enters the information into the Dangerous Address Database.
After Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, has been reviewed and resolved, be sure to remove the INFO-COMM from inside the questionnaire and store it in the appropriate bin box.

title: SC-308, Daily Pay and Work Record
content: Form SC-308, Daily Pay and Work Record is used by field staff to document the date, times and hours worked as well as miles driven. Form SC-308 is returned to the SCO daily. Form SC-308 must be routed to the Administrative area for review and keying into GovTA.

title: Office Review of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire
content:
## Overview
After checking the production work in, the clerk conducts an office review of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires as they arrive in the SCO on a flow basis as interviews are completed to ensure that the entries are legible and completed with a black ink ballpoint pen. The clerks also make sure that Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, pages are not torn, damaged, or wrinkled.
Clerks conducting office review of the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, perform the following tasks:
- Conduct a review to ensure all Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, have entries for required items. Refer to Section 1 -- Questionnaire Review on Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials.
- If an error is found in the Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, the clerks attempt to correct the error in the office. The clerk may call the Supervisor to obtain the needed information. A black ink ballpoint pen must be used to make corrections. All entries must be legible. Cross out incorrect entries with a single line and write the correct information in all capital letters near the crossed-out entry.
- If errors are resolved in the office, Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, can be placed in storage.
- If errors are not resolved in the office, Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, must be placed in Supplemental RI.

title: Office Review of Questionnaires
content: The clerks review several sections of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, to determine if the information was captured. Refer to Section 1 -- Questionnaire Review, Part A, Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, Part B, Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, and Part C Certifications of the SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, for details on conducting office review.

title: Production Address Register Office Review
content:
## Overview
After the Production Address Registers are checked-in, the clerks perform an office review on every Address Register.
Clerks conducting office review on the Production Address Registers: perform the following tasks:
- Conduct a review to ensure every Address Register was updated appropriately and was returned with all the applicable contents. Refer to Section 2 -- Address Register Review on Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials.
- Attempt to correct errors in the office by contacting the FS. If the error is not resolved in the office, the clerks prepare Form SC- 320, Error List, to document the error(s) that need resolution. During DQC, the QC FS resolved the errors on the SC-320, Error List.

title: Production Address Register Office Review
content:
The clerks review every Address Register after the Production work is complete. Refer to Section 2 -- Address Register Review of the SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials for details on conducting Production Address Register office review.
Refer to for instructions on preparing the Address Register for DQC.

title: Group Quarters Enumeration
content:
## Group Quarters Introduction
Group quarters (GQ) are places where people live or stay in a group living arrangement that is owned or managed by an entity or organization providing housing and/or services for the residents. These services may include custodial or medical care as well as other types of assistance, and residency is commonly restricted to those receiving these services. This is not a typical household-type living arrangement. People living in GQs are usually not related to each other. Group Quarters Enumeration (GQE) covers Group Quarters Advanced Contact (GQAC), GQE and Service-Based Enumeration (SBE).

title: Group Quarters Advance Contact
content:
Before we can enumerate group quarters, we must first let the GQ staff know that we are coming and explain the enumeration process to them. We do this during GQAC, which has two components:
- An office operation when clerks call to collect certain information about each GQ to plan for enumeration and enter the information into MOJO.
- A field operation to follow up on any Unresolved cases from the phone operation where a Field Representative (FR) conducts GQAC in person at those locations. Unresolved cases can include:
- Phone interview was not completed
- Contact Person did not set an enumeration appointment
- Case status is Nonresidential
- Refusal
- 999 GQ Type Code that has not been updated
Clerks key in the information collected during the field into MOJO. When the GQAC operation is over, its workload becomes the GQE workload.

title: Group Quarters Enumeration
content: The GQE counts individuals who reside in group settings. Not everyone lives in a house, apartment, or mobile home. Some people live or stay in group settings. Counting individuals where they live or stay requires the use of specially designed operations. These operations are called GQE and SBE. The SBE operation is a part of the GQE operation. Enumeration is another word for counting. The GQE operation will count people who live or stay at GQs such as skilled-nursing facilities, hospitals, correctional facilities, group homes, residential treatment centers, and college residence halls.

title: Service-Based Enumeration
content: Some people do not have a usual residence and often get assistance and meals at service-based locations. The SBE operation is a subset of GQE. It is conducted at places where people experiencing homelessness stay overnight, such as emergency and transitional shelters. SBE also includes Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Locations (TNSOLs). For Special Census (SC), FRs will only enumerate Emergency and Transitional Shelters and TNSOLs in teams.

title: Emergency and Transitional Shelters
content:
Emergency and Transitional Shelters (with sleeping facilities) for People Experiencing Homelessness. They include:
- Shelters that operate on a first-come first-serve basis, where people must leave in the morning and have no guaranteed bed for the next night.
- Shelters where people know they have a bed for a specified period (even if they leave the building every day).
- Shelters that provide temporary shelter during extremely cold weather (such as churches). This category does not include shelters that operate only in the event of a natural disaster.

title: Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Locations
content: The SBE operation also includes outdoor locations where people experiencing homelessness live without paying to stay. We call these places Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Locations'. TNSOLs differ from TLs because they are locations where people are unlikely to live year-round due to the transitory/temporary/impermanent nature of the location. People living in these locations are counted in places such as alleys, under bridges, and in parks.

title: Group Quarters Requiring Unique Procedures during Special Census
content: There are some GQ facilities that require unique procedures during the SC. The SCO needs to know about these GQs exceptions to handle them appropriately. The GQs that fall into this exception group are GQs on American Indian Reservations (AIRS), Domestic Violence Shelters (DVS), GQs on military installations, Salvation Army and TNSOLs. There are currently no special enumeration procedures for GQs that are part of the Salvation Army. Should the SCO staff find any of these GQs in their assignments, refer them to the Field Manager (FM).

title: American Indian Reservations (AIRS)
content: There are special procedures to enumerate GQs on AIRS. AIRS cases are only assigned to residents of the AIRS and SCO staff at the supervisory level. The SCO will determine the staff who enumerates these cases.

title: Domestic Violence Shelters
content:
DVSs are shelters that house individuals fleeing emotional, sexual, and physical abuse. DVS can be community-based homes, crisis centers or shelters. This operation requires discretion and is extremely sensitive. The identity and addresses of these shelters are kept strictly confidential, and steps will be taken in MOJO so that information about these places is not available to everyone that works on the system.
Clerks will not contact a DVS. If a DVS is inadvertently on the list of GQs, you are to contact the FM or SCS immediately for further guidance. The FM or SCS will inform the clerk to not discuss the case any further. DVSs are managed separately from the regular GQ workload and are not enumerated.
If a DVS is discovered during AC (before interviewing):
1. Select **Cannot Locate** in item 27 of the INFO-COMM, as shown in the following image.
![](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.499187445319335in" height="1.062367672790901in"}
9. Write ***Special situation*** in the notes section as shown in the following image.
![](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png)
10. Select **Cannot Locate** on item 34 on the INFO-COMM, as shown in the following image. The GQ is closed out and stays in the SCO.
![](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.499187445319335in" height="1.4685662729658793in"}
If a DVS is discovered as DVS ***after­*** AC - assuming code in item 27 is complete and FR goes to GQ and discovers it is a DVS:
1. Complete a Form SC-225, INFO-COMM. On the form, indicate the name and address of the Domestic Violence Shelter.
2. Once the SC-116, blank ICQ forms, and INFO-COMM are returned to the SCO, the SCO will mark item 34 as cannot locate.

title: Military Installations
content:
Military installation GQs include barracks, bachelor officer quarters, base hospitals, base stockades, and so forth. There is a possibility that a military installation may fall within the SC area. If that is the case, a Regional Office (RO) manager or the SCS will conduct the initial contact. The clerks will not contact military installations to set up enumeration appointments. If there are military installations in your assignment, tell your supervisor. The RO manager or SCS will use the SC-351 *Special Census Group Quarters Advance* *Contact Script* to set up an enumeration appointment with the installation.
Regardless of enumeration method chosen by the military, the initial contact is handled by both the RO manager and the SCS. There may be additional security procedures that must be followed. When the installation is contacted, the contact person is asked to provide a list of the installation's GQs and the approximate population for each GQ.
Military installations will be enumerated if they are inside the SC enumeration area. Military installations, in most cases, contain housing units (HU) as well as group quarters. Enumerating people at military installations requires careful planning since they operate under the need for extreme privacy. They also need to protect standard routine activities against disruption. If there are HU within the military installation, then they will be enumerated by the HU operation.

title: Salvation Army
content: When you arrive at a Salvation Army location, they may change their method of enumeration. Please accommodate them. Also, accept the information they provide the first time and do not ask for more data. They will not provide any names on the enumeration materials, and we accept that. No follow up after the review of the ICQs.

title: Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Locations
content:
The FM or SCS assign staff to go by these locations to complete a much of the advance contact information as they can on the Control Record. This is done so the assignment materials can be prepped in the office. If there is a gatekeeper, that person needs to be identified as the contact person on the Control Record. This person can be of help in gaining cooperation from the residents. The other two items that need to be completed on the GQ Control Record are how many people stay at this location and the best time to visit.
TNSOL Enumeration is generally conducted late at night into the early morning, between the hours of 12:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. There is an exception, locations (such as parking lots or parks) that serve as places for individuals sleeping in cars and/ or trucks are enumerated early night hours starting at 9:00 p.m. A TNSOL must have a specific location description; for example, the Brooklyn Bridge at the corner of Bristol Drive or the 700 block of Taylor Street behind the old warehouse. SCO staff must be prepared because some TNSOLs may change depending on weather conditions. The SCO will receive additional guidance from the RO as to when to conduct these types of enumeration, as they will choose an appropriate or convenient time to conduct this operation.
**Types of Enumeration Methods**
Enumeration methods refer to the approach used for data collection. There are three methods of enumeration used during SC. They are:
- In-Person Interview -- a team of FRs conducts a personal interview with each resident who was served or was staying at the facility on Special Census Day using the Individual Census Questionnaire (ICQ).
- Administrative Records -- The FR collects an administrative list that has certain demographic data about each resident who was served or was staying at the facility on Special Census Day.
- Drop Off/Pick Up -- The FR leaves an ICQ for each resident who was staying at the facility on Special Census Day to fill out and return to a contact person at the GQ by a set date and time.
The enumeration method used is chosen by the GQ Administrator during the Group Quarters Advance Contact.

title: Group Quarters Staff and Responsibilities
content:
## Staffing Overview
A FR or a designated staff will conduct the enumeration of the GQ in the SC. Trainees will receive the entire production training followed by a GQ specific training.
If the SCO is conducting HU and GQE, all trainees will attend the FR training. FRs assigned to the GQE operation will also receive GQE training. The trainer will use the SC-669.12, Special Census Group Quarters Enumeration Guide for Training FRs to train the GQ FRs.
The SCS or designated FS will already be assigned the GQ for enumeration. After training, the supervisor coordinates with his or her team to make assignments based on the information on the Form SC-116, Group Quarters Control Record. The FR receives their assignments from their supervisor who gives them materials to conduct the enumeration. The GQE might happen immediately after training or shortly thereafter.
The staffing will depend on the estimated number of people that will be enumerated at the facility and the method of enumeration selected for the facility. It is possible that if there are several small group quarters in the workload, the SCS or designated supervisor can handle these alone
There will be instances where the supervisor will need a team of FRs, for example, at large facilities such as prisons or hospitals. This is especially true at TNSOLs, where these locations must be enumerated by a team of FRs.
The SCS needs to determine which FRs to assign to the GQ operation so they can be trained in the GQ procedures. The SCS should assign FRs that live nearby the GQs that will be enumerated.

title: Service-Based Enumeration Staffing
content:
As previously mentioned, SBE operation is a subset of GQE. It is conducted at places where people experiencing homelessness stay overnight, such as emergency and transitional shelters. SBE also include TNSOLs.
For SC, FRs will enumerate Emergency and Transitional Shelters and TNSOLs in teams. Teams are created based on the number of expected population (expected pop) at the SBE location. The SCO assigns one (1) FR for every twenty (20) respondents when enumeration is conducted at shelters. At minimum there should be at least two (2) for shelter enumerations. For the SC this would be the Supervisor plus one FR. For unusually large shelters, more than one team may be assigned to conduct the enumeration.
The SCO will use its best judgement based on the expected pop to determine if only 1 team or several teams are required to conduct the shelter enumeration. Knowing the hours operation for the shelter is critical to having a successful enumeration. SCO staff must be organized and work quickly complete the enumeration. Shelter enumerations must be conducted as close to SC Date as possible.
Each team will consist of the team leader and the team members. The team leader oversees coordinating enumeration at the given shelter. It is important for the team leader to plan and create the teams by writing the team members names on a piece of paper then an alphabetic designation next to their name. This is particularly helpfully when tracking the work completed by the different team members. The team leader should make it clear to the team that this is the only time they can conduct the enumeration. There will not be an opportunity to return to the shelter. The team leader makes all assignments, and hands out the enumeration materials to the team on the day of enumeration. Once at the GQ, the team leader meets with the contact person to discuss the enumeration and the best method for collecting the required information at the shelter. The team will then enumerate all residents and turn in the completed work.
The number of ICQs completed should equal the number of ICQs the FR reports that they have completed. The team leader writes this by their name on the control sheet. After adding up the totals and checking to ensure that all forms are collected, the Record is completed and signed.

title: Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Locations (TNSOLS)
content:
Staff needs to be very careful when working at these locations. There are guidelines the staff will follow to be safe and effective during this operation. Even though this type of location can be enumerated using one person, one person alone will not be allowed to enumerate an outdoor location. A team is needed to conduct this enumeration. One FR must watch over the whole team and if there is any cause for concern, everyone should leave the area immediately. The SCS or designated supervisor must account for everyone in their team.
A team will never go into a TNSOL or an encampment by themselves or volunteer to stay behind to finish the enumeration. The supervisor will always pair off with another FR and always be aware of your surroundings.
When conducting enumerations at TNSOLs, the creation of teams will be slightly different. The SCO assigns teams of four or more FRs for each TNSOL. When making the assignments, you should give each team only enough work that they can enumerate that day. You want to use each team efficiently but must make sure you have enough teams to complete the SBE enumeration in one day. Each site is only enumerated once. When you arrive at the encampment, the SCS or designate supervisor will introduce themselves to the gatekeeper, if there is one. A gatekeeper is someone that knows everyone at the encampment and is trusted by them.
Having a gatekeeper would greatly facilitate the enumeration at an outdoor location. The team will then:
- Ask the gatekeeper to let everyone at the encampment know that the Census Bureau is conducting an enumeration.
- Enumerate quickly and diligently.
- Interview everyone at the encampment, including children.
You will also be enumerating people in pre-identified cars, Recreational Vehicles (RVs) and tent encampments. The encampments are ad-hoc locations where people who have no usual home elsewhere are not paying to stay. Examples can be cars and RVs in large department store and municipal parking lots. Included in this example are encampments on open lots and undeveloped land. These encampments **do not** include RV parks and campgrounds where people pay to stay.
Please see the GQ FR Manual for more SBE Guidelines for Safety Tips.

title: Military Installations
content:
Military installations can include HU and transitory locations (TLs) as well as GQs. This includes all branches of the service and the Coast Guard. The enumeration at military installations requires careful coordination because the need to operate under the need for extreme privacy, the need to protect standard routine activities against disruption, and safety issues for the visiting Census Bureau staff as well as for the residents of the facility. It is likely that GQs inside military installations will be enumerated through administrative records. During the Initial Contact to the facility, the SCS or a Census Representative spoke to a point-of-contact person and arrangements were made to enumerate the base. The SCS needs to build a team that will enumerate each area at the base. It is suggested to determine ahead of time if HUs need to be enumerated at the base, so a team of FRs complete the HU enumeration at the time when the GQ enumeration is scheduled. The SCS or other RO manager will discuss the details about enumerating the military installation at the initial meeting with the governmental unit.
**Special Census Office Staff Responsibilities**
SCO Supervisor and Managers are responsible for supervising the work conducted in the office and the enumeration activities in the field. They are expected to supervise the work of the staff who conduct In-Office GQAC, prepare materials for In-Field GQAC and GQE operation. Managers will also:
- Review or approve the workload by reviewing GQs added by FRs in the field,
- Provide the clerks with their assignments
- Check that approved adds are entered into MOJO,
- Check that clerks call each GQ in the GQAC workload using the SC-351, *GQ Advance Contact Script* and complete the SC-116, *GQ Control Record* which includes scheduling an enumeration appointment. Please note that the SC-116, GQ Control Record is used for Advance Contact and Enumeration.
- Check that the clerks prepare materials for any GQs that must go to the In-Field GQAC operation.
- Check that the clerks have printed the SC-116 (CP), *GQ Control Record Continuation Pages* as part of the preparation for GQE and SBE operations.
- Supervise any assignment preparation
- Supervise staff production and quality control phases
- Identify the staff to enumerate the GQs
- Train the staff on GQAC and enumeration procedures.
The SCO Managers will use Form SC-1055(GQE), *Special Census Supervisor Checklist*, to do the review of the completed enumeration materials.
The SCS or another supervisor in the SCO will select and appoint the staff that will work on the GQ operations.
First is the GQ Advanced Contact operation which requires selection of office clerks and FRs. The office clerks and FRs are trained by a supervisor. The clerks call the GQs assigned to them and conduct an interview using the SC-351, GQ Advanced Contact Script. The answers provided by the GQ contact are written on the SC-116, GQ Control Record. If the interview cannot be completed or there is some other issue with the case preventing a completed interview, the case then goes to the in-field GQAC.
The clerk gives the SC-116, GQ Control Record for any incomplete or unresolved case to the supervisor. The supervisor assigns the case to a FR who will conduct an in-person interview, if possible. The FR reviews any notes on the Control Record from the clerk and goes to the GQ to do an interview. The FR uses the GQAC script and writes any additional information on the Control Record the supervisor provided. After the FR has completed the case, the Control Record comes back to the SCO. The Control Record is also used during enumeration operations.
In many cases, the FS will assign a FR to enumerate a GQs. In the situation of a large GQ and during SBE operations, the FS creates a team of enumerators from their FRs. One FR is selected to be the lead FR in charge of enumerating the large GQ or SBE.
The GQ Field Supervisor or lead FR and their respective teams will:
- Visit the GQ on the scheduled day and time,
- Introduce themselves to the contact person and explain how the GQ enumeration will be conducted,
- Conduct GQ enumeration using the GQ contact's chosen enumeration method of In-Person Interview, Drop-off/Pick-up, or Administrative records,
- Verify all questionnaires are turned in, review questionnaires and other enumeration materials, and
- Turn in completed materials to the SCO.
**Clerks Responsibilities**
SCO clerk plays an integral part in GQ operations because they support the operations through the following tasks:
- Inventory GQ kits and bulk supply materials received.
- Assemble training materials.
- Print SC-116, GQ Control Records.
- Conduct In-Office GQAC.
- Perform a variety of tasks using MOJO.
- Prepare GQE and SBE field assignment materials.
- Review completed materials and check in completed materials.
The clerk will use Form SC-1056(GQE/SBE), *Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist*, to do the review.

title: Group Quarters Advance Contact Overview
content:
## Group Quarters Advance Contact Introduction
To update group quarters information and schedule the enumeration for each facility, you use the GQAC script. Collecting this information gives the SCO valuable data to prepare for enumeration operations.
During the GQAC operation, you identify someone at each GQ to serve as the contact person. During the phone interview:
- Explain the SC to the contact person.
- Explain the enumeration procedures for Service-Based or GQE to the contact person.
- Ask the GQ contact to select a method of enumeration appropriate for their GQ.
- Update information about each GQ such as the GQ name, GQ Type Code, maximum population, expected population, address, and the contact person's information, including name, telephone number, and title.
- Set an enumeration appointment.
- Gain cooperation from the contact person by explaining confidentiality issues and ask that the contact person let their residents/clients know that all information that the Census Bureau collects is confidential.

title: Group Quarters Advance Contact Assignment Preparation
content: The office and field staff need the materials in the following table to do GQAC.

title: SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control Record
content: The SC-116, Special Census GQ Control Record contains all the pre-GQAC information about the GQs. Clerk and FRs use the SC-116, Special Census GQ Control Record to conduct GQAC. Must print one for each GQ in the SCO workload.

title: SC-116(CP), Group Quarters Control Record Continuation Page
content: Used to create a list or roster of the GQ. FR fills in each resident's information on the SC-116(CP) as they conduct interviews or create ICQ packets for drop off /pick up.

title: SC-351, Special Census GQ Advance Contact Script
content: GQAC Script guides the clerk and FR through the interview. Tells the staff what and where to fill in the answers on the GQ Control Record.

title: SC-637, GQ Type Code Job Aid
content: Used to help determine the correct GQ Type Code if the current code is incorrect or there a new GQ

title: SC-640, GQ Frequently Asked Questions
content:
Provides answers that respondents may ask during an interview that are not covered in the GQ materials.
As part of GQAC assignment prep, you need a printout of the GQ workload. As the GQ control records are printed out, check them off the workload printout. As cases are given to the staff, you can write their names on the printout as well. You must have a control record for every GQ in the SC enumeration area.

title: Group Quarters Advance Contact Tasks
content:
In addition to the items listed above during the GQAC operation, the clerk or FR will:
- Check the materials and make sure they have everything to do their job.
- Collect the expected population count.
- Write the data from the interview onto the contact record.
- Address concerns related to confidentiality, legal, and security matters.
- Document any issues on the control record and INFO-COMM.
- Turn in the completed materials to their supervisor.

title: SC-920, Address Listing Page
content: The SC-920, *Address Listing Page* contains known addresses for the block(s) listed in the Assignment Area (AA). The information on the SC-920, *Address Listing Page* will be pre-printed on the form.

title: SC-920, Address Listing Page Columns
content:
The SC-920, Address Listing Page consists of a header, a body that is divided into 17 items, and the footer. The address listing page will include every known address in the AA as well as the GQ(s) you will visit. The following image is an example of the SC-920, Address Listing Page.
![](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.5in" height="4.071527777777778in"}

title: Header Information
content:
The first line at the top of each page informs you that the SC-920, Address Listing Page, contains the confidentiality statement including Title 13 and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) information, both of which are protected by the Privacy Act of 1974.
The remaining information in the header identifies the report by form number and name, and the geographic location of the addresses.
The following information is entered in the heading of the form:
- SCID: The 5-digit number identifying your SCO.
- AA: The 6-digit number identifying the AA.
- Page \_\_ of \_\_: Indicates the current page and the total number of pages.
The body of the form contains 17 items, each briefly described below:

title: Item (1), Line No.
content:
Every line on the SC-920, Address Listing Page, has a line number on item 1. This includes lines for blocks that have no living quarters (NLQ) in them. Usually, the lines are numbered in sequential order, beginning with line number 1 on the first page of the Address List and ending with the last address (or NLQ, if applicable) on the last page of the Address List.
Every address is given a line number, starting with 1 and increasing sequentially.
Since you will only receive the page or pages with the GQ(s) assigned to you, the pages might start with numbers other than 1. The rest of the address listed will then be consecutive starting from the number at the top of the page.

title: Item (2), Case ID
content:
All addresses on the SC-920, Address Listing Page have a 12-digits Case ID. This number uniquely identifies each address in the address listing page. This code uniquely identifies the address and matches the Case ID printed on the labeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, for HU addresses or on the SC-116, GQ Control Record.
Note: If a block contains no known living quarters, one line for the block will appear on the Form SC-920, Address List Page. The block number will be entered in Column (9), Block No., and *No known LQs in this block* will be entered in Column (12), Street or Road Name. Xs will be entered in several columns on the same line.

title: Item (3), Special Situations
content: If X is entered, do not make contact at the address (skip and continue canvassing). If PC (proceed with caution) is entered, work the address as usual but be aware that residents may not want you on their property.

title: Item (4), Action Code
content: If X is entered, do not make contact at the address (skip and continue canvassing). Otherwise, after completing a questionnaire for the address, enter the appropriate code to indicate the address's status. In some situations, you will not complete this item until meeting with your supervisor.

title: Item (5) Date Listed
content: This item does not apply to GQ, but only completed for HU addresses. You will leave this item blank. Item 5 is where enumerators conducting the housing unit enumeration will enter when they completed a Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire for that address.

title: Item (6) Date SC-Q Completed
content: This item does not apply to GQ, but only completed for HU addresses. You will leave this column blank. Item 6 is where enumerators conducting the housing unit enumeration will enter when they completed a Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire for that address.

title: Item (7), Address Status
content: Displays the status of the living quarters: housing unit (HU), group quarters (GQ), or transitory location (TL).

title: Item (8), Address Type
content: Indicates if the housing unit address is a single unit (S), multi-unit (M), trailer/mobile home (T), or other (O) type of structure, if known.

title: Item (9), Block No.
content: Displays the Block Number where the provided address is located.

title: Item (10), Map Spot No.
content: If known, the location of the structure containing the address is indicated on the corresponding Block Map by a dot (map spot) and number. This same number appears in Item (10).

title: Item (11), Address No.
content: Displays the address number assigned to the structure, if known.

title: Item (12), Street or Road Name
content:
This item contains a street or road name, a rural route and box number or a P.O. Box number for where the address is located. Roads without a known name may display as:
- UN RD -- Public, unnamed road
- PR RD -- Private, unnamed road (such as a driveway)
- VE TR -- Vehicular trail, usable only by a 4-wheel drive vehicle

title: Item (13) Physical Location Description
content: If an address number and street name are not known for an address, a physical description or location description for the address is displayed here. An example of a description might be *House 1/10 mile north from intersection of Baseline Rd. & Front St, east side of Front St*. This column may also include the name of the GQ.

title: Item (14) GQ or TL Name /Facility Name
content: If the address identifies a GQ or TL, this column displays the name of the group quarters or transitory location, if known.

title: Item (15), Apt/Unit. No.
content: The Apt. No. is the unit designation for living quarters at multi- unit locations, such as an apartment building. Unit designations may be Apt. A, Unit 6, First floor right front Apt. and so forth. This item will usually be blank for GQs.

title: Item (16) ZIP Code
content: Displays the ZIP Code where the address is located.

title: Item (17) FS Use Only
content: This item is for FS use only. Do not make any entries in this item.

title: The Footer Information
content: The codes listed on the footer do not apply for GQ Enumeration. The footer of the SC-920 contains information to help the HU enumerators use the listing page during canvassing work.

title: SC-921, Add Page
The Form SC-921, Add Page Columns
content: The Form SC-921, Add Page consists of a header and a body that is divided into 15 items. In these items you will fill the address and contact information from the group quarters assigned to you.

title: The Header Information
content:
The first line at the top of each page informs you that the Form SC-921, Add Page, contains the confidentiality statement including Title 13 and PII information, both of which are protected by the Privacy Act of 1974.
The following information is entered in the heading of the form:
- SCID (Special Census ID): The 5-digit number identifying your SCO
- AA (Assignment Area): The 6-digit number identifying the AA
The body of the form contains 15 items, each briefly described below:

title: Item (1), Line No.
content:
A sequential number, following the last line number printed on the Form SC-920, Address List Page.
This is the line number for the added address. This Add Page may contain more than one group quarters. The SCO will highlight the number of the group quarters assigned to you.

title: Item (2), Case ID
content: This item does not apply to GQ, but only completed for HU addresses. The Case ID is copied from the unlabeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, used for the address.

title: Item (3), Block No.
content: The number of the block where the address is located.

title: Item (4) Date Listed
content: The numeric date (month/day) the group quarters is entered on the Add Page**.**

title: Item (5) SC-Q Completed
content: This item does not apply to GQ, but only completed for HU addresses. You will leave this item blank.

title: Item (6), Address Status
content: Indicates the living quarters status of the address -- HU, GQ, or TL.

title: Item (7), Address No.
content: The number assigned to the structure. If not known, a physical description and/or location information must be entered in Item (9).

title: Item (8), Street or Road Name
content: The name of the street or road associated with the structure. If not known, a physical description and/or location information must be entered in Item (9).

title: Item (9), Physical Location Description
content: Completed when an address number or street name for the group quarters is not known.

title: Item (10) Apt/Unit No.
content: If the address is in a multi-unit structure, such as an apartment building, the apartment or unit number identifying the unit. If the number is not known, a description uniquely identifying the unit's location in the structure, for example, *front left*, *2nd floor right*, or *3rd floor middle*.

title: Item (11), ZIP Code
content: The ZIP Code associated with the group quarters.

title: Item (12) GQ or TL Name/ Facility Name
content: The name of the group quarters facility or location.

title: Item (13) GQ or TL Contact Name
content: The name of a contact person at the group quarters facility.

title: Item (14) GQ or TL Telephone Number
content: The telephone number of the contact person provided in Item (13).

title: Item (15) FS Use Only
content: This Item is for FS use only.

title: SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control Record
content: The SCO clerk prints the SC-116, *Group Quarters Control Record* for the case assigned to them*.* The *Special Census Group Quarters Control Record* consists of four parts: a Header, Section A, Section B, and Section C.

title: Header Section
Section A -- the Group Quarters Facility Contact Information
content:
![Image showing Section A of the SC-116, Group Quarters Control Record. No data has been entered in this form.](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.5in" height="1.5930555555555554in"}
The fields in Section A of the *GQ Control Record* may be preprinted. Otherwise, the clerk will complete them during the interview. **Section A** Items 1-3 correspond to Questions 1 and 2 on the Advance Contact Script. The SCO clerk confirms, updates, or collects information about the GQ contact. The clerk lists the GQ contact's name, title, and phone number. The clerk updates any of the contact information. If there is new or different contact person now in charge, the clerk adds that information on the *Control Record.*

title: Section B --Group Quarters Information
content:
![Image showing Section B of the SC-116, Group Quarters Control Record. No data has been entered into this form.](/images/imports/1/image3_1abacb97.png){width="6.489583333333333in" height="2.1666666666666665in"}
The SCO clerk needs to be thorough when completing this section. The FRs use this information to locate the GQ and conduct enumeration. Items 4-27 of the *Control Record* corresponds to Questions 3-17 on the SC-351, GQ AC Script. Items 4-27 are as follows:
- Item 4. Group Quarters Name -- This is asking for the Group Quarters name. The GQ contact will either verify the GQ name or the clerk will need to make updates to this information.
- Item 5. Street Name (Minor Change) -- The clerk can only make minor spelling changes to the street name. An example of this would be the GQ street name is 100 Main Street, but Main is spelled Mane. **A minor change is defined as making an address change where the GQ remains in the same block.** If there are any other changes to the address information, this case will be considered a potential GQ add. If possible, the clerk should ask about what is now at the original address and conduct an interview with a contact at the original address. If the clerk cannot do this, the case goes to the field for a GQAC interview.
- Item 6. Facility Name -- The clerk enters the name of the facility
- Item 7. Potential Duplicate -- The clerk will indicate whether it is a duplicate or not and provide the Duplicate Survivor ID in Item 27.
- Item 8. Is the GQ Type Code Correct -- When calling a facility, the GQ Type Code may be already included in the SC-325, Group Quarters Assignment Directory. The clerk will ask the GQ facility contact to verify that the facility type is correct. The SCO clerks will need to be familiar with the SC-637, *GQ Type Code Job Aid Special Census.*
- Item 9. Max Pop -- Is the maximum population of people that the GQ can accommodate. The clerk will record the max population information. This information will be used to determine how many questionnaires will be needed to enumerate this GQ.
- Item 10. GQ Operating on Special Census Date -- The clerk will record a Yes/No/Don't Know response for this item.
![Image showing the continuation of Section B (questions 11 - 20) of the SC-116, Group Quarters Control Record. No data has been entered into this form.](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="6.5in" height="3.9791666666666665in"}
- Item 11. Expected Pop -- The maximum population and the expected population can be different because the GQ may not always be at capacity. The clerk will record the Expected population which is based on the number of people who lived or stayed at the GQ on Special Census Day.
- Item 12. Males/Females/Both -- This information would have been taken into consideration when making assignments. A GQ for males only would not be assigned to a female FR or vice versa. This could be disruptive and may cause problems during the enumeration.
- Item 13. Records with requested information -- The clerk will mark a Yes/No response. This is trying to ascertain if the GQ will provide an Administrative Record. An administrative record helps the clerk to prepare the right number of forms for the FRs to conduct enumeration.
- Item 14. Type of Records -- The clerk will mark one of the options available. The options are Paper/Computer/Both.
- Item 15. Records available to Census worker - The clerk will record a Yes/No response for this item.
- Item 16. Enumeration Methods -- The clerk provides the enumeration method options and asks the GQ contact person for the enumeration method best suited for the GQ. The options are Administrative Records/ In Person Interview/ Drop Off/Pick Up.
- Item 17. Approximate number at the TNSOLS -- is specific for Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Locations. The clerk asks this question only if these locations are in their area. If no contact information is provided, a team of supervisors will visit the TNSOLs to gather this information.
- Item 18. Other Languages -- The clerk will ascertain if there are other languages at the GQ. This alerts the FRs to the potential need for interpreters. If Yes to other language, then list the other languages in the space provided.
- Item 19. Specific Instructions -- Some GQs may have specific instructions for the FRs to follow when conducting enumeration. These instructions will vary. These instructions are to be placed in the notes section of the Control Record.
- Item 20. Enumeration Appointment -- The clerk asks the GQ contact person for a day and time for the FR to visit the facility. The clerk writes the date and time for the enumeration appointment.
![Image showing questions 21a through 27 of the SC-116, Group Quarters Control Record. No data has been entered into this form.](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="6.5in" height="3.71875in"}
- Item 21a. Shelter Opening time -- This item is related to only shelters. The clerk will confirm with the GQ contact the opening times (when the Shelter is open for operation) and work with the GQ contact to select an ideal enumeration time.
- Item 21b. Shelter Closing time -- This item is related to only shelters. The clerk will confirm with the GQ contact the closing times (when the Shelter is closes for operation). This is important to know so the FRs will have an idea of when they will finish.
- Item 22. Client arrival time -- This item is to determine when the doors are open and when clients start to show up at the GQ.
- Item 23. Latest time client can enter shelter -- This item determines the latest time clients can enter the GQ.
- Item 24. Procedures when client enters -- This item provides an idea of what to expect when FRs arrive at the GQ.
- Item 25a. Enumeration contact same as facility contact - This item is to verify that the name of the person to contact as well as their title and phone number is the same as facility contact.
- Item 25b. Staff helping with enumeration - This item is to determine if a staff member from the facility with help with the enumeration.
- Item 26. GQ responsible for additional GQs -- The clerk will ask the GQ contact for additional GQs that the contact is responsible for during the enumeration period. The clerk will record a Yes/No response for this item.
- Item 27. Status code for the GQAC interview -- After conducting the GQAC, the clerk or FR will select one code best describing the outcome.
The clerk should note that there are no corresponding questions on the Calling Script for some Items, specifically the Status Code Items \-- Item 27 on the SC-116, *GQ Control Record*. In this case, the clerk will need to enter the status code for Item 27 on the SC-116, *GQ Control Record* after the call with the GQ contact has ended. If the case has any other status code except for complete, the clerk will hand the case to the SCO Manager/Field Supervisor for review, before entering the outcome in MOJO. The SCO clerk can make notes about the case in the Notes section of the form.
**Section C** -- **Enumeration Information**
Section C is completed by the FR and the SCO Manager or FS after the enumeration.
![Image showing Section C of the SC-116, Group Quarters Control Record. No data has been entered into this form.](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="6.5in" height="1.6270833333333334in"}

title: SC-351, Special Census Group Quarters Advance Contact Script
content:
The SC-351, *Special Census* *Group Quarters Advance Contact Script*, is a conversational document used by the clerks to schedule enumeration appointments. The SC-351, *Special Census* *Group Quarters Advance Contact Script* is written in bold and italicized text \-- the text serve different purposes. The **bold black text** is read to the GQ contact by the SCO clerk during the interview, and the *blue italicized* text are instructions guiding the clerk through the interview. The SC-351*, Special Census* *Group Quarters Advance Contact Script* contains a total of 19 questions, with several skip patterns. To become familiar with the questions and skip patterns, the SCO clerk should read each question repeatedly and carefully before conducting any appointment calls. The clerk should also look at the preprinted information on the Control Record to learn a little bit about the GQ before they call. The questions on the *Advance Contact Script* correspond to the questions on the SC-116 *Group Quarters Control Record*.
When the clerk makes the phone call, the first task is to be sure they are speaking with the correct person before they start the interview. The following pages will illustrate how to use the script to update group quarters records and document the enumeration method the facility contact selects. The instructions on the script tell you how to complete an interview.
In summary, at the beginning of the call, the clerk introduces himself/herself and reads the confidentiality statement. The confidentiality statement is important because it explains the purpose of the SC and how the data collected will be used. The SCO clerk will confirm, the GQ information including the GQ contact name, number, business email, and the address of the existing GQ with the GQ contact. The clerk will also obtain a location description if possible. If the GQ contact confirms that the information is correct, the SCO clerk will continue with the interview to set an enumeration appointment and obtain other information that will be used to prepare the assignment.
The SCO clerk must also be prepared if the GQ Contact has changed or if the address is not correct, for example the GQ has moved. If the GQ called by the clerk is no longer at the address listed, the clerk tries to find out what is currently at the listed address. In cases where the GQ address has changed, or a new facility is at the listed address, the clerk asks the GQ contact for the new address and documents the information on an SC-225 INFO COMM. The information is then passed to the Managers/Field supervisor to resolve. The manager reviews the case to determine whether the GQ is inside the SC Area or not and if the case is already listed in the workload. The manager also determines if the case requires field verification to confirm the GQ location.
If the case is inside the SC Area and is not already included in the workload, the case will be added to the workload. The SCO will delete the old GQ case as Cannot Locate and the new case will be added as a new GQ with the new address. This case will be worked in the same manner as any other GQ. If the case was confirmed to be outside of the SC Area, the SCO will delete the original GQ from the workload as Cannot Locate and the new case will not require any further processing.

title: Group Quarters Advance Contact
content:
The SCO clerks need to understand that GQAC is critical to the success of the GQ enumeration. SCO clerks make GQAC calls to all GQ facilities using the SC-351, *Special Census* *Group Quarters Advance Contact Script* and the SC-116, *Group Quarters Control Record*. The responses given during the interview are written on the *Group Quarters Control Record.* The workload for GQAC is on the SC-920, Address List Page and the SC-921, Add Page. If a GQ is on either of these forms, the page with a GQ is copied and becomes part of the GQAC assignment materials.
There are a few items the clerk needs to be aware of as they make the calls and update the Control Record.

title: Facility Name vs Group Quarters Name
content:
On the *Control Record,* there is pre-filled information from the Census Bureau address file. You ask the GQ contact to verify information about the location, including the GQ Name and Facility name.
For example, you may have a *Control Record* for the local hospital so the Facility Name could be Community Hospital and the GQ Name could be Psychiatric Unit. Another example is for a college. The Facility Name is State University and GQ Name Dorm One. Some types of facilities can have several GQs under their management. This helps us know which GQs belong together and are likely the responsibility of the same GQ Contact Person.
In many cases, these two items can be the same. For example, a group home is likely that its GQ and Facility Name are the same. Facility Name is not a required field. Do not feel you have to fill in this item if it the same as the GQ Name.

title: Updating GQ Names or Collecting a New GQ Name
content:
When updating a GQ, be sure to enter the specific GQ name. Use the proper name for the GQ. Entering a generic GQ name will not truly identify the GQ and could make it difficult to determine if one GQ is a duplicate of another. To avoid this, look at the following list of examples of GQ names that should NOT BE used to complete the GQ name field.

title: Enumeration Methods
content:
In the script, there is guidance on how to present the different enumeration methods to the contact person. There may be times when the GQ contact person continues to ask you for help on which enumeration method they should use. If you have already read all the details provided in the script and looked at the FAQs, here is some additional information you can use:
- In-Person Interview
- Field Representatives use paper Individual Census Questionnaires to conduct the interview.
- Very time consuming. This method is best for locations with a small number of residents or when you can have multiple enumerators to help conduct interviews at the same time.
- Not ideal for GQs whose residents have varied schedules like college students, who may have issues with answering questions or be alarmed by a stranger approaching them.
- Administrative Records
- The GQ contact agrees to provide the FR with a printed administrative list.
- The printed spreadsheet should include all the requested demographic information as specified by the Census Bureau.
- Census needs to ensure facility [will only provide]{.underline} demographic and usual home elsewhere data and to exclude Social Security Numbers and other PII.
- The printed administrative list must be legible and the print large enough to be read easily. Columns clearly separated and labeled. If handwritten, print the info
- The FR completes an Individual Census Questionnaire for each person on the list either on site or off, depending on if the enumerator can take the list with them.
- No contact with the residents/clients at the GQ.
- Minimal time required of the GQ facility contact.
- Drop off/Pick up of Questionnaires
- FRs will drop off ICQ packets for each resident in the GQ and schedule a time to pick them up.
- Requires some help from the facility such as providing a list of current resident/clients and possible passing out and collecting forms.
- Will use ICQs and ICQ Envelopes.

title: GQ Type Codes
content:
Before calling any GQs, it is very important that you know a few things about certain GQ Type Codes. Much of this is also in the In-Field script so you do not have to memorize this.
Most of the interviews you conduct will gather details about the residents that live or stay at a GQs. However, in some cases you need to gather information about the staff at a GQ.

title: GQ Type Code 501, 502, 701, 801, 802, 901, 902 and 903
content:
Staff who live or stay at a GQs with a GQ Type Code of [501, 502, 701. 801, 802, 901, 902]{.underline} and [903]{.underline} are counted with their residents during GQE. If you call a GQs with one of these Type Codes, ask the GQ contact person if they have any staff that live at the GQ. If so, inform the GQ contact person that the questions you are asking apply to the residents and staff who are living or staying there.
For any Non-SBE GQ, the reference date for enumeration and any population numbers is the Special Census Day. For the SBE GQs, their Special Census Day and reference date for any population numbers is the date of their enumeration appointment.

title: GQ Type Code 901
content:
A GQ Type Code of [901]{.underline} is for Workers Group Living Quarters and Job Corps Centers. This GQ type also includes staff living quarters at certain GQs (101-106, 201-203, 301, 401-405) who are counted separately from residents during enumeration.
For example, if you have two GQs -- one is for GQ Type Code 203 --and the other is 901, both with the same address of the Juvenile Dentation Center, when you speak with the GQ contact person, you have to be clear that you need the information about the staff that are living or staying at that facility on a permanent basis as of the Special Census Day as well as the detainees. You write the staff GQ data on the Control Record with GQ Type Code 901. The information for the other GQ -- the detainees - is entered on the other Control Record with GQ Type Code 203.
If, however, the GQ is a Job Corps Center, vocational training facility, or Workers Group Living Quarters you will ask about residents and staff. They are counted all together in the one GQ with Type Code 901.
*For example*:
\(1\) If you visit a GQ Type Code 901 facility that is a Jobs Corps Center, or migratory farm worker living quarters, you include both residents and staff who are living there as of the Special Census Day.
\(2\) If you visit a GQ Type Code 901 facility that is part of or associated with a correctional facility --include ONLY the staff who are living there as of the Special Census Day. This GQ should not include any of the inmates housed at the facility. The building where inmates live is a separate GQ with a different GQ Type Code.

title: GQ Type Code 999
content:
You may have a GQ Type Code of 999 (unknown) in your workload. In this case, during Question 4 of the script you should tell the GQ Contact Person that their GQ type is unknown. Use the SC-637*, GQ Type Code Job Aid* to classify their location.
Work closely with the GQ contact to find the best GQ Type Code to describe their facility. If you cannot update the GQ Type Code from 999 because you cannot speak with a knowledgeable person who can identify what is at the address, try to continue the interview. Collect as much information as you can. You should not add a GQ with Type Code 999 or change an existing GQ Type Code to a 999.

title: GQ Type Code 703
content:
There is one type of GQs that you **do not** visit/interview and that is a Domestic Violence Shelter (DVS). If you find during your interview that the GQ it is a DVS:
- Apologize to the contact person and end the call.
- Write in the Notes section of the Control Record or use an *INFO-COMM* that says, For SCO Contact Designee only.
- Do not use the term DVS, do not identify what kind of GQ this is.
- Do not discuss this location with anyone else.
- Place all the materials related to the DVS into a messenger envelop and write on the envelope, ***To be Opened by SCO Contact Designee only***.
- Give this to your supervisor.

title: Housing Unit
content: Some of the GQs in your assignment may now be HU. You thank the contact person, end the interview, and mark the Housing Unit status code on the Control record and end the call. Inform the SCO Supervisor of the need to conduct a HU interview.

title: Out of Enumeration Area
