title: Status Codes
content:
Status codes tell what action you took for a particular address. Each address is assigned a status code so we know which cases need to go to in Field GQAC, those that can move on to enumeration, and those that should not continue to be part of the SC. When you begin your interview, some of these codes will apply right away and you will mark it on the control record. Others are chosen after you have completed some of the questions with the contact record. During the phone interview, you can select the following status codes:
- Complete
- Housing Unit
- Transitory Location
- Out of Enumeration Area
- Nonresidential
- Cannot Locate
- Demolished/Burned Out
- Duplicate Survivor ID \#
- Refusal
- Military or Maritime Vessel
- Closed on Special Census Day
- Uninhabitable (Open to the Elements Condemned/Under Construction)
- Dangerous Address
- Unresolved (Cannot reach by phone)
If the status code is anything other than Complete, tell your supervisor. They need to review those cases and confirm if the status code is correct. Your completed work will be reviewed so be sure any additional notes you made about the address must be clear and thorough on the control record and/or INFO-COMM. The definitions for each status code are below.
**Complete -** An interview was completed for a GQ. This means that an enumeration method and appointment date and time have been set.
**Housing Unit -** A house, an apartment, a mobile home, a group of rooms or a single room that is occupied (or if vacant, is intended for occupancy) as separate quarters.
**Transitory Location -** A TL is a location where people are unlikely to live year-round due to the transitory/temporary/impermanent nature of the location. TLs include places such as campgrounds, recreational vehicle (RV) parks, marinas, hotels, motels, racetracks, circuses, or carnivals. Generally, people living or staying at a TL either pay fees to stay there, or they work there temporarily.
**Out of Enumeration Area -** the address is not within the boundaries of the SC area.
**Nonresidential -** Any locations where people do not live or stay, such as a formal office building, a bank, car dealership, etc.
**Duplicate Survivor ID \#** **--** the GQ is already in the workload and only one should be kept in the workload. The GQ you decide to use is the survivor GQ. You mark the duplicate box then write the ID of the survivor. There is space provided on the Control record to write in the survivor ID. Also write an explanation in the Notes section to explain that the record is a duplicate. Be sure to include the GQ Control Number of the remaining Enumeration Record in your note.
**Refusal -** The GQ Contact Person refused to participate in Census activities or complete the interview as well as when you are not allowed onto the GQ property.
**Military or Maritime Vessel --** no interview is conducted, and you report the case to the appropriate supervisor.
**Unresolved** -- during the phone interview there may be cases that could not be reached by phone. The case goes to the field interview for verification. During the in-field interview, this status code would only apply if none of the other codes can identify the situation at the address. Detailed notes about an unresolved case must be written on an INFO-COMM.
***Note:** Some GQs will include multiple GQ Types, but the address may be the same.*
**Closed on Special Census Day --** the GQ was not open on the Special Census Day, so it is not enumerated.
The status codes that can be selected after the In Field interview include those listed above plus these:
**Cannot Locate -** Location could not be found by the field employee.
Based on the outcome of the GQAC interview, you mark the appropriate status code in Item 27.
**Demolished/Burned Out --** for GQs which are already demolished, or to be demolished if there is reinforcing evidence, such as a sign, notice, or mark on the structure or in the block, indicating that the structure is to be demolished but on which demolition has not yet been started. Also, for structures that have been torn down or burned out.
**Uninhabitable (open to the elements/Condemned/Under Construction) --** the structure is exposed to the elements, that is, if the roof, walls, windows, or doors no longer protect the interior from the elements. There is reinforcing evidence, such as a sign, notice, or mark on the structure or in the block, that the unit, has been condemned but not yet demolished (see Demolished/Burned Out), the structure is falling, in disrepair or is still being built but no one is living there yet.
**Dangerous Address -** There is reason to believe that hurt, harm, or injury may occur at the location, or the location is currently deemed dangerous.

title: GQ Without a Scheduled Enumeration Appointment or No Longer Exist
content:
There might be instances where the GQ might no longer be in operation, does not exist or there is no scheduled enumeration appointment. This occurs if the SCO does not have a good telephone number for the facility or the telephone contact attempts were not successful. In some cases, the GQ contact that answered the clerk's questions might say that the facility might not be in operation or is no longer in operation. The clerk will write a note on the *Group Quarters Control Record* to indicate this GQ needs to be checked in the field. In these cases, the clerk will prepare an assignment with the *Control Record* for field verification. The FR will do one of two options:
- Complete the partially completed SC-116, *GQ Control Record* and take it back to the SCO, where the clerk prepares an assignment with the required number of enumeration documents needed for GQ enumeration, or
- Verify the facility is still operating as a GQ. In some cases, the GQs might no longer be in operation, is no longer a GQ, might not exist on the ground, etc. In these cases, the clerk will be instructed that the GQ needs to be deleted from the workload.

title: Address Changes Guidelines for Existing GQs
content:
When there is an address change for **existing GQs** (those listed on the SC-325) additional steps are required. The clerk writes the new address written on the INFO COMM, then checks if the new address is:
- Already in the workload and if not,
- Still located within the same block as the original address and if not,
- Still within the SC enumeration area.
Details about adds are in the next topic.

title: Processing of GQAC materials
content:
The GQAC phone call can result in a completed case. The updated Control Records are used during enumeration.
If the GQAC phone call does not result in a completed case for any of the reasons explained above, it must go to the In-Field GQAC for resolution. The FR will need the Control Record, possibly a copy of the associated Address List page or Add page, and INFO-COMM, if applicable. Using the same script, the FR will go to the address as shown on the Control record and attempt to complete the GQAC interview. When the FR finishes with the case, the Control Record and any other materials for the case are returned to the SCO.
The SCO staff will review the Control Record to check that the FR has marked a status code and if not, are there notes to explain why.

title: Group Quarters Adds and GQ Type Code Job Aid
content:
There will be times when a potential GQ is found and must be checked before adding it to the workload. This can happen during the GQAC interviews and in field operations.
If a newly discovered GQ is found, take the following steps:
- Complete an SC-225, INFO-COMM with all the information about the potential add. If done in the field, give the INFO-COMM to your supervisor.
- SCO receives INFO-COMM from field of a not listed GQ
- SCO verifies against SC-325 GQ Assignment Directory that this GQ isn't listed somewhere else
- After verifying that this new GQ doesn't exist in another location, it will be added to the workload in MOJO using the instruction in the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO
- After the new GQ is added, print the SC-116 and follow same process to conduct advance contact and enumeration
**Form SC-637(GQ), GQ Type Code Identiﬁcation Job Aid Special Census**
While FRs are performing their duties for GQAC In-Field operations, they may have to do other procedures in addition to completing the scripts. It is very likely that a contact person may tell them about other GQs that they do not have in their workload. This will require completing an SC-225, INFO-COMM with all the information about the potential add. Some interviews may require that they change to a different script because the GQ Type Code has changed from what is printed on the corresponding SC-116, Group Quarters Contact Record and now requires a different script.
When the GQ Type Code printed on the SC-116, Group Quarters Contact Record is no longer correct for the facility they are visiting, the Special Census GQAC Script tells them to use the *GQ Type Code Job Aid* to determine what the correct Type Code should be.
The *GQ Type Code Job Aid* leads them through all the appropriate questions to help determine the correct GQ Type Code for the facility. Follow the skip pattern based on the answers the GQ contact gives them. After the GQ Type Code is identified, they will go back to the in-field script to finish the interview.

title: Preparing and Distributing Enumeration Assignments
content:
**Introduction**
The SCO clerk performs Assignment Preparation by putting together all the documents needed during the GQE operation. The steps for Assignment Preparation are to be followed as laid out in this manual to ensure an efficient process during enumeration. The manager will instruct the SCO staff to store GQ packets in a designated space in the SCO.

title: Preparing Group Quarters Assignment Materials
content:
Once the GQAC calls and in-field visits are completed, the clerk begins assignment prep. The clerk will prepare the assignment using the materials listed above. The clerk will put all the enumeration forms in a messenger/large envelop. This will help the FRs to stay organized during enumeration. The clerk gives the FRs enough forms to complete their assignment. The number of ICQs needed for each GQ is dependent on the max number of persons at the GQ plus 10%. The clerk is responsible for preparing the assignment will write the GQ name and SCID number for each GQ in the upper right corner of the envelope.
For larger GQs there may be more than one messenger envelope for a GQ. The clerk will write the GQ name and the SCID on all envelopes. Each envelope will also be numbered
Page [1]{.underline} of [3]{.underline}
Page [2]{.underline} of [3]{.underline}
Page [3]{.underline} of [3]{.underline}
The clerk will assemble the GQ assignment. Every assignment will contain GQ forms for **only** **one** GQ assignment. The clerk will prepare the assignment that will include all forms needed for enumeration. The clerk will perform the following steps to prepare the assignment:
- Locate the SC-325 with the list of GQs to be enumerated. This helps with organization and efficiency when creating assignments. The clerk will mark off each case on the SC-325 as the materials are being put together.
- Check item 9 in the Control Record for the max number of people the facility serves to determine the number of Individual Census questionnaires (ICQs) to prepare.
- To determine the number of ICQs to include in the packet, multiply the number of persons in item 9 by 10 percent. For example, if a facility can accommodate 50 persons, multiply 50 by .10 and you get 5 forms. Therefore 5 additional blank forms are to be included in the assignment.
- Add pens, pencils, or any other supplies needed to conduct the operation. Refer to the table above.
- When the address register arrives in the SCO and before it is checked out for work, it is advisable to make a copy of the SC-920, *Address Listing Pages* where the GQ is listed (for existing GQs) or make a copy of the SC-921(GQ), *Group Quarters Add Page* where the GQ is listed (for added GQs). If there is more than one GQ listed on the listing page, the clerk will use a highlighter to indicate the GQ that corresponds to the assignment.
- When the map pouch (that accompanies the address register) arrives in the SCO and before it is checked out for work, it is advisable to make a copy of the AA Locator Map, AA Map, and Block Map where the GQ is located and insert the maps in the GQ envelope.
- For Service Based and/or Targeted Non-Sheltered Outdoor Location Enumeration cases, the clerk will also include flashlights and reflective vests to the assignment package.
- Once the packets are assembled, the clerk will check the total packets created and the number of GQs to ensure that the number of packets is equal to the number of GQs. Additionally, the clerk will conduct a quality check to ensure that the correct packet is prepared for the right GQ. The clerk checks:
- There is a stack of materials for each case on the SC-325.
- There is an SC-116 GQ Control Record for each case on the SC-325.The correct number of ICQs and ICQ Envelopes are with each GQ Control Record.
- The cases are stacked by appointment.
- SBE cases have the correct number of documents and the associated items such as a flashlight and reflective vests.
When all GQ assignments are prepared, the clerk will check-out the assignment to a FS or other designated staff responsible for the assignment. The clerk will check out items using MOJO.
Assembling of each GQ packet is very similar except for those for the military. After completing all GQ packets, they should be grouped by installation. The clerk must exercise great care in keep in the materials for the respective installation together as this reduces the number of contact the SCO will need to make with the installation. Furthermore, the SCO Supervisor must be able to give the installation all the enumeration materials needed at once. The clerk will print the maximum number of documents required plus the additional 10% needed.
The clerk will:
- Locate the SC-325 with the list of military GQs to be enumerated.
- Gather the number of SC-Q-GEs, based on the maximum pop of each facility.
- Prepare all SC-Q-GEs and ICQ envelopes for the Control Record for each Military GQ
- Also include extra Confidentiality notices.
Additionally, the clerk should conduct a quality check for materials and grouped by installation.

title: Supervisor Role
content:
The FS will distribute assignments to his or her staff to conduct the operation. Be sure each FRs has the supplies they need to conduct the enumeration. The SCO supervisor must check to ensure that all materials are prepared for the FRs to complete their assigned tasks. These materials will include:
- Form SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control Record
- Form SC-116 (CP), Special Census Group Quarters Control Record Continuation Page
- Form, SC-Q-GE, Individual Census Questionnaires (there should be enough ICQs for the max pop, and an additional 10%)
- SC-CN-(E/S), Confidentiality Notice
If an item is missing from the assignment, the FS will contact the SCO. The FS will make assignments ahead of time to minimize delays in performing enumeration. The FR will enumerate only one GQ at a time. The FS will determine regularly scheduled times to meet with the FRs to discuss cases, their progress and provide materials as needed. The FS will keep track of the FRs and ensure that they are completing their assignment. If FRs are struggling to complete their assignments, they will have their workload reduced and cases reassigned. The SCO should be mindful not to overextend FRs who are productive as this could lead to falsification of assignment. For each GQ assigned an FR, give that FR the appropriate assignment package. Be sure that you complete Section C items 28 and 29 on each Control Record as you give them to the FR. Make sure you give the right package to the right FR. Hold the packages for any GQs that are not initially assigned until later.
For GQs that fall into the GQs without a scheduled enumeration appointment or GQs that might no longer be in operation or does not exist category, the supervisor will hold these GQ assignments until in field operation is completed, then the cases are assigned to respective FRs. Additionally, if a GQ contact chooses Drop-off/Pick-up as the enumeration method, the date for enumeration should be noted on the SC-116, *GQ Control Record*.

title: Enumeration
content: There are three different procedures used to enumerate GQs. A GQ's residents/clients can be enumerated by in-person interviews. The other procedures are a FR can drop off enumeration materials with the GQ and pick them up later or use administrative records where the GQ provides a paper listing with the census response data the FR uses to complete ICQs for each person at the GQ.

title: Procedures for In-Personal Interview
content:
Be sure that the GQ contact person has given the FR permission to go room-to-room, etc.
For In-Person interviews, the FR will not leave ICQ packets. The FR will go to each resident's room/bed/unit to conduct a personal interview with the prepared ICQ packets as follows:
- Knock on the resident's door.
- Introduce themself to the resident and explain that they are there to take the census.
- Show the resident their Census ID badge.
- Hand the resident the SC-CN (E/S), *Confidentiality Notice* to read and keep.
- Explain that they need to conduct an interview by asking a few questions to fill out the census questionnaire. Tell them that it will take approximately ten (10) minutes.
- Conduct the interview. Read each question and the response options exactly as written.
- Go to Item B in the For Official Use Only section on the back of the ICQ. Mark (X) Respondent for Item B.
- Make sure you have written the PN in Item A in the For Official Use Only section on the back of the ICQ. The PN number comes from the SC-116(CP) GQ continuation page.
- Put the completed form in the ICQ Envelope.
- Mark this case as checked in on the *Control Record Continuation Page* in Column (5).
- Take the envelope and its ICQ with them.

title: Procedures for Drop Off/Pick Up
content:
Ultimately, the FR is responsible for the distribution of ICQs to the residents of the GQ. If the GQ contact person wants to hand out the forms instead of the FR doing it, make sure the contact person is provided clear instructions how to do this. The FR must swear in any staff at the GQ who helps with the enumeration.
- If the FR hands the ICQ Packet to the resident, do the following:
- Emphasize the importance of filling out the form completely and legibly.
- Tell each resident to seal his or her completed form in the envelope provided.
- Point out the date/time on the envelope for when the FR (or the GQ Contact Person) will return to pick up the completed ICQ in the sealed ICQ envelope.
- If the GQ contact person or other staff member distributes ICQs, do the following:
- Give the packets to the GQ contact person to distribute to the residents.
- Explain to the GQ contact person that they must deliver each packet to the resident whose name/room number is written in the FOR section on the envelope.
- Explain to the GQ contact person that they must tell the residents to seal their census questionnaires in the envelopes provided when they finish completing the forms.
- Tell the GQ contact person that they **[must not]{.underline}** look at the completed census questionnaires or open the returned envelopes.
- Tell the GQ contact person that you will return to pick up the completed ICQ on the date and time you wrote on the ICQ envelopes. Work with the GQ contact person to select a date that is soon after the materials have been dropped off (3-5 days). Make sure the FR writes this date and time on the GQ Control Record, in the Notes section.
- Remind the GQ contact person not to photocopy the ICQ. Each ICQ has a unique barcode/identifier, which is vital to correctly process the completed forms.
- Before leaving the GQ, the FR should call their supervisor to notify them that they have dropped off the prefilled enumeration materials.

title: Procedures for Administrative Records
content:
The FR can use administrative records where the GQ provides a paper listing with the census response data the FR uses to complete ICQs for each person at the GQ.
If using administrative records, then do the following:
- Secure a quiet place to work.
- Using the listing supplied by the contact person, fill out the ICQ for each person who is living at the GQ on Special Census Day.
- Put a check mark in column (5) of the SC-116 (CP) as you finish a form. The check mark goes on the line corresponding to that person's name and PN.
- On the ICQ, copy the PN for the individual from the SC-116(CP) to PN box in the **For Official Use Only** section.
- Go to Item B in the For Official Use Only section on the back of the ICQ. Mark (X) Group Quarters Administrator for Item B.

title: Review and Check in Materials
content: The review and check-in process takes place post enumeration. The materials are first reviewed in the field before they are returned to the office by the Supervisor/Lead FR. Then the clerk conducts an office review **before** they check in any materials into the system.

title: Review Completed Materials in the field
content:
If SCO has assigned a supervisor/ Lead FR for the enumeration tasks, then the FR turns in the completed materials to the supervisor/ Lead FR. If there are any problems, the supervisor will address it with the FRs. The Supervisor/ Lead FR use the *SC-1055(GQE), Census Field Supervisor Checklist,* to review completed enumeration materials. The supervisor/ Lead FR will confirm that the following items are completed:
- The SC-116, *GQ Control Record* has been completed for the correct GQ.
- The enumeration date is correctly filled out.
- The FR's name and signature is completed.
- The SC-116 (CP), Group Quarters Continuation Page (GQ Listing Sheet).
- This is a listing of the rooms or bed locations and names of those enumerated at a specific GQ. Each resident's room or bed number and name will be listed in the appropriate columns. In rare cases, a name will not be available, but the room or bed number should be completed. The Supervisor or Lead FR will check that the information in the header of the form is complete and correct for the appropriate Control Record. The Lead FR's name is listed in the *Field Representative* space in the footer if the enumeration was a team effort. Column **(1)** is the Room/Bed Number; Column **(2)** Person Name; Column **(3)** Participant Number; Column **(4)** Check in Mark (X) if received; Column **(5)** is marked as Complete or Incomplete on each line to indicate that the ICQ for each respondent was complete or incomplete. If any ICQs are blank, the GQ population is zero or incomplete then the notes section of the Control Record, or an INFO-COMM should be filled out.
- The number of ICQs recorded match the number of ICQs received. If the number of ICQs recorded do not match the number received, the Supervisor/ Lead FR should have the FR check if they have misplaced an ICQ in their cars or if an extra one is in their bags or stuck to any turned in materials. If the ICQs have the correct Bar Code ID Number, then update the SC-116, *Special Census GQ Control Record* with the correct total. The Supervisor/Lead FRs may need to also review the *Control Record Continuation page* to ensure that the ICQ corresponds to the number on the SC-116, *GQ Control Record*. Moreover, they need to ensure that the ICQs turned in are not photocopied, but if there are photocopied ICQs, then the information should be transcribed onto a blank ICQ.
- All ICQs should be filled out. The Supervisor/Lead FR will confer with the FR if a note is not provided regarding incomplete ICQs.
- If there is a zero population, mark the appropriate status code based on the notes from the FR. If the FR did not provide a note regarding the zero population, then the Supervisor or Lead FR will contact the FR and enter the status codes. Status codes indicate why there may be a zero population or why no ICQs were turned in for a GQ.
- If the location is a HU or TL, make sure this is recorded in the notes section of the SC-116, *GQ Control Record* and a completed SC-225, INFO-COMM. If it is a HU, we mark it as HU in GQ AC and it doesn't go to GQ enumeration. We then alert the FS/FR to go there and add it as an HU and conduct the enumeration. GQ FRs should only focus on dealing with GQs; however, they can complete an INFO-COMM for any new housing developments or group quarters that they are made aware of. The INFO-COMM should include the type of living quarter that they wrote up as a potential add - Group Quarters/Service-Based Location, HU, or TLs.
- After the Supervisor/Lead FR has confirmed that all the enumeration materials are completed and accurate, the Supervisor/Lead FR will bring the completed materials and hand them to the clerk for office review and check in.

title: Review Completed Materials in the SCO
content:
After each case is returned to the office, the clerks must complete a quality check. This quality check includes counting the ICQs to be sure that it is equivalent to the Special Census Day population. The case will then be checked in. Any discrepancies between the total ICQ count and the Census Day population should be reported to the Manager/Field Supervisor.
The Enumeration items on the Control Record are 28 to 36, which covers Assignment, Certification, Supervisory Use Only and Reinterview (RI). The Assignment Area shows the Name of the FR who has been assigned the case, the date the case was assigned, the date enumeration was completed, and the Total population.
- Item 28. Assigned to (Print FR's Name) -- The manager assigning the case printed the FRs name in this section.
- Item 29. Date Assigned -- The date the case was assigned to the FR.
- Item 30. Date Enumeration Completed -- The date that the FR conducted enumeration.
- Item 31. Total ICQs -- The total ICQs should be equivalent to the Total population at the GQ.
- Item 32. FR Signature & Item 33. -- The FR will also need to sign and date the form certification statement.
- Item 34. Supervisory Use Only -- Based on the information received from both the clerk and the FR the SCO Manger/FS will mark one option in the For Supervisory Use Only section.

title: Review and Check-in by the Clerk
content:
The clerk will use the Form SC-1056*,* *Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist* to do their review of the completed materials. The clerk reviews and documents on the checklist any errors/problems found. The checklist has an instruction section and a Task List, which consists of six (6) Items. Each clerk uses only one Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist per completed case. During the office review, the clerk reviews the *GQ Control Record* and the ICQs completed for the GQ before checking in the work. The clerk should take extra care to review any additional documents or attached Continuation Pages that belongs to the GQ. All this review is done **BEFORE** you check in completed materials to make sure you have everything ready for check in MOJO. Refer to the SC-445 to check in GQ materials from the field into MOJO.
To begin the review process, the clerk needs the following items:
- Completed SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control Record
- Completed SC-Q-GE (E/S) *Individual* *Census* *Questionnaires* (ICQs) that belongs to each Control Record
- Completed SC-116 (CP), Group Quarters Continuation Pages, if applicable
- Associated completed SC-225, *INFO-COMMs*
- Blank copies of the SC-1056, Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist
- Pencil -- use to complete the checklist
The clerk may receive unused materials such as extra ICQs or Continuation pages. Return blank ICQs or Continuation Page to bulk supply.
When completing the SC-1056, *Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist* complete the following information in the top righthand corner of the Office Review Checklist:
1. Date Prepared: Write in the date you are doing the review.
11. Name of Office Clerk: Write in your name.
12. Name of FR: Copy the name of the FR (or the Supervisor/Lead FR in some cases) from the Control Record.
13. Name of GQs: Copy the name of the GQ from the Control Record.
14. Case ID: Copy the Case ID from the Control Record.
15. State: Copy the State from the Control Record.
16. Block: Copy the Block from the Control Record.
17. County: Copy the County from the Control Record.
The clerk conducts the review of the Control Record following the directions on *the SC-1056,* *Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist* by marking off each task in the right-hand column. If a task is not completed or there is a problem, mark the Error(s) column. Notify the supervisor of the problem and work to fix it. If the mistake can be fixed, then the clerk will initial in the last column on the right-hand side. The clerk will make notes in the Notes Section of the form to bring about clarity concerning the case review.
If the clerk cannot fix the problem, then the case is given to the supervisor after finishing the review. The clerk will then tally the total errors marked and the total corrections made in the appropriate spaces. Give the checklist with the case materials to the supervisor; if the clerk discerns that they need help with resolving errors the case should also be given to the supervisor.

title: Review of the SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control Record and SC-Q-GE, Individual Census Questionnaires
content:
The clerk will complete a review of the Control Record to make sure it is accurate and complete. This review is done independently without the associated GQ documents. Associated GQ documents should be set aside briefly and reattached to the respective Control Record once the review is done. To complete a review of the Control Record, the clerk will check to ensure that there are no errors. If errors are found, then:
- Mark the appropriate boxes in the Error(s) column.
- Enter the total errors in the space provided at the bottom of the Error(s) column.
- Provide any notes in the Notes section on the back of the checklist about the error and what was already done to fix the problem.
- If necessary, give the materials to the supervisor for resolution.
After the successful independent review of the Control record, the clerk will then conduct a thorough review of the Control Record, and its associated ICQs. The review of the Control Records and ICQs are done together to ensure that the materials are for the correct GQ and that the forms are properly completed. The clerk uses the SC-1056, *Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist* Task List to complete the review.
There are six (6) items on the Task List on the SC-1056, *Group Quarters Quality Control Office Review Checklist*. Each item helps the clerk to determine thoroughness of the work completed during enumeration and the appropriate actions to be taken to rectify any discrepancies before checking in. The six items are expounded on below:

title: Item 1: All ICQs are original, not photocopies
content: The clerk checks all ICQs ensuring they are the original, not a photocopy. If there are photocopies or info copies, the clerk transcribes the data from those to new ICQs. This includes the PN and Bar Code ID Label on the back of the ICQ. The clerk talks to the supervisor first, so the supervisor knows what is being done to get this case through review. All photocopied ICQs will be destroyed.

title: Item 2: All ICQs have the GQ Case ID written on the back of the form
content:
The clerk checks to see that the GQ Case ID (found on the SC-116) is transcribed in the GQ Case ID Box on the back of the ICQ. The clerk then checks:
- Is this person and the associated Participant Number (PN) on the GQ Continuation Sheet for the GQ?
- Is the PN is unique to this case's materials?
The clerk then checks the Continuation Page, once they are sure the ICQ belongs to the Control Record.

title: Item 3: The number of ICQs received for this GQ matches the Total Pop number written on the Control Record.
content:
The clerk will count the ICQs and ensure that they have all the ICQs for the associated Control Record. If there is a difference, check the Notes section on the Control Record for an explanation. If there is written explanation for the discrepancy, then proceed with check in.
If there is no explanation, continue with the following steps:
**If there are more ICQs than what is on the Control Record:**
- Check that all the ICQs belong to that Control Record. The FR may have accidentally included ICQs from another GQ, or the Facility Manager might have duplicated or photocopied ICQs.
- Verify the case ID on the Control Record matches the case ID on the back of the ICQs. If they all match, make a note of this on the Notes section located on the back of the Office Review checklist to show the correct total.
- Let the supervisor know about this so they can follow up with the Supervisor/Lead FR. Be sure to document the answer they provide in the Notes section on the checklist.
**If the number of ICQs is less than what is on the Control Record:**
- Then check the other assignment materials turned in by the same FR. The ICQs may be mixed in with another case. If you do not find the missing ICQs, make a note on the Control Record that the Initial Count was short.
- If the missing forms cannot be found in the office, you or your supervisor will contact the Lead FR or the Supervisor
- Continue to review and process this case. Any additional forms for the case can be checked in later.
- Once you have an answer, immediately document that on the Notes section located on the back of the Office Review Checklist.

title: Item 4: The Date Enumeration Completed box is filled in (Section C, Item 30 on the SC-116).
content: If this box is not filled in on the Control Record, contact the Supervisor/Lead FR to collect this information.

title: Item 5: If the number of ICQs is 0 (zero) or this GQ has incomplete ICQs, then there is documentation in the Notes section of the Control Record or an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM.
content: If the GQ has 0 ICQs or incomplete ICQs, there should be notes to explain the 0 ICQs or incomplete ICQs. If there are no notes on the Control Record or an accompanying INFO-COMM, ask the Supervisor/Lead FR to provide the missing information. The clerk will also check the Continuation Page to determine if it list any incomplete ICQs.

title: Item 6: If the number of ICQs is 0 (zero) then there is a box marked in the *For Supervisory Use Only* section.
content: If the number of ICQs is 0 (zero), then there is a box marked in the *For Supervisory Use Only* section of the Control Record. If no box is marked but there is documentation about this on the Control Record or an accompanying INFO-COMM, ask your supervisor to review and provide guidance as to the appropriate box to mark. **The clerk is not allowed to decide on their own in this instance.**

title: Corrected and Error Free Control Records
content:
When the errors are corrected, the individual who makes the correction enters their initials in the appropriate box on the Office Review Checklist. They will also enter the Total Number of Corrections Marked. When all the errors are corrected (Total Number of Errors Marked equals Total Number of Corrections Marked), the case is ready for check in.
If the materials do not have any errors, then on the Office Review Checklist:
- Check the boxes in the Free from errors column.
- Enter 0 in the space provided for Total Number of Errors.
- Proceed to check in the case.

title: Reinterview
content:
**Overview of Group Quarters Reinterview Process**
Reinterview RI is an important part of the quality control procedures during SC. During SC all completed cases are eligible for RI with a few exceptions listed below. RI procedures involves checking the completed work for veracity. RI involves checking all turned in materials and calling the GQ contact to confirm that the FR conducted enumeration on the date and time specified on the GQ Control Record.
Cases Eligible and Ineligible for Reinterview
Some of the cases received from the field will qualify for RI while others will not. A case is eligible for RI when the case is:
- Completed through an in-person interview.
- A drop-off/pick up of questionnaire.
- Enumerated using Administrative Records.
- Completed by multiple FRs. (These cases will still have a lead FR.)
- Conducted by any user role.
Cases are not eligible for RI when the case:
- Has a GQ Type Code corresponds to a Maritime (900), Military (106, 404, 601, 602) or SBE (701, 702, 704, 706) or the Type Code is unknown (999).
- Does not contain at least one ICQ.
- Was previously selected for RI.
- Was assigned for Rework.
- Is a domestic violence shelter (703).
**Conducting Reinterview**
Before conducting RI, the clerk will check and sort through all the turned in field materials including the SC-116, Special Census *Group Quarters Control Record* and the SC-116(CP), *Special Census Group Quarters Control Record Continuation Page.*
The procedure for conducting RI is one where the clerk will call the GQ contact to obtain the information for RI. During each phone call, the clerk should ensure that they are speaking with the GQ contact who was present on the day of enumeration. If this is not possible, the clerk will inform the Manager. During RI, the clerk will use Items 35 and 36 on the SC-116, *Special* *Census* *Group Quarters Control Record* to complete RI. The questions are as follows:
- **Item 35**. Our records show our Census Field Representative visited your facility on \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (transcribe date from item 20 above) to count your residents/clients. Is that correct?
- **Item 36**. What is the approximate number of residents/clients you think were counted as a result of that visit? This number might be different than the maximum number of persons you could have at your facility.
When applicable, the clerk will check the appropriate response or write the appropriate response from the GQ contact for each question. The completed forms are turned into the Manager, who will then assign an outcome to the case.
**Status Assigned to RI cases**
The SCO Supervisor will review each RI case and assign it an outcome code before it is checked in by the clerk. The SCO Manager/Field Supervisor or designee will complete Items 35 and 36. See the For Supervisor Use Only -- RI Result Section on the SC-116. There are four outcomes for cases assigned during RI, they are:
- **Pass** -- The results of reinterview RI and the original FRs agree.
- **Soft Fail** -- The results of RI indicate honest FRs error or a reasonable explanation. For example, the FR accidentally went to the wrong HU to complete a questionnaire.
- **Hard Fail -** Discussed the case with the FR and the FR does NOT receive a reasonable explanation. The SCS or FM determines the FR intentionally falsified or deviated from procedures. After further research the FR has a pattern of not following procedures after feedback was provided to correct the patterns; or was found falsifying some or all the data in the questionnaire.
- **Noninterview** - Neither the clerk nor the Manager could contact the GQ for interview.
If the cases pass RI, or the clerk was unable to contact the GQ contact then the case is given back to the clerk to be checked in and prepped for shipment, because the case is now done with the quality control process. If the case does not pass RI, then there are additional steps that the manager must take. If the case receives a fail, then it may need a minor correction or needs to be reworked. The Manager will make the decision about the cases that need to be reworked.

title: Transitory Locations Advance Contact (TLAC) and Enumeration at Transitory Locations (ETL)
content:
## Transitory Locations Advance Contact (TLAC) and Enumeration at Transitory Locations (ETL) Operations Overview
## Special Census ETL Operation
The purpose of the Special Census ETL operation is to enumerate (count) people who live or stay at census-defined transitory locations (TLs) on the Special Census date who do not have another place where they live or stay most of the time (no Usual Home Elsewhere (UHE)).
The Special Census enumerates people in seven defined types of transitory locations with in-person interviews using a paper questionnaire. Transitory locations include:
- Campgrounds (TL Type Code 10)
- Recreational Vehicle (RV) Parks (TL Type Code 20)
- Marinas (TL Type Code 30)
- Hotels/Motels (TL Type Code 40)
- Racetracks (TL Type Code 50)
- Circuses/Carnivals/Fairs (TL Type Code 60)
- Other (TL Type Code 90)
The Special Census ETL operation consists of two phases:
- Transitory Locations Advance Contact (TLAC)
- Enumeration at Transitory Locations (ETL)

title: What is TLAC?
content:
The Special Census TLAC is an in-office and field-based operation conducted by the office clerks, Field Supervisor (FS) or Lead Field Representative (FR) before the ETL operation. The office clerks conduct in-office phone interviews to gather information about the transitory locations. They identify a contact person to verify the address and other information and schedule the best date and time for field representatives to conduct the count of residents during the Enumeration at Transitory Locations Operation (ETL). FS or Lead FR conduct the in-field interviews and uses the Form SC-688 (TLAC), TLAC In-Field Script to complete the TLAC section of the Form SC-117, Transitory Locations Control Record (TLCR).
The purpose of the TLAC operation is to:
- Conduct phone interviews to verify or identify a respondent at each transitory location to serve as a contact person and collect or update if it's a new contact person, the person's name, title, and telephone number(s).
- Conduct a phone interview to verify or obtain information about the TL such as the TL name and address, TL Type Code, Maximum Units, Estimated Occupied Units, among other data.
- Prepare for the TLAC in-field interviews completed by the FS or Lead FR if the TLAC in-office interviews were not successful.
- Set an enumeration appointment to enumerate (count) the TL residents during the ETL operation (see below).
- Gain cooperation from the contact person by providing the Form SC-CN (E/S), *Confidentiality Notice* and Form SC-LFM-TL (E/S), *Transitory Locations Facility Manager Letter* and ask that the contact person advise their residents of the upcoming ETL operation.
- Use the information completed in Section A, *Transitory Locations Advance Contact* of the Form SC-117, *Transitory Location Control Record (TLCR)*, to prepare for the ETL.
There are two phases of the TLAC operation. The first is an in-office component which the clerks will attempt to conduct the TLAC interviews by phone. The second is an in-field component. TL cases that could not be contacted by phone will be sent to the field with a FS or Lead FR for an in-person interview.
What is the Enumeration at Transitory Locations (ETL) operation?
- The Special Census Enumeration at Transitory Locations (ETL) operation is conducted in-field *after* the TLAC to interview the *residents* of transitory locations who have no Usual Home Elsewhere (UHE) and who live at the location on Special Census Day.
- Either the FS or Lead FR conducts ETL fieldwork with a team of FRs on a scheduled date and time, to list each living quarter (Transitory Unit, TU, and mobile home/permanent structure) in the transitory location and interview residents of all occupied living quarters, using a Form SC-693.2, *Transitory Location Listing Sheet* and Form SC-Q-TL, *Transitory Location Questionnaire (EQ)*.

title: Transitory Locations (TLs) Defined
content:
## What are TLs?
TLs are defined by the Census Bureau as places where people are *unlikely* to live year-round due to the transitory, temporary, or impermanent nature of the locations. These types of locations include campgrounds, Recreational Vehicle (RV) parks, marinas, hotels/motels, racetracks, carnivals, fairs, and circuses.
Due to economic and social changes in society, people have become more mobile and living space has shrunk. Some people no longer maintain a traditional residence, such as a house, apartment, condominium, or mobile home, etc., but instead have chosen alternative types of housing, which could be in a boat in a marina, a hotel or motel room, a tent at a campground, or a RV at an RV park.
*Generally, people living or staying at a transitory location either pay fees to stay there, or they work there temporarily.* A transitory location is, therefore, a business that may provide some type of space (site, space, unit, slip, etc.) for erecting, parking, or mooring a portable living quarter and/or offer other amenities in exchange for some form of payment.
We usually think of a transitory location as a place where people do not stay very long. The usual types of residents we expect to find in a TL are staying only temporarily, a few days, or maybe a week or two; they may be away from home on business for a period of travel and/or leisure. The assumption is that although these people are in-transit between one destination or another, they will eventually return to their permanent or UHE.
The Special Census ETL:
- Counts (interviews) **ONLY** those individuals who live or stay on an extended, long-term, or permanent basis in a census-defined transitory location, not the people who are passing through. In other words, for inhabitants of a TL, the TL is their recognized place of residence; they have no UHE. *Include owners, managers and other employees who usually live or stay in the transitory location and have no UHE.*
- Does **NOT** count (interview) people in transitory locations who have a UHE; in other words, people who do not usually live and sleep at the transitory location will not be interviewed. The premise is that since these people have a UHE, they will return to the place where they usually live and be counted there.
- Does **NOT** count people who live or stay at two or more residences (during the week, month, or year), such as people who travel seasonally between residences (for example, snowbirds) -- Counted at a residence where they live and sleep most of the time. If they cannot determine a place where they live most of the time, they are counted where they are staying on Census Day.
- Does **NOT** count (interview) people in transitory locations, such as a hotel, motel, hostel, or YMCA, **if** the residents do not live or stay there on a long-term basis. Hotels without long-term guests are considered **Non-Residential**.
- Do **NOT** count (interview) people in transitory locations, such as a hotel, motel, hostel, or YMCA, when it is used **100%** to house people who are experiencing homelessness.
- In such a case, the hotel is not a transitory location but a *group quarter*. This population is counted in the Group Quarters Enumeration (GQE) operation called Service-Based Enumeration (SBE).
- However, if there is ONE or more persons living or staying in the hotel with the residents who are experiencing homelessness, the hotel is a transitory location.
- Does **NOT** count (interview) people who are experiencing homelessness and living in what appear to be *transitory-type locations*, such as city parks, sidewalks, under bridges, parking lots, or wooded areas behind local stores in makeshift shelters or in vehicle encampments. This population is counted in the Service-Based Enumeration (SBE) operation.

title: Transitory Units (TUs*)*
content:
In transitory locations, the dwelling that the resident occupies is called a Transitory Unit; or a *portable/mobile housing unit*, because, *in most cases,* it can be moved from place to place.
- TUs are not permanent structures, which are fixed in place (anchored to the ground), and unable to be moved around. Although, technically, any housing unit can be moved, the point is that most TUs are intended to be mobile. Note that this definition does not apply to hotels, which are structures with living quarters, such as rooms or suites (TUs).
- For purposes of TL enumeration, examples of a portable housing unit or TU would be:
- A Recreational Vehicle (RV) parked in a space in an RV park or campground.
- A tent erected on a site in a campground.
- A slip where a yacht, houseboat, floating house, Floating on Water Residence (FOWR), or house barge is or can be moored.
- A single room or suite in a hotel, motel, hostel, lodge, resort, inn, bed-and-breakfast, **if** **that room is occupied by persons living or staying on an extended or long-term bas****is.**

title: A TL consists of Sites, Slips, Pads, Spaces, Rooms, or Units
content:
A TL will contain designated spaces where TUs (see above) can be erected, set up, parked, moored, or located. A TL may also contain semi-permanent or permanent structures such as mobile homes or cabins where people can live or stay.
For Special Census purposes, list and enumerate *only* those permanent structures in a transitory location that are *used or intended to be used as a living quarter,* such as a standard house, cabin, cottage, bungalow, or mobile home. Do NOT list any non-residential or commercial type structures, such as storage sheds, drydock facilities, garages, etc., with no living quarters.

title: Special Census Office (SCO) Staff Duties
content:
## SCO Managers
SCO managers, who include the Special Census Supervisor (SCS), Field Manager (FM), and Field Supervisor (FS) are responsible for supervising the work conducted in the office and the enumeration activities in the field. They coordinate and monitor the work of the staff who prepare the materials for TLAC and ETL operations.

title: Field Manager (FM)
content:
- Leads and directs the activities of the SCO staff.
- Supervises the research of any potentially new TLs, provided by the Governmental Unit or FRs using all possible sources (local knowledge, internet search applications, and other references, as required).
- Approves the addition of new TLs to the SCO workload and ensure its accurate entry into MOJO.
- Collaborates with the FS to select TLAC/ETL field staff.
- Oversees the training of all TLAC/ETL staff, including in-office and field.
- Supervises the preparation of all TLAC and ETL in-field materials.
- Supervises the review, check-in, and proper disposition of all Special Census TLAC/ETL materials.
- Responds to and resolves all TLAC and ETL in-office/field related operational issues, including Dangerous Addresses, Refusals, possibly new TL locations,
- Monitors the timely completion of all TLAC and ETL office and field work.
- Assists in the selection of a Lead FR to conduct the TLAC and lead a team of ETL FRs.
- May also conduct TLAC for transitory locations on U.S. military installations.

title: Field Supervisor (FS)
content:
- Trains the TLAC/ETL field staff.
- Makes assignments to TLAC and ETL FRs.
- Oversees the timely completion of TLAC and ETL Field activities.
- Meets frequently with the FM to discuss the progress of field activities.
- Meets frequently with the Lead FR and team of FRs.
- Reviews completed work of TLAC/ETL FRs.
- Ensures that all completed TLAC/ETL work materials are returned to the SCO for review and check-in.
- Approves Form BC-27, Time, Attendance, and Cost Report and Form BC-27A, Field Employee's Reimbursement Expenses, submitted by field staff.

title: Lead Field Representative (Lead FR)
content:
A Lead FR will be appointed to conduct the TLAC in-field visit and lead a team of FRs for the ETL operation. They will also:
- Perform other duties as assigned by the FS, such as assisting in the training of FRs; they will also collect, review, and return completed enumeration materials to the SCO.
- Conduct the in-field interviews at all assigned transitory locations, review their work, and submit completed enumeration materials to the Lead FR/FS for approval.
- Submit the Form BC-27, Time, Attendance, and Cost Report and Form BC-27A, Field Employee's Reimbursement Expenses, to the FS for approval.
- Review the Form SC-693.2(ETL) TL Listing Sheet for completeness and correctness.

title: Field Representative (FR)
content:
- Conducts the in-field interviews at all assigned transitory locations, review their work, and submit completed enumeration materials to the Lead FR/FS for approval.
- Submits the Form BC-27, Time, Attendance, and Cost Report and Form BC-27A, Field Employee's Reimbursement Expenses, to the FS for approval.
- Reviews the Form SC-693.2(ETL) TL Listing Sheet for completeness and correctness.

title: TLAC Clerk
content:
The TLAC Clerk will:
- Conduct phone interviews for TLAC.
- Key information into MOJO and document updates.
- Prepare assignments for TLAC in-field operation. Perform all assignment preparation tasks for the TLAC operation, including the printing of the Form SC-117, *Transitory Location Control Record* (TLCR) from MOJO, and checking out assignments to the field.
- Protect all Title 13 and PII. Store all PII materials in a secure area in the SCO until receipt of disposition instructions.
- Review all returned Forms SC-117, TLCR to ensure completeness and correctness and to determine which cases will be assigned to the ETL operation.
- Advise the supervisor of any TLAC field related issues notated on the Forms SC-117, TLCR and SC-225, INFO-COMM.
- Identify and add new TLs to MOJO. Assist in the research of possibly new TL adds, or GQ conversions and make the appropriate entries in MOJO.
- Key the Form BC-27, Time, Attendance, and Cost Report and Form BC-27A, Field Employee's Reimbursement Expenses, data into the GovTA system.
- Ship materials to the RO and/or the National Processing Center.

title: ETL Clerk
content:
The ETL Clerk will:
- Assemble and inventory ETL kits.
- Perform all assignment preparation tasks for the ETL operation.
- Advise the supervisor of any ETL field related issues notated on the Forms SC-117, TLCR and SC-225, INFO-COMM.
- Assist in the research of possibly new TL adds, or GQ conversions and make the appropriate entries in the SCOCS.
- Review completed ETL materials according to instructions in the Form SC-691(ETL), ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist.
- Store all PII materials in a secure area in the SCO until receipt of disposition instructions.
- Key the Form BC-27, Time, Attendance, and Cost Report and Form BC-27A, Field Employee's Reimbursement Expenses, data into the GovTA system.
- Ship materials to the RO or National Processing Center.

- Review the completed materials (see TLAC Assignment Check-in and Review).

- Prepare cases for the ETL operation.
Your SCO manager will advise you when TLAC field activities begin and when you must start preparation for the operation.

title: Form SC-117, TL Control Record (TLCR)
content: The Form SC-117 contains PII information and must be stored in a secure location.

title: Print and Staple Form SC-117
Assign the Case to the Lead FR
content:
In the **Header** section:
- Print the FR's name to whom the case is assigned in **Item P, Assigned to field** as provided.
- Enter the date assigned in MO (**01-12**), DAY (**01-31**), YEAR (**4-digit year**) format (MM/DD/YYYY) in **Item Q, Date assigned field**. This is the date that you complete the assembly of the kit, and it is available for pick up by the Lead FR.
- Leave **Item R, Date returned field** blank until the Form SC-117 is returned by the Lead FR after the in-field interview (see **Topic 5**, *TLAC Assignment Check-in and Review*).

title: List Additional Blocks in TL in Same AA
content: Sometimes a TL may consist of several blocks but only one block can be printed in **Item L, Block field** in the Header. This section allows you to list additional block numbers if necessary. Your supervisor will advise you when this occurs.

title: Assemble TLAC Kit Materials
content:
For each case, paperclip (do not use rubber bands) the following forms together:
- Form **SC-688**, TLAC In-Field Script (1)
- Form **SC-CN**, Confidentiality Notice (1)
- Form **SC-LFM-TL (E/S**), TL Facility Manager Letter (1)
- Form **SC-ID,** Language Identification Card (1)
- Form SC-945, ETL Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) (1)
- Form SC-946, TL Type Codes and Definitions Job Aid (1)
- Place the assembled forms in a messenger envelope.
- Paperclip the associated printed Form **SC-117**, *TL Control Record*, to the outside of the envelope.

title: Quality Control Assignment Materials
content:
Another TL clerk should double-check the assignment packages to make certain that all materials for each case are in the envelope.
- Place in a bin labeled **TLAC CHECKOUT**.
- Print the TL Assignment Directory Report (List of all TLs in the workload)
- The Field Manager will print a spreadsheet containing the list of all TL cases. You will use the spreadsheet to keep track of cases checked-out (assignment packages taken from the SCO by the Lead FR and checked-in (returned to the SCO by the Lead FR). The FS will notify the Lead FR when to pick up and return completed TLAC assignments.
- Enter the date in MO (**01-12**), DAY (**01-31**), YEAR (**4-digit year**) format (**MM/DD/YY**), the Lead FR left the SCO with the assignment package (this date may be different from the **DATE ASSIGNED** on the Form SC-117).
- Enter the Lead FR's name.
- Enter your initials to indicate you approved the release of the materials.
- Keeping a record of the chain-of-custody of these documents is vital to security of the Special Census data. If materials are not returned in the timeframe allotted, you or your supervisor must contact the Lead FR to find out the status.

title: TLAC Assignment Check-in and Review
content:
## TLAC Assignment Check In
The clerk will check in all materials returned from the TLAC in-field visit. Materials will be reviewed to determine which TL cases will be prepared for the ETL operation.

title: Prepare TLAC Review area
content:
Organize your work area so that you can sort and place reviewed materials in a recognizable and well-labeled space.
- Label a bin or other container, **ETL.** SC-117 cases that will be moved to the ETL operation will be placed in this bin.
- Label a bin or other container, **NO ETL.** SC-117 cases that will not proceed to the ETL will be placed in this bin.
Remember that the Forms SC-117 and SC-225 contain PII data and must be safeguarded. After reviewing, store the completed forms in the secure area designated by your SCO.

title: TLAC Assignment Receipt
content:
When a TLAC Lead FR finishes an assignment, they will return the following materials to the SCO:
- Form SC-117, Transitory Location Control Record
- Form SC-688, TLAC In-Field Script
- SC-225s, INFO-COMMS, completed and/or blank
- TL Site Maps
- Unused/extra Forms SC-CN (E/S), Confidentiality Notice
- Unused/extra Forms SC-LFM-TL (E/S), TL Facility Manager Letter

title: Check-in TLAC Assignment
content:
Using the printout of the TL workload (see TLAC Assignment Preparation and Checkout) for TLAC assignments:
- Go to **Item P, Assigned to field** to locate the Lead FR's name to whom you made the assignment for the TL.
- Go to **Item R, Date returned field** and enter the date in MO (**01-12**), DAY (**01-31**), YEAR (**4-digit year**) format **(MM/DD/YY),** the assignment was returned.

title: Collect Unused/Blank TLAC Forms
content:
Collect blank Form SC-225s, Form SC-688, unused/extra Forms SC-CN (E/S) and SC-LFM-TL and place them in the allocated storage area in the SCO.
- The Form SC-688, *TLAC In-Field Script,* can be reused if no stray markings or if in good condition.
- The Lead FR should not have made any entries to questions in the script in lieu of writing on the Form SC-117.
- If you have a Form SC-688 with answers circled **and** there is no Form SC-117 with **Sections A1** and **A2** completed:
- Contact the Lead FR. Since they visited the TL, they must be responsible for transcribing the information to the Form SC-117.
- Also refer the case to your supervisor. The Lead FR may need to be retrained on the TLAC in-field procedures.

title: Review and Edit TLAC Forms
content:
1. Sort the Forms SC-117 by **TL Name/Barcode ID**:
- Keep duplicate Forms SC-117 together.
- Keep any Forms SC-225, *INFO-COMMs* and TL site maps with the accompanying Form SC-117.
18. Write the date the Form SC-117 was returned in **Item R,** **DATE RETURNED** **field** of the Form SC-117 header section. Enter MO (**01-12**), DAY (**01-31**), YEAR (**4-digit year**) format.

title: Section A2: TLAC Status
content:
Check **Section A2**: *TLAC Status*, to determine the outcome of the TLAC in-field visit:
1. If COMPLETE (ETL Appointment Scheduled, including appointments for Housing Units) was marked (X), make certain Section A1, Item 12, contains the DATE and TIME (am or pm circled) scheduled for the ETL visit and that Item 13 is marked (X) YES. Note that if a housing unit is located at the address on the Form SC-117, the Lead FR must make an appointment for the ETL interview (see instructions in Item 3.b.iv, below).
19. If Item 12 is complete and Item 13 is marked (X) **YES,** **go to Item 4** of these instructions.
20. If no DATE and or TIME (am or pm circled) in Item 12, and Item 13 is marked (X) **YES**, contact the Lead FR to resolve the discrepancy and make the appropriate entries in Items 12 and/or 13. Based on the information the FR provides, you may have to change the TLAC status code.

title: Other TLAC Status Codes
content:
1. Out of Enumeration Area
A.  Check the **Notes** section for a reason why the case is out of the SCO enumeration area.
B.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM for additional information.
C.  Refer the case to your supervisor for additional research and confirmation of the status. If confirmed, the case will not move forward to the ETL.
D.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
21. Duplicate: Survivor ID#
A.  You should have already sorted the Forms SC-117 by TL Name/Barcode ID and would have identified any duplicate forms.
E.  Make certain the TL Barcode ID of the Survivor Form SC-117 is written in the field provided beside **Duplicate.**
F.  Review the Survivor SC-117 starting with Item 2.
G.  Place the duplicate Form SC-117 in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
22. Dangerous Address
A.  Check the Notes section for a reason why the case was identified as dangerous.
H.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
I.  Refer the case to your supervisor for additional research and confirmation of the status. If confirmed, the case will not move forward to the ETL.
J.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
23. Housing Unit, No Appointment
A.  The Lead FR may have determined that a housing unit is at the address on the Form SC-117 but was unable to conduct the TLAC in-field interview and/or make an appointment for the ETL (no one home, vacant, refusal).
K.  Check the **Notes** section for any explanations.
L.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
M.  This case will move forward to the ETL.
N.  Place in a bin labeled **ETL.**
24. Group Quarters
A.  The Lead FR may have determined that a group quarter is at the address on the Form SC-117.
O.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
P.  Refer the case to your supervisor for additional research and confirmation of the status. Group Quarters are handled during the Group Quarters Advance Contact (GQAC) and Group Quarters Enumeration (GQE) operation. The SCO will delete the GQ from the TL workload and add it into the GQ workload.
25. Closed on Special Census Day
Check Item 6, Will you be open between (Special Census Dates)? on the Form SC-117:
A.  If **NO** is marked, the TLAC Status is valid. Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
Q.  If **YES** or **DON'T KNOW** is marked, then Items 7-17 of the Form SC-117 should contain an entry. If not, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
R.  Refer the case to your supervisor for additional research and confirmation of the status, if necessary. If confirmed, the case will not move forward to the ETL.
S.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
26. Demolished/Burned Out
A.  Check the **Notes** section for an explanation.
T.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation. The case will not move forward to the ETL.
U.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
27. Uninhabitable (Open to the Elements/Condemned/Under Construction)
A.  Check the **Notes** section for an explanation.
V.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation. The case will not move forward to the ETL.
W.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
28. Closed/Not Operating/Vacant
A.  The Lead FR may have arrived at the address and determined that the transitory location is closed, not operating or vacant (devoid of inhabitants).
X.  Check the **Notes** section for an explanation.
Y.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
Z.  The TL may have been closed at the time of the TLAC visit but may be open during the Special Census ETL timeframe. The case will move forward to the ETL.
A.  Place in a bin labeled **ETL.**
29. Refusal
A.  The TL contact may have refused to cooperative with the TLAC in-field interview or may not have allowed the Lead FR to enter the premises of the TL.
B.  Check the **Notes** section for an explanation.
C.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
D.  Refer the case to your supervisor. They will attempt to convert the refusal and conduct a TLAC interview.
E.  Whether the case is converted or not, it will move forward to the ETL.
F.  Place in a bin labeled **ETL.**
30. Nonresidential
A.  The Lead FR may have determined that the structure/place at the address is Nonresidential (commercial establishment, such as a store, bank, car dealership or used for storage of equipment, machinery, or other goods).
G.  The case will not move forward to the ETL.
H.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL.**
31. Cannot Locate
A.  The Lead FR may have been unable to locate the address of the transitory location. This may happen more often if the TL is a Type Code 60, Circus/Carnival/Fair because the event moved to another location and the FR was unable to find it at the new location.
I.  Check the **Notes** section for an explanation.
J.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
K.  The case will not move forward to the ETL.
L.  Place in a bin labeled **NO ETL**.
32. Other
If **Other** is marked, make certain there is a written entry in the space provided for the category.
A.  Check the **Notes** section for an explanation.
B.  Check for an accompanying SC-225, INFO-COMM. If none, contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
C.  Depending upon the description/explanation provided, the case may or may not move forward to the ETL.
D.  Refer the case to your supervisor if you cannot make an accurate determination of the TLAC status.
E.  Place in the proper disposition bin based upon the review.
If the TLAC Status is **COMPLETE or Housing Unit (No Appointment Scheduled), Closed/Not Operating/Vacant, or Refusal** (and your supervisor determined that the Refusal case should move forward to the ETL):
A.  Check **Section A:** *Transitory Location Facility Contact Information*, Items 1, 2 and 3 to determine if there are corrections to any of these fields. Make the appropriate changes in MOJO.
M.  Review each Item in **Section A1,** *Transitory Location Advance Contact Information*:
**Item 4/5**, TL Name/Street Name:
- The Lead FR may have made corrections to the TL Name and/or Street Name, if necessary, on the lines provided.
- If the **TL name** is other than the one printed in the Header of the Form SC-117, refer the case to your supervisor for additional instructions. This may not the same location as the one in the workload. See **Topic 2**, *Adding Transitory Locations to the Workload*.
- If the street number, street name, and/or directional prefix is different from what is printed in the **Header** of the Form SC-117, refer the case to your supervisor for additional instructions. Only **MINOR** spelling corrections are allowed. This may not the same location as the one in the workload and could be a new TL. See **Topic 2**, *Adding Transitory Locations to the Workload*.
**Item 6**, Will you be open between (Special Census Dates)?
- If **YES** or **DON'T KNOW**, there should be an entry in Item 7.
- If **NO**, the FR should not have made any other entries in **Section A1** but should have marked *Closed on Special Census Day* in **Section A2:** *TLAC Status*, of the Form SC-117.
**Item 7**, TL Type Code:
- One of TL Type Codes 10-60 will be marked.
- If TL Type Code 40, Hotel/Motel is marked, **Rooms** should be marked in Item 8, **Type of spaces or units**.
- If TL Type Code 90, **Other,** is marked, there should be a description that might assist in determining which specific TL Type 10-60 could apply.
**Item 8**, Type of spaces or units:
- More than one type may be marked as the transitory location may be mixed use (e.g., TL Type Code 10, Campground and TL Type Code 20, RV Park).
- If TL Type Code Hotel/Motel is marked in Item 7, make sure **Rooms** is marked in Item 8. If not, mark (X) the box beside **Rooms**.
- If **Other,** is marked, there should be a description that might assist in determining which specific type of spaces or units could apply.
**Item 9**, Maximum Number of Spaces or Units at Location:
- Check to make certain there is a number entered on the line provided. You will use this number to estimate the number of Forms SC-Q-TL, *Transitory Location Questionnaires* (EQs), needed for the enumeration of the location.
- If no number, contact the Lead FR.
**Item 10**, Average Number of Occupied Units:
- Check to make certain there is a number entered on the line provided.
- If a housing unit, the Lead FR should have entered the number of people expected to occupy the unit on Special Census Day.
**Item 11**, Are there any people who live or stay at this hotel/motel on an extended basis?
- The Lead FR completed this Item only for TL Type Code 40, Hotel/Motel (Item 6 of the Form SC-117).
- If **YES** is marked, go to Item 12.
- If **NO** is marked, there should be no further entries in **Section A1** of the Form SC-117.
- Make certain that Nonresidential is marked in **Section A2,** *TLAC Status.*
**Item 12**, What is the best day and time to conduct the Special Census at this location?
- Check to make certain there is a date and time on the appropriate lines, if Item 11 was **YES** or if any of the previous Items 1 through 10 contain an entry.
- If there should be an entry and there is none, or it is incomplete (e.g., date but no time or a.m./p.m.), contact the Lead FR.
**Item 13**, Appointment Scheduled?
- Check to make certain Item 11 is marked **YES,** if Item 12 contains an entry.
- If Item 12 does not contain an entry, check to make certain Item 13 is marked **NO**.
**Item 14**, Are there any specific instructions that Special Census staff need to know to count the people at this location?
- Make certain that if **YES** is marked, one or more of the options (Gated Community, Locked Entrance, or Other: Describe) is marked).
- Otherwise, **NO** should be marked.
**Item 15**, Are there people at this location who do not speak or understand English?
- If **YES** is marked, make certain there is a language written in the lines provided for language(s) spoken. A FR who speaks the language or a translating service may be needed for the ETL visit.
- Otherwise, **NO** should be marked.
**Item 16**, TL site maps:
- If **YES** is marked, then make certain the maps are attached. If there are no maps, contact the Lead FR for clarification. Keep the TL site maps with the SC-117; the FS/Lead FR will distribute them to the ETL team members.
- Otherwise, **NO** should be marked and there will be no site maps.
**Item 17**, TL Contact responsible for additional location(s):
- If **YES** is marked, there should be information in the **Notes** section and/or a Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, regarding the possible additional locations. These locations may or may not be in the Special Census TL workload or could have been assigned to another Lead FR.
- Refer the SC-117 and SC-225 to your supervisor.
- The transitory locations will have to be researched to determine whether they are already in the workload, should be added to the workload for a TLAC visit, or are out of the SCO enumeration area.
- See **Transitory Location Adds, of this chapter.**

title: Ensure that all Forms SC-117 are Checked-in and Stored
content:
Make certain that you have accounted for all Forms SC-117 that have been checked-in and/or referred to your supervisor for further research. If your supervisor does not return a Form SC-117 to you for correct allocation (ETL or NO ETL), follow-up with them.
- Forms SC-117 and associated TL site maps that will be used during the ETL operation (**ETL** bin) should be stored in a secure location in the SCO. These forms will be used for ETL assignment preparation.
- Forms SC-117 that will not be used during the ETL operation (NO ETL bin), should be stored in a secure location in the SCO until final disposition instructions are received.

title: TLAC Add Cases
content:
## TLAC Transitory Location Adds
During the TLAC interview, Lead FRs may learn that:
- The assigned transitory location has undergone a name or an address change (Form SC-117, **Section A1**, *Transitory Location Advance Contact Information*, **Item 4,** *TL Name* and **Item 5**, *Street Name* fields are different from what is in the **Header** of the Form SC-117). They could have visited the incorrect location, or *it may be a new TL*.
- Notify your supervisor.
- You may be instructed to conduct research or to accept the correction and continue with checking-in the case.
- The TL contact person manages another TL (Form SC-117, **Section A1**, **Item 17** is marked **Yes**) but the Lead FR does not have another Form SC-117 for that location, therefore they could not conduct an in-field interview for that TL. They should have completed information in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117 and a Form SC-225, INFO-COMM about the potentially new TL.
- Notify your supervisor.
- You may be instructed to conduct research.

title: Conducting TL Research
content:
## TL Name/Address Changes
You need to determine if the Lead FR visited the right location.
- Search the TL workload to determine if that location is already in the workload. It may be in the workload under the corrected name/address, but a different TL Case ID.
- Use **Google Search** for the original address to determine what is at that location.
- Use **Google Search** for the TL name to determine what the address is (and to verify if it is within the SCO enumeration area).
- If you determine that the address is not in the workload, then you must add the location to the TL workload via MOJO.

title: Potentially New TLs
content:
If there is information in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117 and/or a Form SC-225 containing information about another TL that the TL contact person manages:
- Search the TL workload to determine if that location is already in the workload. It could be assigned to another Lead FR.
- If it is already in the workload, indicate on the Form SC-117/SC-225 that the TL is a duplicate of a case in the workload and will not be added.
- If you determine that the address is not in the workload, then you must add the location to the TL workload via MOJO.
    - Print the Form SC-117 for the new TL.
Your supervisor must assign a Lead FR to the case for a TLAC in-field interview. Follow instructions in *Topic 4, TLAC Assignment Preparation and Checkout,* for preparing the TLAC in-field assignment.

title: ETL Assignment Preparation and Check-out
content:
## Background
A Lead FR or FS will be assigned to lead a team of FRs to make personal visits to transitory locations to conduct the ETL interviews. Clerks will prepare kits for the Lead FRs/FRs containing ETL materials to conduct the interview. After the in-field visit, the Lead FR will return the completed materials to the SCO.
Your SCO manager will advise you when ETL field activities begin and when you must start preparation for the operation.

title: Retrieve the Forms SC-117, TL Control Records (TLCRs)
content:
After TLAC, the cases eligible for ETL were stored in a bin labeled **ETL**. There should be only one TLCR per transitory location. These include:
- Cases that were marked as **COMPLETE** in **Section A2**, *TLAC Status*, of the Form SC-117 (**Item 12** contains an appointment date and time, and Item **13** is marked (X) **YES** for Appointment Scheduled)
- Cases that were marked Housing Unit, No Appointment in Section A2, *TLAC Status,* of the Form SC-117.
- Cases that were marked Closed/Not Operating/Vacant in Section A2, *TLAC Status*, of the Form SC-117 because the FM/SCS verified that the TL was only temporarily closed or vacant due to repairs or some other reason and could or will be open on Special Census Day.
- Cases that were marked Refusal in Section A2, *TLAC Status*, of the Form SC-117 because the FM/FOS determined that an enumeration visit should be attempted on Special Census Day (the supervisor was able to convert the refusal).
Transcribe Maximum Number of Spaces or Units to Master List Report
For each TL Case ID on the Master List Report:
- Find the Form SC-117 with the matching TL Case ID/TL Name.
- Transcribe the number written in the space provided for Item 9, **Maximum Number of Spaces or Units at Location**, on the Form SC-117, to the line for the case on the Master List Report.

title: Assemble Field Representative Kits
content:
Work on ONE case at a time.
1. Locate the SC-117 for the case.
N.  Starting with the first case on the list, locate the corresponding Form SC-117.
O.  Attach the form SC-117 to the packet for the lead FR only. The Lead FR is responsible for making entries on this form after visiting the ETL. No additional copies should be provided to the ETL FR team.
33. Determine how many SC-Q-TLs are needed.
A.  Look at the number of **Maximum Number of Spaces or Units** from Item 9 on the SC-117 and:
Never photocopy any questionnaires. Each form has a unique case id.
P.  Count out enough Forms SC-Q-TL, *Transitory Units Questionnaire* (s)(EQs), to match the number on the Master List Report.
Q.  **Add 10% more** questionnaires (MAX NUMBER + 10%): If the Maximum number is 50, then 50 x .10 = 5. Therefore, include 55 questionnaires.
R.  Look at Item 15, Are there any people at this location who do not speak or understand English? on the Form SC-117.
S.  If **Yes** is marked, check to see if the language(s) spoken is **Spanish** (or similar Hispanic origin language). The Lead FR should have written the language spoken on the line provided.
T.  There may also be a notation in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117 indicating that Spanish is spoken. If so, but a specific number of Spanish speakers is not recorded, count out **five** Forms SC-Q-TL(S), *Transitory Units Questionnaire (Spanish)* (EQ).
34. Count out **10** Forms SC-CQ-TL, *Transitory Units Continuation Questionnaire(s)*(CQs) for **each case.**
