35. For each case, complete the **Identification** section of **five** (**5)** Forms D-693.2, *TL Listing Sheet(s)* or one for each Lead FR or FS assigned to the case.
The FR has blank TL Listing Sheets in their FR supply kit. If they need more than one sheet, they will copy the identification information to the additional sheet(s).
36. Copy the following information from the **Header** section of the Form SC-117 to the corresponding Items in the **Identification** section of the TL Listing Sheet as follows:
A.  Copy the five-digit Case ID from the box **A** on the SC-117 to box **a** on the SCID boxes on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="3.6037160979877516in" height="1.1769356955380577in"}
U.  Copy the name of the Governmental Unit (GU) from the box **B** on the SC-117 to the Name box on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="3.978669072615923in" height="1.1040288713910762in"}
V.  Copy the two-digit State Code from box G on the SC-117 to Box **b** on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="2.1143186789151356in" height="1.3644127296587927in"}
W.  Copy the three-digit County Code from box H on the SC-117 to box c on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="3.2600087489063867in" height="1.0936132983377078in"}
X.  Copy the six-digit Tract Code from box K on the SC-117 to box d on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="2.5309339457567805in" height="1.062367672790901in"}
Y.  Copy the six-digit AA number from box J on the SC-117 to box f on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image4_5a3fa4b0.jpeg){width="2.510102799650044in" height="1.2185979877515312in"}
Z.  Copy the TL Name from box C on the SC-117 to box **g** on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="5.207682633420823in" height="1.051952099737533in"}
A.  Copy the TL Name from box C on the SC-117 to box g on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="5.207682633420823in" height="1.1248589238845144in"}
B.  Copy the street address or location description of the TL from box D or N on the SC-117 to box g2 on the SC-693.2.
![](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="6.5in" height="1.1in"}

title: Prepare Assignments
content:
1. Clip together all the EQs/CQs/TL Listing Pages for each case; do NOT rubber band them together.
37. If a clip will not hold together what is needed for a single case, place them in a messenger envelope and clip the associated Form SC-117 to the outside of the envelope.
38. If more than one envelope is needed to hold a case, use as many as necessary.
39. Mark the envelopes **1 of 2**, **2 of 2**, etc., to alert the Lead FR that there are multiple envelopes of materials.
40. Write the TL Case ID/TL Name on any additional messenger envelopes.
41. If the case is very large, put the materials in a box and affix the associated Form SC-117 to the top so you know which TL the case is for.
42. Complete Section B: Enumeration at Transitory Locations Information on the Form SC-117.
43. Print the name of the FS/Lead FR to whom the case is assigned in the space provided for **ASSIGNED TO**.
44. Print the date (MM/DD/YY) the case was assigned in the **DATE ASSIGNED** fields.
45. Mark off (draw a line through or checkmark (√) each case) on the TL Assignment Directory Report as you finish packaging the materials.
46. When you finish one case, begin the next and repeat this process until you have finished preparing materials for every case on the TL Assignment Directory Report.
47. After you have finished, you should have accounted for every Form SC-117. Make certain you did not miss any case on the TL Assignment Directory Report.

title: Quality Control Check
content:
Have another clerk check the assignment materials. They must make sure that:
- There is a stack of materials for each case shown on the TL Assignment Directory Report.
- There is a Form SC-117, Transitory Location Control Record (TLCR) for each case on the TL Assignment Directory Report. The correct number of questionnaires is included.

title: ETL Assignment Review and Check-in
content:
## Introduction
ETL Assignment review is a three-stage process.
- After the FR completes the enumeration of their assigned area of a TL, they review their materials, using the Form SC-671, *ETL Field Representative Checklist*.
- The Lead FR/FS collects the completed enumeration materials and reviews them, using the Form SC-682.2(ETL), *ETL Field Supervisor Checklist*.
- The Lead FR/FS returns the completed TL enumeration assignments to the SCO, where the office clerk reviews them, going through the task list, using the Form SC-691(ETL), *ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist*.
- Complete one Form SC-691(ETL), *ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist*, for every Form SC-117, *TL Control Record*, returned with its associated enumeration materials. Review the materials for one Form SC-117, before checking-in the questionnaires.

title: ETL Materials Returned to SCO
content:
The Lead FR/FS will return the following materials to the SCO:
- Completed Form SC-117, *TL Control Record*
- Completed Forms SC-693.2(ETL), Transitory Location Listing Sheets
- Completed Forms SC-225, INFO-COMMs
- Completed Forms SC-Q-TL/SC-Q-TL (S), *Transitory Units Questionnaires* (EQs, English and Spanish version, if included)
- Completed Forms SC-CQ-TL/SC-CQ-TL (S), *Transitory Units Continuation Questionnaires* (CQs, English and Spanish version, if included)
- Unused/blank enumeration materials could also be turned in, such as, extra questionnaires, and TL Listing Sheets.
- Store blank questionnaires, unused TL Listing Sheets and Forms SC-LFM-TL(E/S)*, TL Facility Manager Letter(s),* in the bulk supply at the SCO.

title: Steps to Review ETL Enumeration Materials
content:
Begin your review by using a blank Form SC-691(ETL), *ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist,* and a pencil to complete the checklist, after completing the following three initial examinations:
- Review Form SC-117, TL Control Record
- Use the TL Assignment Directory Report which contains the list of TLs and the name of the Lead FR assigned to the case. Enter the date (MM/DD/YY) the materials were returned to the SCO beside the FR's name.
    - On the Form SC-117:
      - Make certain that a date (MM/DD/YY) was entered in the **Item 21**, **DATE ENUMERATION COMPLETED** fields.
      - Make certain that the FR certified the results of the ETL visit by signing their name and entering the **Date Signed** (MM/DD/YY) in **Item 22 and Item 23**, of the **Certification** section (**Section B**, *Enumeration at Transitory Locations Information*).
      - Check the **Notes** section for any pertinent information related to the enumeration of the TL that you might need to bring to your supervisor's attention.
- Review Forms SC-693.2(ETL), Transitory Location Listing Sheets
- Make certain that all TL Listing Sheets for each TL are in *block number order* (see **Block No** in upper left corner of each TL Listing Sheet).
- Make certain that all TL Listing Sheets for each TL are numbered **(Page\_\_of\_\_\_** in the **Identification** section), for example **page 1 of 10**, **page 2 of 10**...**page 10 of 10.**
- Review Forms SC-225, INFO-COMM
- Read associated Forms SC-225 to determine if they contain any pertinent information related to issues or problems affecting the enumeration of the TL.
- Refer all SC-225, INFO-COMM related to aggressive refusals, dangerous addresses, TLs requiring security clearances or payment/fees to access the site to your supervisor. *These cases require management attention and need to be addressed immediately!*
- Review EQs and CQs and Finish Reviewing the Form SC-117, using the Form SC-691(ETL), ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist
- Complete the **Header** section of the Form SC-691(ETL):
![Image showing the header section of the Form SC691(ETL). The form is blank and items 1 through 8 are visible. ](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="5.960313867016623in" height="1.9562051618547682in"}
1. Using the **Task List**, review the Form SC-117, *Transitory Location Control Record (TLCR)* and Forms SC-Q-TL (EQ) and SC-CQ-TL (CQ) for completeness, accuracy, and legibility.
48. For each of the **Tasks** (**1-6**), mark (X) the box as you complete each one.
49. Mark **YES** if the answer to the question is **YES.**
50. Mark **NO** if the answer to the question is **NO** because a correction is required.
51. Enter your initials in the appropriate column.
52. If necessary, enter any notes in the **Notes** section of the form.
53. If an error is discovered, and you cannot fix it, bring it to the attention of your supervisor.
![Image of the Task List portion of the Form SC-691(ETL) showing items 1 through 6 and columns A through F. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="5.81790791776028in" height="3.037619203849519in"}
**DO NOT:**
- Write on any of the EQs/CQs, mark through any of the boxes, or otherwise make any corrections on the form itself. Smudges, marks, or extraneous lines could interfere with the clarity of the digital scan.
- If you find an error, according to the **Task List** instructions, you may need to complete a new EQ/CQ. *Notify your supervisor.*
**DO:**
- Check-in the Form SC-117 and any other enumeration materials, when all errors are corrected.
- Store the Form SC-117 and associated EQs/CQs in a secure location until ready to be shipped once the operation is over.
- Follow the procedures in the office manual in the SC-1131 Special Census Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, if you find duplicates.
- Do not check-in a case, if you determine that the case requires supervisor or management attention (Refusal or Dangerous Address); instead, take all the materials to your supervisor.
- Store the materials that DO NOT require shipping in Block/County order in a secure location in the SCO.

title: How to Use the Task List
content:
## Task List No. 1 (Column (A))
- Mark (X) the box in Column (B) as you complete Task 1.
- Visually inspect each EQ and CQ for the TL to make certain each one is an original copy and not photocopied.
- If all are originals, then mark (X) **Yes** in Column (D) and enter your initials in Column (F).
- If any of the EQs or CQs are a photocopy, mark (X) **No** in Column (E) and *notify your supervisor*.
- Your supervisor will contact the FR about using photocopied census forms and may instruct you to transcribe the information onto a new EQ.
- Do NOT throw the photocopied EQ/CQ into the trash. They must be destroyed according to SCO instructions as they contain PII information.
- Write **DESTROY** on the front of the document.
- Place the discarded form in a bin labeled **HOLD FOR DESTRUCTION** and store in a secure location in the SCO.
- Enter your initials in Column (F).

title: Task List No. 2 (Column (A))
content:
- Mark (X) the box in Column (B) as you complete Task 2.
- Make sure you have all the questionnaires for the associated Forms SC-117.
- Count the number of EQs received for the TL and compare it to the written number in **Item G**, **Section B1: ETL Summary** of the Form SC-117.
- If the number matches, mark (X) **Yes** in Column (D) and enter your initials in Column (F).
- If the number doesn't match, mark (X) **No** in Column E, and look for an explanation in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117. If there is no explanation and:
- **If there are [more]{.underline} EQs** than what is indicated in **Item G,** **Section B1**: *ETL Summary*, of the Form SC-117:
- Make certain that you have only the EQs for the TL you are working on by comparing the geocoding data (**SCID, State, County, AA Number, TL Tract, TL Block codes**) on the EQ to that on the SC-117. If it belongs to another TL, place it with that group.
- **If there are [fewer]{.underline} EQs** than what is indicated in **Item G,** **Section B1**: *ETL Summary*, of the Form SC-117:
- Check the EQs for other TLs you are working on to make certain the missing EQ is not mixed in with another TL's materials.
- If you cannot find the missing EQs, write **Initial Count was Short** in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117.
- If the missing form cannot be found in the office, you or your supervisor must contact the FS.
- Continue to review and process this case. Any additional forms for the case can be checked in later. Do not hold the case back from check-in to wait on more forms.
- Enter your initials in Column (F).
- When you learn the answer, document the explanation in the **Notes** section on the SC-691(ETL) *ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist.*

title: Task List No. 3 (Column (A))
content:
- Mark (X) the box in Column (B) as you complete Task 3.
- Look at the Interview Summary section on the back of the EQ. If **Yes** is marked in Item C, compare the number entered in the boxes to the number of CQs that accompany the EQ. Make certain there is a CQ for each EQ that required the use of a CQ.
![Image showing question C the questionnaire that asks if there any continuation questionnaires for this address. ](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="5.173961067366579in" height="1.2192902449693788in"}
- If the numbers match, mark (X) **Yes** in Column (D), enter your initials in Column (F), and place the CQ back inside its corresponding EQ.
- If the numbers do not match, look at the *Questionnaire of Questionnaire(s)* section on the front of each CQ to determine if the FR counted correctly.
![Image showing the fields Questionnaire \_\_\_\_ of \_\_\_\_\_ questionnaires. These fields allow staff to know which questionnaire this is of the total number of questionnaires.](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="4.771023622047244in" height="1.4058825459317585in"}
- If the number is greater, make certain that you have only the CQs for the TL you are working on by comparing the geocoding data (**SCID, State, County, AA Number, TL Tract, and TL Block codes**) on the EQ to that on the SC-117. If it belongs to another TL, place it with that group.
- If the number is fewer, and after recounting, you cannot locate a possibly missing CQ, notify your supervisor, and contact the Lead FR for an explanation.
- Enter your initials in Column (F) and place the CQ back inside its corresponding EQ.
Example: If a TU qualifies for a full interview, and 18 people live or stay in that TU, there should be one EQ and two CQs. Each EQ can hold responses for up to 6 people. The additional 14 people would be enumerated on the two CQs.

title: Task List No. 4 (Column (A))
content:
- Mark (X) the box in Column (B) as you complete Task 4.
- If the **TL POPULATION COUNT** in **Item H, Section B1:** *ETL Summary*, of the Form SC-117 is zero (0), there should be **no** EQs or CQs. Confirm that a status other than **Complete** is marked in **Section B2**: *ETL Status* of the Form SC-117.
- If **Yes,** then, mark (X) **Yes** in Column (D), enter your initials in Column (F)
- If the **TL POPULATION COUNT** is **NOT** zero and there are EQs/CQs, yet a status other than **Complete** is marked, then change the status to **Complete** in **Section B2**, of the Form SC-117.
- Mark (X) **No** in Column (E) and enter your initials in Column (F).

title: Task List No. 5 (Column (A))
content:
- Mark (X) the box in Column (B) as you complete Task 5.
- You may wish to use a calculator for this step, so that you do not miscount the population number.
- Add up the number of people written **Item B** of the **Interview Summary** section on page 8 of **each EQ** for the TL and compare the number to the **TL POPULATION COUNT** in **Item H**, **Section B1**, *ETL Summary*, of the Form SC-117. See **Figure 15.12**.
- If the numbers match, mark (X) **Yes** in Column (D) and enter your initials in Column (F).
- If the numbers do not match, mark (X) No in Column (E).
- Reconcile the numbers, and enter the correct number in **Item H**, **Section B1**, *ETL Summary* of the Form SC-117.
- Enter your initials in Column (F).
![Image showing item B from the questionnaire which asks for the number of people listed on questionnaire(s). This is also called the pop count. ](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="5.316135170603674in" height="0.9165748031496063in"}

title: Task List No. 6 (Column (A))
content:
- Geocoding data will be entered only on the front of EQs (See **Figure 15.13**) in which a full interview was conducted. The FR transcribes this information from the Form SC-693.2(ETL), *Transitory Location Listing Sheet*.
![Image showing the geocoding information from the questionnaire including SCID, State, County, AA, TL Tract, and TL Block. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image5_9a76b513.png){width="4.161334208223972in" height="1.5613167104111987in"}
- Confirm that a full interview was conducted by checking that the answer to **Screening Question S2,** "Do *all of the people staying in this \[RV/boat/room/unit\] have another place where they usually live?* was marked **No**. If the answer was marked **Yes**, a full interview was not conducted, and the geocoding data need not have been completed on the form.
- Mark (X) the box in Column (B) as you complete Task 6.
- For each EQ/CQ for which there is a complete interview (as described above), verify that all the geocoding fields (**SCID, State, County, AA Number, TL Tract, and TL Block codes)** are completed correctly and that they match the information in the header of the Form SC-117.
- If **Yes**, mark **Yes** in Column (D) and enter your initials in Column (F).
- If **No,** mark **No** in Column (E). You may have to complete a new EQ/CQ.
- Enter your initials in Column (F).

title: Check-in ETL Materials
content:
Once you have completed office review for a TL, using the Form SC-691, *ETL Clerk Office Review Checklist*, and there are no errors to be fixed, start to check-in the Form SC-117, *Transitory Location Control Record* (TLCR) and the associated EQs/CQs.
- Separate the EQs/CQs and Form SC-117 from any other materials associated with the TL (Forms SC-225, INFO-COMMs, Forms SC-693.2(ETL), TL Listing Sheets). **You will scan only the EQs/CQs and Form SC-117.**
- Scan the TL Barcode ID on the Form SC-117.
- Scan each EQ and its associated CQ. Place the CQ(s) back inside the EQ.
- As you scan the EQs/CQs, place them into storage until the end of the operation to eventually get shipped to NPC.
- Place the scanned Form SC-117 on top of the scanned questionnaires.
- Even if a TL doesn't have TL questionnaires, scan it into MOJO anyways. These questionnaires will have the outcome entered into MOJO.

title: ETL Add Cases
content:
## ETL Transitory Location Adds
During the ETL visit, FRs may learn that:
- The assigned transitory location has undergone a name or an address change (Form SC-117, **Section A1**, *Transitory Location Advance Contact Information*, **Item 4 and 5,** *TL Name* and *Street Name* fields are different from what is in the **Header** of the Form SC-117). They could have visited the incorrect location, *or it may be a new TL*.
- Notify your supervisor.
- You may be instructed to conduct research.
- The TL contact person manages another TL (Form SC-117, **Section A1**, **Item 17** is marked **Yes**) but the Lead FR does not have another Form SC-117 for that location, therefore they could not conduct an in-field interview for that TL. They should have completed information in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117 and a Form SC-225, INFO-COMM about the potentially new TL. In this situation, you should also notify your supervisor and possibly be prepared to conduct research.

title: Conducting TL Research
content:
- TL Name/Address Changes
- You need to determine if the ETL team visited the right location.
- Search the TL workload to determine if that location is already in the workload. It may be in the workload under the corrected name/address, but a different TL Case ID.
- Use **Google Search** for the original address to determine what is at that location.
    - Use **Google Search** for the TL name to determine what the address is (and to verify if it is within the SCO enumeration area).
- Potentially New TLs
- If there is information in the **Notes** section of the Form SC-117 and/or a Form SC-225 containing information about another TL that the TL contact person manages, then you should:
    - Search the TL workload to determine if that location is already in the workload. It could be assigned to another Lead FR.
    - If it is already in the workload, indicate on the Form SC-117/SC-225 that the TL is a duplicate of a case in the workload and will not be added.
- If you determine that the address is not in the workload, and it is within the SCO's enumeration area, then you must add the location to the TL workload via MOJO.
    - Print the Form SC-117 for the new TL.
    - Your supervisor must assign a Lead FR to the case for a TLAC in-field interview if there is time. Follow instructions in **Topic 4,** T*ransitory Locations Advance Contact (TLAC) Assignment Preparation and Checkout.*

title: Quality Control Operations
content:
## Introduction
## Overview
This chapter provides information about the quality control (QC) program used to monitor, control, and enhance the quality of the housing unit data collected by Special Census Field Representatives. This chapter provides information on the different activities performed by the office staff to support the quality control operations.

title: The Special Census Supervisor's Role in Quality Control
content:
The Special Census Supervisor implements the QC plan to ensure the collection of the highest possible quality data. The QC activities include field and office reviews of completed work.
For the field work, the Special Census Supervisor ensures that:
- SC-1222, Special Observation Checklists are completed within one week after FRs receive their first assignment
- Based on initial observation results, determines if a Field Representative requires an additional observation they should be marked as Additional observation. The Special Census Supervisor also determines the type of administrative action to take on a Field Representative that is marked as Additional observation
- QC Field Supervisors complete the Dependent Quality Check (DQC) and perform Recanvass for AAs that fail DQC
- Production work is checked in to MOJO and selected for reinterview
- Reinterview work is assigned as soon as Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, are selected for Reinterview
- Reinterview cases that could not be completed over the telephone are assigned to a RI FR
- A final reinterview status is assigned to cases where Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, does not match Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires
- Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, requiring additional reviews are placed in Supplemental Reinterview

title: QC Program Field Components
content:
The Special Census QC program consists of five distinct components. These components are:
- Initial Observations
- Dependent Quality Check (DQC)
- Zero Housing Unit Recanvass
- Population and Housing Unit Comparison Test
- Reinterviews

title: Initial Observations
Responsibilities for Initial Observations
content:
The Field Supervisor observes the Field Representative perform his or her duties. For production, the Field Supervisor observes the Field Representative working five housing unit addresses and conducting at least one interview or for up to two hours, whichever comes first. For Reinterview, the Field Supervisor observes the Field Representative conducting three housing unit interviews or for up to two hours, whichever comes first. If the Field Representative performs adequately, he or she is allowed to work without further observation.
If the Field Representative does not perform adequately during the initial observation, the Field Supervisor recommends to the Field Manager that the FR is observed an additional time. Field Supervisors may also recommend discussing other actions with the Field Manager. Field Supervisors can only recommend a termination, but the Special Census Supervisor makes the final decision.
The Manager reviews Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, and evaluates the Field Supervisor's notes from the initial observation. The Field Manager considers the following when deciding whether to allow an additional observation:
- Were the tasks the Field Representative failed to perform adequately difficult?
- Was the enumeration area difficult to enumerate?
- Did the Field Supervisor observe enough housing units to determine a fair outcome?
- Did the Field Supervisor base his or her outcome on only one observed housing unit?
- Does the Field Supervisor think this Field Representative will benefit from on-the-job training and a second observation?
The Field Manager decides to:
- Allow the Field Supervisor to conduct an on-the-job training and an additional observation, or
- Mark the Field Representative as Consult manager
Marking a Field Representative as Consult manager means the Field Representative was unsatisfactory performing the listing and enumeration tasks and providing on-the-job training and an additional observation will not benefit the operation. Even though this is possible, it is unlikely that a Field Representative will not improve his or her performance after an on-the-job training session.
If, after reviewing the results of Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, the Field Manager determines that the Field Representative is unsatisfactory in performing listing and/or enumeration activities, the Field Manager must complete Form SC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems and Form SC-283, Documentation of Termination for Performance and/or Performance Problems and contact the Regional Office to obtain approval to terminate the employee. Refer to Chapter 7 for the instructions for terminating an employee for performance problems.
If the Field Manager allows an additional observation:
- For Production, the Field Supervisor provides further training before observing the Field Representative perform the listing and/or enumeration activities for five housing unit addresses and conducting at least one interview or for up to two hours, whichever comes first. If the Field Representative performs the listing/enumeration tasks adequately, he or she will be allowed to continue working.
- For Reinterview, the Field Supervisor provides further training before observing the Field Representative perform the enumeration activities for three housing unit interviews or for up to two hours, whichever comes first. If the Field Representative performs the listing/enumeration tasks adequately, he or she will be allowed to continue working.
The clerks enter the observation recommendation from Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, into MOJO. Depending on the result of the initial observation, the clerks may need to enter information for an additional observation. If an additional observation is needed, a new Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, will be completed by the Field Supervisor during the additional observation and returned to the SCO for keying into MOJO. Refer Chapter 13, Topic 5 for more information about updating MOJO when a Field Representatives requires an additional observation. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for MOJO for steps to enter observation data in MOJO.

title: Monitoring the Completion of the Observation Forms
content: All observations and Form SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist, must be completed within the first week of field operations. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager use Table [XXX]{.mark} in MOJO to monitor the completion and results of the observations. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager must refer to Table [XXX]{.mark} to determine if there are any outstanding observations after the first week of operations. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager must follow up with the Field Supervisor to complete the outstanding observations. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for MOJO for steps to monitor the completion and results of the observations.

title: Dependent Quality Check
content:
## Overview
The Dependent Quality Check (DQC) is used to determine if the Field Representatives (FRs) properly follow listing and canvassing procedures. During listing, Field Representatives canvass blocks in their assigned AA to locate all housing units and verify and update all information on the address registers completely and accurately. The Quality Control Field Supervisor (QC FS) determines whether the AA passed or failed DQC by checking a sample of 12 consecutive addresses on the ground. If fewer than 12 addresses exist in the AA, the QC FS checks all addresses in the AA. The QC FSs use the SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record to record the results of DQC. If the AA fails DQC, then the QC FS recanvasses the entire AA.
In addition to checking a sample of addresses, if there are blocks within the AA or an entire AA with zero housing units, the QC FS performs a zero-housing unit recanvass during DQC. During this recanvass, the QC FS:
- Verifies that the AA or specific blocks within the AA do not have any housing units.
- Enters a note in the first row of the SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record, confirming there are no living quarters in the AA.
- Adds housing units and conducts an interview for housing units that were added during DQC.
If blocks have a 10% difference in the housing unit and population counts between the 2020 Census and the Special Census, the QC FS will also canvass those blocks during DQC.

title: Special Census Supervisor Responsibilities for DQC
content: The Special Census Supervisor ensures that QC FSs conduct DQC as AAs are assigned for DQC. After DQC is complete, the Address Register is checked in.

title: Preparing the Address Register for Dependent Quality Check
content:
Every Address Register must go through DQC. After the Address Registers are checked in from production, clerks prepare the Address Registers for DQC. Clerks run report SC-328B, Count Comparison by Block from MOJO to identify blocks that have a population count and/or housing unit count that is 10% over and/or under the 2020 population count/or housing unit count. Clerks prepare Form SC-320, Error List, for each AA and include it with the Address Register for DQC only when:
- Errors from production are identified during the Address Register Office Review process.
- There is a 10% difference (over and under) between the 2020 Census housing unit and population count and the Special Census housing unit and population count
- There are blocks with zero housing units or entire AAs with zero housing units.
Clerks complete the header of the SC-320, Error List, by entering the following items in the provided spaces:
- SCID number
- AA number
- Date the SC-320, Error List, was prepared
- Field Supervisor's name
The clerks enter the following information:
- Column (a), Form Type -- check the appropriate box to indicate the form where the error was identified
- Column (b), Form Line No. -- the line number of the form where the error was identified
- Column (c) -- the Case ID associated with the address (only filled out if there was an error identified on Form SC-920, Address List Page, or Form SC-921, Add Page)
- Column (d) Issue -- a short description of the error. For example, Line 3 is missing an action code, confirm 10% over for the housing unit count, or verify no LQs in block 1001
Column (E), Resolution, is completed in the field by the QC FS.
After preparing Form SC-320, Error List, the clerks make a copy keep in the office. The original Form SC-320, Error List, is placed inside the cover of the Address Register so the QC FS can resolve the error(s) while conducting the Dependent Quality Check.
To prepare the Address Registers for DQC, the clerks:
- Write, using a black ink ballpoint pen, the Dependent Quality Check starting address line number identified by MOJO in the Starting address line number box in the upper right corner of the SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record, which is the last page in the Address Register. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for instructions on accessing the starting address line number for DQC.
- If the DQC starting line address happens to be a line that was crossed out by the FR because the address was mistakenly added, then write the number for the next available line on Form SC-921, Add Page. If there are no additional addresses listed on Form SC-921, Add Page, then write the first line number of Form SC-920, Address List Page.
- Insert filled out Form SC-320, Error List, if applicable, inside the front cover of the Address Register.
- Confirm there is a line drawn in red pencil under the last address added during production on Form SC-921, Add Page. If not, draw a line in red pencil under the last address added during production on Form SC-921, Add Page.
- If there are no adds on Form SC-921, then write no adds in red pencil in the first row of Form SC-921, Add Page
- On Form SC-940, Address Register Cover Page, in Section 1, Assignment Information, under row (d) DQC FS, enter the Name, Employee ID, and Telephone Number of the DQC FS to which the AA will be assigned.
- Assign and check out the Address Register to the appropriate QC FS. Refer to Form SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for the steps to assign an Address Register for DQC.

title: Check In from DQC
content:
After DQC has been completed for an AA, the Address Registers arrive in the SCO. Clerks check in Address Registers through MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for steps to check in Address Registers. The clerks:
- Retrieve Address Registers from the IN bin.
- Check in the Address Register to MOJO.
- Select/confirm the name of the QC Field Supervisor that completed the DQC on the Address Register from MOJO.
- Review the SC-320, Error List, if applicable, to ensure all errors were corrected.
- Consult the Field Manager or Special Census Supervisor for guidance if errors were not corrected.
- Enter the *Total number of failed addresses* (located in Column 5, under row 12) from Form SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record, which is in the back of the Address Register, into MOJO.

title: Office Review for DQC
content:
After the Address Registers are checked in from DQC, the office clerks conduct an Office Review of each Address Register and any associated questionnaires. Form SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record is used by QC FS to record the results of the DQC. Form SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record is the last page in the back of the Address Register. The clerks review the completed Form SC-435, Dependent Quality Check Record, after the Address Register is checked in from DQC.
The clerks follow the Section 7, Dependent Quality Check Office Review of Form SC-1131 Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, to see if instances of over coverage or under coverage were identified by the QC FS during DQC:
- Entered listing line number in Column (2), if Address Missing is from List Page and Add Page. This indicates under coverage. In this situation, the QC FS adds the housing unit address to the Add Page and conducts an interview. The clerks must ensure a Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, was completed by the QC FS. Refer to Section 7, Dependent Quality Check Office Review of Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, for office review procedures.
- Entered listing line number in Column (3), (Look at Form SC-920, Address List Page) if the Action Code in Column 4 of the Form SC-920 has Action Code U (Uninhabitable), N (Nonresidential), DCL (Unable to Locate), or CW (Cannot Work) but should have Action Code V (Verified) or C (Correction). This indicates under coverage. In this situation, the QC FS conducts an interview at the housing unit and completes the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire during the DQC. The QC FS has six attempts to contact a respondent at the housing unit. The first attempt must be made in person. Any later attempts can be made in person or by telephone, if a telephone number was provided. The QC FS enters responses to the questions on the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire. The clerks must ensure a Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, was completed. Refer to Section 7, Dependent Quality Check Office Review of Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials.
- Entered listing line number in Column (4), (Look at Form SC-920, Address List Page) if the Action Code in Column 4 of the Form SC-920 has Action Code V (Verified) or C (Correction) but should have Action Code U (Uninhabitable) or N (Nonresidential). This indicates over coverage. Refer Section 7, Dependent Quality Check Office Review, of Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, for Dependent Quality Check Office Review.
If an Address Register fails DQC, then the clerks must also review the Address List Page(s) and Add Page(s) to determine if new housing units were discovered during Recanvass and to determine if any known addresses on the Address List Page had an action code change during Recanvass that changed an address from a housing unit to a non-housing unit and vice versa. Refer to Section 7, Dependent Quality Check Office Review of Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials.

title: Population and Housing Unit Comparison Test
content:
## Overview
The population and housing unit comparison test is used to determine whether an area experienced a large increase or decrease in the population or housing unit count compared to the totals from the 2020 Census. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager must print the report from MOJO and review the SC-328, Count Comparison by Block, report daily and to conduct this comparison. If there are concerns after reviewing the SC-328, Count Comparison by Block, report the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager discusses with the Field Supervisor.

title: The Special Census Supervisor Role in the Population and Housing Unit Comparison Test
content:
If the population or housing unit count largely differs from the 2020 Census, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager contacts the Field Supervisor for a possible explanation. For example, Happy Valley, a new subdivision of 37 homes was built since the 2020 Census. This information can help the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager decide whether an AA should be verified.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager reviews and evaluates the reasons for an increase or decrease provided by the Field Supervisor to determine if they are valid.
- If there is a reasonable explanation, the Address Register continues with the check in and office review process.
- If there is no reasonable explanation for the large difference between the 2020 Census and the Special Census population count or housing unit count, the clerk adds an issue to Form SC-320, Error List. The Field Manager and Special Census Supervisor define the strategy for addressing the issue.
Pending results of the investigation, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager may require the AA to be recanvassed and put all questionnaires into Supplemental Reinterview.

title: Reinterview
content:
## Overview
The purpose of Reinterview (RI) is to verify the accuracy of the housing unit status and population count recorded by the Field Representatives on completed Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires.
As completed Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires are checked in to MOJO, they are randomly selected for Reinterview.
Reinterview cases with telephone numbers are initially assigned to office clerks to complete over the telephone. Cases that could not be completed over the telephone or that did not have telephone numbers are assigned to Reinterview FRs to complete in the field.

title: Types of Reinterview
content:
There are three types of Reinterview cases. These are:
- Random
- Supplemental
- Hard Fail Supplemental

title: Random
content:
MOJO selects one of the first three housing unit cases worked by the FR, followed by one randomly selected case from the next 10 completed housing unit cases, and then every 10th completed housing unit case thereafter. If the selected case is ineligible for RI, MOJO will select the next RI eligible completed case.
Questionnaires with a unit status of Cannot Locate and Duplicate as well as questionnaires with an Interview Outcome Code of Refusal (REF) are ineligible for Reinterview. Closeout cases (a case is closed out when it is still incomplete at the end of the operation) and replacement questionnaires (forms the QC FR completed during reinterview) are also ineligible for RI.
Clerks and RI FRs use the Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, when conducting the Reinterview. If the housing unit was contacted, the clerks or RI FRs complete Questions 1 through 6 on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire and complete the roster in Question 7. If the housing unit was not contacted or the respondent does not remember being contacted, the clerks or RI FRs complete Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, for housing unit.

title: Supplemental Reinterview
content:
If at any time the SCO staff have reason to suspect that a FR is falsifying data, or if they suspect an interview has not been done following established procedures, they can include additional interviews in Supplemental RI. SCO staff can either flag a specific case for supplemental RI or can flag an FR in which case the system will select the next two eligible cases worked by the FR for RI. The SCO staff flag supplemental RI cases for an FR if they suspect the FR conducted poor listing work and therefore want to check on the quality of the enumeration work of the FR. Supplemental Reinterview can be used as verification that the Field Representative completed the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, according to the Special Census procedures.
The SC-425(RI), RI Questionnaire List, includes a column that shows the RI Type (type of RI: random, supplemental, hard fail supplemental).
Refer to Topic 7 for guidance on when it is appropriate to select questionnaires for supplemental reinterview.

title: Hard Fail Supplemental Reinterview
content:
If a Field Representative is found falsifying work or intentionally not following procedures, the Field Representative will be flagged as a Hard Failed Field Representative. In this situation, all the eligible completed work by the Field Representative is sent to Reinterview as a Supplemental Hard Fail. The reason for this action is to ensure that all previously completed work by this Field Representative was done following Special Census procedures.
Refer to Topic 6 in this chapter for more information about hard fail Reinterview.

title: The Special Census Supervisor Role in Reinterview
content:
The Special Census Supervisor has a dual role in Reinterview operations. One role is to ensure that production clerks prepare the Reinterview assignments and that Reinterview cases are assigned to QC clerks in the SCO or to RI FRs. The other role is to evaluate and decide on a final reinterview status in instances where Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire completed by a Field Representative does not match the corresponding completed SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
The Special Census Supervisor ensures that:
- Cases selected for Reinterview are set aside for Production clerks to prepare the Reinterview assignment
- Production clerks print the appropriate English or Spanish version of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, to match the version used for the production interview. MOJO provides an indicator of whether the production interview was conducted in English or Spanish on the screen used to print Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
- Production clerks transcribe the original interview Respondent Information to the Original Respondent Information section on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
- Check MOJO to determine if an address is flagged as proceed with caution: and adds a note in the Notes section that includes the reason the address is dangerous and a note to inform the FR to proceed with caution when approaching the address.
- Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires with telephone numbers are assigned QC clerks to conduct telephone reinterview.
- Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires without a telephone number or where the QC clerks could not complete a reinterview over the telephone within 3 attempts are assigned to RI FRs.
- QC clerks check in completed SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires to MOJO. The QC clerk who checks in the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire must not be the same QC clerk who completed the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
The Special Census Supervisor also:
- Reviews cases where the original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, and the corresponding Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire do not match
- Determines a final reinterview status when Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire does not match Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
- Places cases in Supplemental Reinterview that may need a second review, such as questionnaires with where more information is needed to assign an outcome.

title: Assigning Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires to QC Clerks
content:
Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire is initially assigned to QC clerks or QC FSs. All Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires with a telephone number in OR2, Original Respondent Telephone Number, are assigned and checked out to QC clerks to complete over the telephone. QC clerks have three attempts to complete Form SC-RQ, Special Reinterview Questionnaire over the telephone.
Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires that do not have a telephone number in OR2 or interviews were not completed after three attempts by QC clerks are grouped by AA and assigned to QC FSs to assign to RI FRs to complete by personal visit. Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire(s), without a telephone number in OR2 or interview were not completed after three attempts by a QC clerk are checked out to the QC FS in MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for the steps to checkout Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires to staff for the Reinterview operation.
After checking out Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires out to the QC FS:
- Clerks secure all the Forms SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires for the same AA using a binder clip.
- The Field Manager delivers all the Forms SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires to the QC FS.
- The QC FS writes the RI FR reassignments on Form SC-336.1, Reassignment Worksheet, and provides it to the Field Manager to return to the office.
- The clerks reassign, in MOJO, each Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire from the QC FS to the appropriate RI FR based on the information on Form SC-336.1, Reassignment Worksheet.

title: Completing Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire over the Telephone
content:
The QC clerks conduct telephone reinterviews in instances when a telephone number is available. During telephone reinterview, a QC clerk may only need to complete Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. In other instances, the QC clerk may also complete a full telephone interview using Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, based on responses provided during reinterview. QC clerks must have a supply of unlabeled Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, available during the reinterview in case a full interview is required. All entries on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, and Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, must be made using a black ink ballpoint pen.
Refer to Form SC-50.1, Special Census Office Job Aids, for details on conducting a telephone reinterview.
Refer to Reinterview on page [350](#reinterview-1) for additional information on Reinterview.
The QC clerks use Form SC-50.1, Special Census Job Aids to complete Form SC-RQ over the telephone. Refer to *Office Telephone Reinterview Job Aid in Form SC-50.1* for the script to use when completing the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
A black ink ballpoint pen ***must*** be used when completing questionnaires.
QC clerks must also have a supply of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire available in case a full interview is required. Refer to *Office Telephone Interview Job Aid* in Form SC-50.1 for the script to use when completing the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire.
The QC clerks use a black ink ballpoint pen when completing Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire while conducting telephone interviews.

title: Original Respondent's Information Section and Type of Respondent
content:
The QC clerks contact the original respondent the Field Representative contacted in his/her original interview. This original respondent could be a person living at the address or it can be a proxy respondent living at a different address.
It is important that QC clerks understand who they are contacting during the telephone interview. There are two items on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire the QC clerks look at to determine type of respondent being contacted. Items OR3, Original Respondent Type and OR4, Address of the neighbor or proxy who provided the information on the original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire provide information on the type of respondent.
![An image showing an example of the questionnaire items OR3. Original Respondent Type and OR4. Address of Neighbor or Proxy. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="4.833333333333333in" height="3.1666666666666665in"}
If the *Lived or stayed in this \[house/apartment/mobile home\] on (Special Census Day)* or *Moved into this \[house/apartment/mobile home after (Special Census Day)* boxes are marked, the QC clerks contacts a respondent at the address shown on the address label. The information in OR1, Original Respondent's Name, and OR2, Original Respondent Telephone Number contain information about the original respondent the Field Representative contacted.
If the *Did not live or stay in this \[house/apartment/mobile home\](neighbor or other proxy)* box is marked with X in item OR3, the QC clerks contact a neighbor or proxy that provided the information for the address shown in the label. In this case, the QC clerks may need to remind the neighbor or proxy that he or she is asking about the address in the label and not about their own address, which is the address in OR4 Address of neighbor or proxy.

title: Record of Contact
content:
The QC clerks have up to three contact attempts on different days and different times to contact the respondent by telephone. The Record of Contact is completed after the QC clerks finish with the telephone call.
For each contact attempt, the QC clerks enter in the Record of Contact the following information:
- **Interview type** -- the QC clerks always mark X the Telephone box,
- **Month, Day, Hour, Minutes** -- the QC clerks enter the month, day, hour, and minutes when the telephone Reinterview was attempted. The clerks also mark X the a.m. or p.m. as appropriate, and
- **Outcome** -- the QC clerks enter the interview outcome:
- **NV** -- Not used by the QC clerk
- **NC** -- Used if the QC clerk made a phone call and did not make contact
- **RE** -- Used when the respondent refused to complete the reinterview
- **CI** -- Used when the QC clerk conducted the reinterview
- **OT** -- Used when for other reasons, such an invalid telephone number.
The QC clerks only log three attempts in the Reinterview Record of Contact section. If the QC clerk is unable to complete the telephone reinterview after three contact attempts, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager reassigns the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire to a QC FS so a personal interview can be conducted by a RI FR.
![Images showing the Reinterview Record of Contact section of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="6.5in" height="1.8694444444444445in"}
Introduction Section and Contacting the Original Respondent
Questions 1through 6 are the introductory questions for the reinterview. These questions determine who the clerk is talking to, who lives at the address shown on the label, whether the unit was vacant or not a housing unit on the Special Census Date, and the population count if the housing unit is occupied.
The QC clerk:
- Contacts the original respondent by using the information in Items OR1 or OR2, to verify the housing unit status and population. Clerks must know if they are talking with a resident or a proxy.
- Introduces himself or herself to the respondent using the introduction in Question 1.
![Image showing an example of question 1 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="4.770833333333333in" height="1.4375in"}
- Asks Question 2 exactly as worded.
- If the respondent responds No or Don't Know, follows instructions in Form SC-50.1, SCO Office Job Aids to conduct a full interview using the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire.
![Image showing an example of question 2 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="4.645833333333333in" height="2.0in"}
Asks Question 3 exactly as worded.
![Image showing an example of question 3 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="4.520833333333333in" height="1.3020833333333333in"}
This question asks if anyone was living or staying at the **Address printed on the label** on the Special Census Day. If the QC clerk is talking to an original proxy respondent, the QC clerk must remind the respondent that he or she is asking for the information related to the address on the label.
If the respondent answers Yes, follow the skip pattern and continue with Question 5.
If the respondent answers No, continue to Question 4.
Asks Question 4 exactly as worded.
![Image showing an example of question 4 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="3.4479166666666665in" height="1.1770833333333333in"}
Asks Question 5 exactly as worded.
![Image showing an example of question 5 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="4.697916666666667in" height="1.65625in"}
This question asks for the number of people that were living or staying at the address shown on the label. If the address is for the original respondent, then the QC clerk is asking the respondent about their own home. If the address is for a proxy, then the QC clerk must remind the proxy respondent that he or she is providing information for the housing unit shown on the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire label and not his or her own housing unit.
The QC clerk writes the number of people living at the address on the Special Census Day.
Asks question 6 exactly as worded.
![Image showing an example of question 6 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="4.677083333333333in" height="2.9270833333333335in"}
This question asks whether there were additional people not included in Question 5 that need to be included in the count. The QC clerk marks the appropriate box.
Asks Question 7 exactly as worded.
![Image showing an example of question 7 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is blank.](/images/imports/1/image6_98eef807.png){width="6.5in" height="3.390277777777778in"}
The QC clerk collects the household roster for the address shown on the label. The respondent provides the names of the people living at the housing unit on the Special Census Day.
Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire has space for collecting 10 names. If there are more than 10 persons living at the housing unit, the QC clerk uses another blank Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire and continues adding the names of the people living at the housing unit. The QC clerk numbers each Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire in the upper right corner.
Refer to the figure below on where to place the number of forms.
![Image showing an example of writing the number of this forms and the total number of forms. The image shows a the handwritten forms as 1 of 3 and in a hand-drawn circle above question 1 of the reinterview questionnaire. The form is otherwise blank.](/images/imports/1/image7_e63915e1.png){width="3.7551060804899388in" height="2.3684733158355207in"}

title: Completing Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
content:
After the QC clerk completes a telephone reinterview, he or she thanks the respondent for their time responding to the questionnaire. We always want to leave a good impression with our respondents.
The QC clerk completes Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire by:
- Completing the Reinterview Record of Contact section
- Signing his or her name in the Certification section
- Entering his or her Employee ID in the Certification section
- Entering the Month, Day, and Year in the Certification section under their signature
- Adding the FSA Number in the Field Supervisor area of the Certification section
Use a paper clip or a binder clip, when there are multiple Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires from a large household, to keep all Form-RQ, Special Census Questionnaire(s)together before checking them in to MOJO.
Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, must be checked in to MOJO after the reinterview is complete. **Do not check in any Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire completed during QC until after Reinterview Office Matching is complete.** If Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, is used during Reinterview, then the office staff must print the associated HU Full-RI label from MOJO and affix it to Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, used during Reinterview. The HU Full-RI label includes a different form type value in the barcode ID to ensure it is different from Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed during production. After checking in Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, the next step is to complete the matching of the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire to the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire.
If the QC clerk is unable to complete the telephone reinterview within three telephone attempts, the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire must be reassigned to a QC FS for reassignment to a RI FR.

title: Matching the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire with the Corresponding SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire
content:
After the reinterview is completed, in the office or returned from the field, and Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, has been checked into MOJO, the QC clerks conduct an office review of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, to determine if all needed information was collected and also match the completed Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, with its corresponding Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the production Field Representative. The QC clerks locate the original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, in a secured temporary bin to match it with its corresponding Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. The clerks review the Case ID on both questionnaires to ensure the Case IDs match.
After the Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, and Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, are matched, the QC clerk conducts a matching review. The QC clerk conducting the matching review cannot be the same clerk that completed Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. Refer to Topic 6 for more information on the matching review.
When reviewing a case, keep in mind that names in the roster may not match for many reasons. Differences in spellings, or in the form names take, in the original interview and the reinterview can occur. Refer to the Reinterview Matching Names Job Aid section of the SC 50.1 SCO Job Aid for help in matching.

title: Reinterview Check In, Reinterview Office Review, Matching Review and Entering Reinterview Status
content:
## Overview
Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires, are checked in to MOJO prior to Reinterview Office Review and Matching Review. **Do not check in any Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed during Reinterview until the after Reinterview Office Matching is complete.**
After checking in completed Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires, to MOJO, clerks perform an office review on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, to determine if all the needed information was collected.
If the information was collected appropriately, the clerks match Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, with its corresponding Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, to determine if the Field Representative followed the Special Census procedures.
If the information from Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, and Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, match, the clerks mark X in the Pass box in the Clerk Office Review -- Initial in the Reinterview Status section of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. If the clerk finds one or more mismatches between Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire and Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire the clerks mark X in the Defer to Supervisor box and provides the case to the supervisor to decide on a final reinterview status.

title: SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire Check In
content:
Reinterview work is checked in to MOJO after reinterviews are completed by QC clerks or by RI FRs. Ensure Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, is checked in with the appropriate QC clerk or RI FR who completed the interview. **Do not check in any Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed during Reinterview until the after Reinterview Office Matching is complete.**
Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for the steps to check in Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires, to MOJO.

title: Reinterview Office Review
content: The QC clerks perform a review of the completed SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. The clerks ensure all questions are answered appropriately. The QC clerks attempt to fix any missing information in the office before conducting the matching review. Refer to Section 5, Reinterview Office Review of Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials for instructions on completing the reinterview office review. After the Reinterview Office Review is complete, the QC clerks conduct the Reinterview Office Matching.

title: Reinterview Office Matching
content:
The QC clerks compare the original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire to Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire to determine if the questionnaires match.
During the Reinterview Office Matching the QC clerks:
- Determine if the respondent of the reinterview was previously contacted by a Field Representative
- Determine whether the housing unit status of the SC-RQ, Special Census Questionnaire, matches the housing unit status of the SC-Q, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
- Check, if the housing unit was occupied on the Special Census Date, that the number of people that lived or stayed at the housing unit on the Special Census Date collected in Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, matches the number of people collected in Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
- Check, if the housing unit was occupied on the Special Census Date, that the people listed in the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, and the people listed in the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire match at least 75% of the names listed.
Refer to Section 6, Reinterview Office Matching of Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials, for instructions on completing the reinterview office matching. Also refer to Form SC-50.1, SCO Job Aids.

title: Supervisor Review Matching Final Reinterview Status
content:
All cases coded Defer to the Supervisor are reviewed by the Special Census Supervisor or the Field Manager in the SCO. It is the responsibility of the supervisor or Field Manager to assign a final reinterview status to the cases deferred to him or her by the QC clerks.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager checks the Field Representative's work against the reinterview completed for the same housing unit. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager determines if the Field Representative followed Special Census procedures and ensures data was not falsified.
To determine a final reinterview status on these cases, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager:
- Reviews other work completed by the same Field Representative
- Places additional work in supplemental reinterview
- Speaks to the Field Representative or Field Supervisor to resolve discrepancies between the original interview and reinterview questionnaire.
Based on the review of the case, the Special Census Supervisor assigns a final reinterview status and makes any necessary corrections to the questionnaires.
The supervisor assigns a final reinterview status of:
- **Pass** -- after further research, the Special Census Supervisor determines that the Field Representative followed procedures and discrepancies were not due to Field Representative error. For example, a respondent might have forgotten a Field Representative visited the household to complete a questionnaire.
- **Soft Fail/honest mistake** -- the Special Census Supervisor receives a reasonable explanation from the Field Supervisor or Field Representative related to the discrepancies found between the questionnaires. For example, the Field Representative accidentally went to the wrong housing unit to complete a questionnaire.
- **Hard Fail/intentional falsification or deviation from procedures** -- after further research the Field Representative has a pattern of not following procedures after feedback was provided to correct the patterns; or was found falsifying some or all the data in the questionnaire.
- **Non-Interview --** after all allowed contact attempts, the Reinterview Field Representative could not complete a reinterview or was unable to collect enough data for the reinterview to complete matching.
The Special Census Supervisor selects the appropriate Final Reinterview Status on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Questionnaire, and documents the steps taken to investigate the case in the Notes section of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.

title: Final Reinterview Status
content:
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager takes further actions depending on the outcome of the case. After the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager decides on final Reinterview Status, the QC clerks update MOJO with the Reinterview Status from Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.
The final reinterview status must be entered in MOJO for every reinterview case. If a final reinterview status has not been entered in MOJO at the time the corresponding SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, is being boxed at the end of the operation, then an error is displayed to remind the clerk that a final reinterview status must be entered for the questionnaire before it can be added to a box. In MOJO, table SC-342C(RI), RI Questionnaires Not Checked In, can be used to monitor reinterview progress at the AA level by tracking reinterview questionnaires that have not been checked into the SCO.

title: Pass
content: If the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager can resolve the discrepancies between the original interview and the reinterview, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager assigns a final reinterview status of Pass. No further action is required for cases passed by the supervisor.

title: Soft Fail
content:
The soft fail final reinterview status is used for mistakes made by the Field Representative. Experience show that mistakes will occur early in the operation. For example, a Field Representative might have entered the wrong unit status for the housing unit he or she enumerated.
After further research, if the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager decides the discrepancy was an honest mistake, then the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager assigns a final reinterview status of Soft Fail.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager refers to Table SC-342S(RI) RI Status in MOJO to monitor the status of RI for Field Representatives that have multiple soft fails. If the Field Representative has two or more soft fails on the same error, this can be an indication that the Field Representative is intentionally or knowingly not following procedures. The Field Supervisor or Field Manager provides appropriate feedback on the errors committed by the Field Representative.
Cases coded as soft fail require that the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager informs the Field Supervisor about the Field Representative's mistake. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager prepares Form SC-225, INFO-COMM, to inform the Field Supervisor of the mistake. The Field Supervisor provides feedback to the Field Representative, so the mistake is not repeated.
After further research, if the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager determines that a Field Representative is intentionally or knowingly not following procedures, this situation could be grounds to hard fail the Field Representative. The Special Census supervisor or Field Manager closely reviews previous work by this Field Representative and determines if re-training, other corrective action, or administrative action is necessary.

title: Hard Fail
content:
A hard fail occurs when a Field Representative is intentionally or knowingly not following procedures or is found to have falsified part or all the data on a questionnaire. These cases require careful attention from the supervisor. A Field Representative found to be falsifying data or intentionally not following procedures can be grounds to remove the Field Representative from federal work.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager must be certain that a Field Representative is intentionally not following procedures or falsifying data before assigning a hard fail final reinterview status.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager must have information that supports a Field Representative has intentionally not followed procedures or has falsified data. If the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager believes appropriate information to support a hard fail is available and decides the outcome should be hard fail, then he or she:
- Informs the RO manager that a hard fail final reinterview status should be assigned to the Field Representative.
- Shows or explains the reason(s) for the hard fail.
- Completes Form SC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems and Form SC-283, Documentation of Termination for Conduct and/or Performance Problems, if the RO agrees to hard fail the Field Representative.
It is the responsibility of the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager to gather all the appropriate information that supports the Field Representative was found falsifying data or intentionally not following procedures. This supporting information is used to complete Form SC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems and SC-283, Documentation of Termination for Conduct and/or Performance Problems to remove the Field Representative from federal work. Refer to Chapter 7 for more information about removing staff from federal work.
Only after Form SC-282, Documentation of Conduct and/or Performance Problems and Form SC-283, Documentation of Termination for Conduct and/or Performance Problems are completed and signed, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager assigns a final reinterview status of Hard Fail.
When a hard fail final reinterview status is assigned to a Field Representative, all previous eligible completed work done by that Field Representative is automatically selected for hard fail Supplemental Reinterview to check if other work was completed according to procedures, and all their remaining work must be reassigned. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager instructs the clerk to:
- Print Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, from MOJO
- Locate, in the SCO storage area, all completed Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, completed by the hard fail Field Representative
- Transcribe the original respondent information from Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, onto Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. Refer to Preparing Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire in Chapter 13, Topic 3
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager ensures these questionnaires are checked out in MOJO.
Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO for the steps to place Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires in supplemental hard fail reinterview. In addition, any work that is currently assigned to this Field Representative must be reassigned to another Field Representative in the FSA.

title: Non-Interview
content:
If after all allowed contact attempts, the Reinterview Field Representative could not complete a reinterview or was unable to collect enough data for the reinterview to do a matching, a final reinterview status of *Non-interview* is assigned.
These are cases where the Field Representative could not complete a reinterview questionnaire for the housing unit. The Reinterview Field Representative who conducted the reinterview enters RI NI in the Notes section on the back of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, to indicate he or she could not complete the reinterview.
The Field Supervisor or Field Manager must ensure the Reinterview Field Representative made all attempts to complete the reinterview by checking the Reinterview Record of Contact section on the back for Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire. If the Field Supervisor or Field Manager is satisfied that the Reinterview Field Representative made every effort to complete Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, then a final reinterview status of *Non-interview*. The original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, is placed back to the storage bin.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager monitors the RI NI received in the office. The RI NI code should be used as a last resort and it is expected that clerks and Reinterview Field Representatives complete most if not all Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire.

title: Entering the Final Reinterview Status on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
content:
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager enters the final reinterview status on Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, after reviewing the results of the office matching review. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager enters in the Notes section on the back of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, a brief explanation of the final reinterview status assigned. This note must include the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager initials and date. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager marks X the appropriate box in the Reinterview Status section on the back of Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, to record the final reinterview status. See the following image for an example of this section completed.
![Image showing the Certification, Reinterview Status, and Notes sections of the form SC-RQ completed. The form is signed by an FR, is marked Defer to Supervisor, and includes a note that says, \"The population count on the SC-RQ is 3 and doesn\'t match the population count on the SC-Q which is 2.\"](/images/imports/1/image7_e63915e1.png){width="6.249219160104987in" height="2.8954713473315836in"}
**Managing Cases where the Respondent was not Contacted by the Field Representative**
The clerks automatically defer to the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager any Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire where the respondent answered that he or she was not contacted by a Field Representative (answered No or Don't Know for Question 2). These SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire(s), must have Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire completed for the housing unit.
In this situation the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager determines if a questionnaire was already completed for the housing unit. Sometimes respondents forget Census Bureau staff contacted them.
If Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire was previously completed for this housing unit, clerks compare both Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the Field Representative with the one completed by the QC clerk or Reinterview Field Representative to determine if the information matches between both questionnaires.
If Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the production FR and Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the QC clerk or RI FR **match**, the clerk:
1. Passes the SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, by marking X in the Clerk Office Review -- Initial Pass box in the Reinterview Status section.
54. Prints the appropriate HU Full RI label and affixes to the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed during RI
55. Checks in Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the QC clerk or RI FR. DO NOT mark the REP box on Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the QC clerk or RI FR.
56. Place Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the QC clerk or RI FR in the appropriate storage bin.
57. Return Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the production FR to the appropriate storage bin box.
58. Check in Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, and enter the RI Final Outcome in MOJO.
59. Place Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire, in the appropriate storage bin box.
If Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, completed by the QC clerk or Reinterview Field Representative **does not match** Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire completed by the Field Representative, the Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager determines which version of the SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire to accept. Refer to Form SC-1131, Office Checklist for Reviewing Materials and Section 6 -- Reinterview Office Matching, for detailed procedures.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager determines if this is a case of falsification or intentionally not following procedures by the Field Supervisor or Field Representative. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager researches the reasons why these questionnaires do not match and takes appropriate action.

title: Update MOJO with the Reinterview Status
content:
After check-in, Office Review, and Matching Review are complete, clerks enter the final Reinterview Status upon check in to MOJO.
Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for the steps to enter the Reinterview Status from Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaires, into MOJO.
