After entering the Reinterview Status, place Form SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire in the appropriate storage bin for the FSA. Place any original Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire(s), back in the appropriate storage bins.

title: Additional Questionnaire Reviews
content: The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager can send additional work to the field to be reviewed. For example, the Special Census Supervisor can send to supplemental reinterview cases with a population of 1 if the volume seems too high for the AA. The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager monitors and reviews the SC-341, HU Status by AA report to determine if additional Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires need to be sent to supplemental reinterview.

title: Reviewing the SC-341, HU Status by AA Report
content:
The SC-341, HU Status by AA report must be reviewed daily. This report shows the status of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires checked in to MOJO. A complete explanation of each column of the report is included in Chapter 17.
The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager uses this report to put Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, into supplemental reinterview if anything appears out of the ordinary, such as a high percentage or POP 1.

title: Sending Other Questionnaires for Supplemental Reinterview
content: The Special Census Supervisor or Field Manager may consider sending to supplemental reinterview other Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, completed by the Field Representative that may need more information to determine a final reinterview status. For example, multiple soft fails could be an indication that a Field Representative could be falsifying information or intentionally not following procedures. In this instance, consider selecting some questionnaires for supplemental reinterview to determine a final reinterview status for the FR.

title: Using Management Reports
content:
## Management Reports
## Overview
Field operations in the Special Census (SC) are short in duration and fast paced. It is extremely important to anticipate problems and resolve issues that may occur in the field as soon as possible. The SC management reports will help the Special Census Supervisor (SCS) detect issues and take appropriate action to resolve these issues. This chapter will explain in detail the management reports used during the SC operation.

title: Production Reports/Tables
content:
## SC-1019, Employee Listing
The SC-1019, Employee Listing, provides useful employee information. This report shows the employees by name, title, and spoken languages. This report also includes the employee's address and contact phone numbers.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-1019, Employee Listing, contains the following information:
- Employee ID
- FSA (the FSA to which the employee is assigned)
- Employee Name (Last Name, First Name, Middle Initial)
- Employee Type
- FR
- FS
- Language(s) (display all languages the employee speaks)
- Address (Address Number, Street Name)
- Phone Number(s)

title: Report Uses
content: This report is useful to identify staff with special language skills that the SCO can use to complete a questionnaire in a specific language. It can also be used to locate or communicate with field staff as necessary.

title: SC-336 HU Assignment Directory
content: The SC-336, HU Assignment Directory, shows housing unit assignment information for each AA by FSA. It is used to keep track of which FS or FR currently is assigned the case.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-336, HU Assignment Directory, contains the following information:
- SCO
- Date Assigned (date the AA was assigned)
- AA (6-digit AA number)
- Employee Name (Last Name, First Name, Middle Initial)
- Employee ID
- HUs (number of housing units expected in the AA)
- State (2-digit state code/2-character state abbreviation)
- County (3 county code/county name)
- FS

title: Report Uses
content: This report is useful to keep track of which FS or FR currently is assigned the case. Once the FS decides what FR to assign the case to, the FS will cross out their name and put in the FR name. The directory goes back to SCO for clerk to update MOJO with FR name.

title: SC-325 GQ Assignment Directory
content: The SC-325, GQ Assignment Directory, shows what FS or FR is assigned the GQ. It shows the GQ assignment information for each AA.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-325, GQ Assignment Directory, contains the following information:
- SCO
- Date Assigned (date the AA was assigned)
- AA (6-digit AA number)
- **Case ID**
- **GQ Name**
- **GQ Address**
- Employee Name (Last Name, First Name, Middle Initial)
- Employee ID
- GQs (number of GQs expected in the AA)
- State (2-digit state code/ 2-character state abbreviation)
- County (3 county code/ county name)
- FS

title: Report Uses
content: This report is useful to keep track of which FS or FR currently is assigned the GQ case.

title: SC-326 TL Assignment Directory
content: The SC-326, TL Assignment Directory, shows what FS or FR is assigned the TL. It shows the TL assignment information for each AA.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-325, TL Assignment Directory, contains the following information:
- SCO
- Date Assigned (date the AA was assigned)
- AA (6-digit AA number)
- **Case ID**
- **TL Name**
- **TL Address**
- Employee Name (Last Name, First Name, Middle Initial)
- Employee ID
- TLs (number of TLs expected in the block)
- State (2-digit state code/ 2-character state abbreviation)
- County (3 county code/ county name)
- FS

title: Report Uses
content: This report is useful to keep track of which FS or FR currently is assigned the TL case.

title: SC-958 Observation Summary
content: The SC-958, Observation Summary, shows all active employees that have observation data entered in MOJO.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-958, Observation Summary, contains the following information:
- SCID
- FSA
- Employee Name (Last Name, First Name)
- Employee ID
- Case types (lists the various types of cases such as HU,GQ)
- Observation Status (header)
- Observation (contains the following):
- First Observation Date
- First Observation Recommendation (continue assigning work, additional observation, consult manager)
- First Observation observer Employee ID
- Additional Observation Date
- Additional Observation Recommendation (continue assigning work, additional observation, consult manager)
- Additional Observation observer Employee ID

title: Report Uses
content: This report is useful to keep track of which employee has had an observation and the status of the observation.

title: SC-994 Observations Outstanding
content: The SC-994, Observations Outstanding, shows active employees who have no record of having an observation entered into MOJO OR have had a first observation keyed but required a second observation that has not yet been keyed.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-994, Observations Outstanding, contains the following information:
- SCID
- FSA
- Employee Name (Last Name, First Name)
- Employee ID
- Case types (lists the various types of cases such as HU,GQ)
- Observation Report Uses
This report is useful to keep track of which employees have no record of a first observation or if needed, a second observation.

title: SC-342A, AAs Not Checked In
content: Generate the SC-342A, AAs Not Checked In, daily to determine which address registers have not been checked into MOJO.

title: Report Contents
content:
The report contains the following fields of information:
- AA
- Employee (last name, first name, middle initial, Employee ID)
- Date Assigned (date the AA was assigned)

title: Report Uses
content: This report can be used at the end of operations to determine staff with AAs that have not been checked-in to MOJO. It can also be used in combination with the SC-301 and/or SC-333A, HU Progress by AA, to determine FRs that might be having difficulties completing an AA. Refer to the SC-302, AA Completion Status, and SC-333A, HU Progress by AA, Report Uses sections to manage FRs not meeting completion schedules.

title: SC-342C, HU Questionnaires Not Checked In
content: Generate the SC-342C, Questionnaires Not Checked In, daily to monitor HU progress at the AA level by tracking questionnaires that have not been checked into the SCO.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-342C, HU Questionnaires Not Checked In, contains the following information:
- AA
- Case ID (case ID from the address list page in the register)
- Block (block number associated with the AA and housing unit)
- Address List Page Line Number
- Employee (last name, first name, middle initial, Employee ID)
- Date Assigned (date the AA was assigned)

title: Report Uses
content: The SC-342C, HU Questionnaires Not Checked In, can be used in combination with the SC-342A, AAs Not Checked In, to identify questionnaires that are in the field. Use this report to monitor the questionnaires checked into MOJO.

title: SC-342B, GQ/TL Questionnaires Not Checked In
content: Generate the SC-342B, GQ/TL Questionnaires Not Checked In, daily to monitor GQ and TL progress at the AA level by tracking questionnaires that have not been checked into the SCO.

title: Report Contents
content:

title: SC-302, AA Completion Status

title: Report Contents

title: Report Uses
content:
This report shows the status of work checked in to the SCO. The SCS can quickly determine the completion status of AAs in the field.
Depending on Regional Office guidance on completed progress goals, a good rule to follow to determine if operations are on track to finish on time is to divide the schedule of operations into four portions.
For example, if a SC is scheduled to take four weeks to complete, the completion targets should be as follow:
- 25% or more work needs to be completed by the end of the first week,
- 50% or more work needs to be completed by the end of the second week,
- 75% or more work needs to be completed by the end of the third week, and
- 100% needs to be completed on or before the end of the fourth week.
The SCS can compare the completion targets against the work checked-in percentage column to determine if the field worked is being completed on time.

title: SC-957, Added and Deleted Addresses and Erroneous Adds

title: Screen Uses

The screen is designed to help the Special Census Supervisor reconcile Added and Deleted addresses. It is particularly helpful for verifying changes when a housing unit is coded in the wrong block.
It is expected that erroneous adds do not occur often or at all in the SC. Housing unit appearing on this screen can be an indication that an FR is not following procedures. If housing units appear, ask the FS to provide immediate feedback to the FR, especially if the FR appears multiple times, to ensure he or she knows the proper procedure to add housing unit to the address list.

title: SC-342S(RI), Reinterview Status
content: This SC-342S(RI), Reinterview Status, shows the status of reinterview field operations and the final RI status for the production FR.

title: Report Contents
content:
The SC-342S(RI), Reinterview Status, contains the following information:
- Production Employee (Last Name, First Name, Middle Initial of the production employee)
- Total Prod (number of questionnaires completed by the FR; this is the number of questionnaires checked in from the field )
- Total RI (number of questionnaires in RI; includes randomly selected RI questionnaires, mandatory selected questionnaires, supplemental questionnaires, and/or hard fail supplemental questionnaires)
- \% Prod in RI (number of questionnaires in RI presented as a percent of the total number of questionnaires in production)
- Rand (number of randomly selected questionnaires for RI)
- Supp (number of questionnaires selected for supplemental RI)
- Mandatory (number of questionnaires selected for mandatory RI)
- Hard Fail (number of questionnaires sent to RI for each FR that falsified data on a questionnaire or intentionally did not follow procedures)
- Checked In without a RI status (number of RI questionnaires checked in to MOJO without a RI status entered)
- Checked In with a RI status (number of RI questionnaires checked in to MOJO with a RI status entered)
- Pass (number of questionnaires for the Production FR that passes the office matching review)
- \% Pass (number of questionnaires for the Production FR that passed the office matching review represented as a percent of the total RI questionnaires checked in)
- Soft Fail (number of questionnaires the Production FR was assigned a soft fail because of the office matching)
- \% Soft Fail (number of questionnaires the Production FR was assigned a soft fail because of the office matching represented as a percent of the total RI questionnaires checked in.
- Hard Fail (number of questionnaires the Production FR was assigned a hard fail because of the office matching review)
- \% Hard Fail (number of questionnaires the Production FR was assigned a hard fail because of the office matching review represented as a percent of the total RI questionnaires checked in)
- Non interview (number of questionnaires the Production FR was assigned a Non interview because of the office matching review)
- \% Non-interview (number of questionnaires the Production FR was assigned a Non interview because of the office matching review represented as a percent of the total RI questionnaires checked in)

title: Report Uses
content:
This report summarizes information about reinterview progress, check-in results, and office matching review outcomes. The following are suggested columns to review during operations:
\% Prod in RI -- The percentage shown in this column will be around 5%, if only random cases are selected for a Field Representative. Cases selected for supplemental reinterview (regular and hard fail) will increase the percentage shown in this column.
The Special Census Supervisor should make sure that he or she is selecting supplemental reinterviews only when necessary. Adding additional cases to reinterview will have an impact in the cost of the operation.
Ckd In -- These columns show the number of reinterviews checked-in to MOJO either with or without a RI status entered. The Special Census Supervisor should ensure this number is close or equal to the number shown in the Total RI column.
Soft Fail -- Monitor this column for each Field Representative. Field Representatives that have multiple soft fails for the same error can be an indication of intentionally not following procedures and be grounds for coding a case for this Field Representative as a hard fail. There are some suggested actions the Special Census Supervisor can take if a Field Representative has multiple soft fails:
Investigate the reasons for the soft fails. If the soft fails are for different errors, make sure the Field Supervisor is providing feedback to this Field Representative, so the Field Representative does not repeat the errors again.
Consider sending to supplemental reinterview other questionnaires with the same results as one that was coded as soft fail to verify this Field Representative is following procedures. If there is a pattern that the Field Representative is committing the same errors, this might be an indication of intentionally not following procedures. Talk to the Field Supervisor and make sure he or she provided feedback to the Field Representative to correct the errors. If the Special Census Supervisor has supporting information that this Field Representative is intentionally not following procedures, consider hard failing the Field Representative.
Hard Fail -- If there is a case hard failed for the Field Representative, make sure all other completed work for this Field Representative is sent out to supplemental hard fail reinterview.
Non-Interview -- It is expected that the majority of reinterviews are completed either in the office or in the field. The Field Supervisor is the only person allowed to assign a non-interview outcome for reinterviews that could not be completed in the field. This number should be as close to zero as possible. The Special Census Supervisor should talk to the QC Field Representative conducting the reinterviews to ensure he or she is doing everything possible to complete the reinterviews in the field.

title: Closing Out the Special Census
content:
## Activities Prior to Closing the Special Census Office
## Overview
After the Special Census Office (SCO) has completed all field work, including quality assurance (QA) activities, and checked in all the questionnaires, the Special Census Supervisor (SCS) can start the activities for closing the operation and the SCO. These activities include:
- Ensuring all enumeration materials are collected from field staff, such as badges, bags, manuals, etc.
- Resolving missing cases and ensuring that all cases are checked in to MOJO

title: Collecting Field Enumeration Materials from Field Staff
content:
Field Supervisors (FSs) collect the following materials from their Field Representatives (FRs) and return them to the SCO at the end of the FRs job with the Special Census (SC).
- Census Carrying bags
- Unused forms such as blank Special Census Questionnaires (SC-Qs), unused INFO -- COMMs, etc.
- Office supplies such as pens, pencils, etc., if available
- Census Bureau-issued ID badges from every FR
- Enumeration reference materials such as manuals, job aids, etc.
The SCS collects from the FSs their enumeration materials, supplies, and their Census Bureau-issues ID badges. It is important to collect from the FSs Form SC-20, Field Supervisor's Management Record, as this contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII) information.

title: Resolving Missing Cases
content:
Ensure that all cases are checked in to MOJO. The SCS monitors that status of work by referring to various reports and tables to determine if there are any:
- Assignment Areas (AAs) Not Checked In (SC-342A)
- Housing Unit (HU) Questionnaires Not Checked In (SC-342C)
- Reinterview (RI) Cases Not Checked In (SC-342C(RI))
- Group Quarters (GQ) and Transitory Location (TL) Questionnaires Not Checked In (SC-342B)
These table should show that all items listed above are checked in at the end of the SC. The SCS needs to resolve any cases still in the field that may be showing as not checked in at the end of the operation. If the report or table shows a case that has not been checked in, the SCS follows up with the FR or FS that was assigned this case to check on the status of the case. In some cases, resolving a missing case may include sending the assignment out to the field and completing the assignment again.
If the SCS determines the case is lost that contains Title 13 or PII information, he or she must report the incident to the Census Service Center, within one hour, at 1-877-343-2010, then select option #1 for Cyber Security, Physical Security, and PII Breach Incident Reporting. The SCS must also call the Regional Office (RO) for further guidance. Provide the police report number if the materials were stolen. Obtain a case number from the Census Service Center operator.

title: Statement of Expenditures for the Governmental Unit
content: The Statement of Expenditures, for the governmental unit, is a summary of all expenditures that are charged against the government unit's account.

title: Final Census Results
content: Do not make a commitment regarding a date for the release of the final census results. Headquarters staff prepares the final counts letter for the U.S. Census Bureau Director to sign after all data is collected and processed. A sample of this letter is in []{.mark}Appendix E.

title: Packing and Shipping Materials to NPC and the RO
content:
## Overview
The Regional Office (RO) informs the SCS when to ship materials out of the SCO. The RO provides guidance as to which shipping company to use and the delivery terms for shipment.
All Census Bureau materials are shipped out of the SCO. The SCS will:
Determine material disposition (communicated via a memo) See Appendix G for an example of the memo.
Ship materials to the RO or National Processing Center (NPC) based on the materials dispositions.

title: Materials Dispositions
content: All materials used for the SC need to be boxed and shipped to either the NPC or RO. The SCS uses the memo as a guide as to where materials need to be shipped. See Appendix G for an example of the memo.

title: Materials that Need to be Shipped to NPC
content:
The SCO ships to NPC all completed enumeration materials. These include the following scanned items:
- Address registers, including the map envelope with the maps
- SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, with their corresponding SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, if applicable
- SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
- SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control RecordSC-Q-GE, Special Census Individual Census Questionnaire (used for GQ)
- SC-Q-TL, Special Census Transitory Units Questionnaire, with their corresponding SC-CQ-TL, Special Census Transitory Units Continuation Questionnaire, if applicable
This item, while not scanned from MOJO, does get sent to NPC in the same box.
- SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist
- SC-116(CP), Special Census Group Quarters Control Record Continuation Page
    - The SCO will put the SC-1222 checklists and the SC-116(CP) pages into an envelope.
    - The office will mark the outside of the envelope indicating that observation forms and continuation pages are inside.
    - The envelope is then put into the same box as the barcoded forms and shipped to NPC.
Do not include office supplies in the boxes of Address Registers and questionnaires being sent to NPC.

title: Materials that Need to be Shipped to the RO
content:
The SCO ships to the RO all other materials used in the SC such as:
- Unused reference materials such as manuals, training guides, job aids, etc. These are recycled for other SCs in the area the RO covers
- Unused enumeration materials such as blank questionnaires, INFO-COMMs, Notice of Visit pads, etc.
- Office supplies such as pens, pencils, pencil sharpeners, etc.
The SCO needs to also send back to the RO all forms or materials that contain Title 13 and or PII information. This includes:
- Employee folders
- The materials in the Title 13/PII locked destroy bin
- All completed SC-20, Field Supervisor Management Record
- All completed BC-27, Pay and Work Record
- Administrative forms that contain PII information
- SC-117, Special Census Transitory Location Control Record
- SC-693.2, Special Census Transitory Location Listing Sheet
Refer to the memo that will be sent at the conclusion of the operation for a comprehensive list of the items that need to be shipped and where the items need to be shipped.

title: Packing and Shipping Materials to the RO
content: Clerks will sort materials in the SCO prior to shipping the materials to the RO. The SCS also needs to ensure that Title 13 and/or PII materials are properly handled when placing the materials into the boxes for shipping to the RO.

title: Packing Unused Materials to the RO
content:
Materials to be shipped to the RO need to be boxed in the same boxes that the materials came into the SCO. Make sure to save the boxes that arrive from NPC. Materials need to be sorted by type, for example, clerks will sort:
- Manuals and training guides by type such as FR materials, FS materials, etc.
- Enumeration materials by type such as unused Notice of Visit pads, unused Confidentiality Notices, etc.
- Forms by type such as unused Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires, and Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaires, and unused INFO-COMMS; etc.
- Office supplies by type such as pens, pencils, erasers, pencil sharpeners, etc.
When boxing these materials be sure to keep the type of materials separate whenever possible.

title: Packing Title 13 or PII Materials to Send to the RO
content:
The Title 13 and PII materials need to be packed by type. The clerks pack the administrative materials separate from the used enumeration materials.
When packing Title 13/PII materials, they must be securely double wrapped in opaque paper and taped, so the materials do not show through the wrapping.
The outer wrapping must specify that the package or envelope is for delivery only to a specific recipient, preferably an individual where possible. The outer wrapping should be opaque and NOT indicate that the package or envelope inside it contains controlled unclassified information (CUI).
The inner wrapping must be opaque, tamper-evident, and be labeled as follows:
**Important:** CUI//SP-CENS
>
**Important:** Disclosure Prohibited\--Title 13 U.S.C.
>
**Important:** To be opened by addressee only.
The CUI marking CUI//SP-CENS must be distinguishable from other information in the label.
To prevent loss when the outer wrapping/packaging is damaged, the inner wrapping also must be addressed to a specific recipient, preferably to an individual wherever possible.
The clerks also write on the outside wrap the following:
**Important:** This package contains Title 13 and/or PII information. The release of which to unauthorized persons is prohibited by law.
The Title 13/PII materials that were temporarily placed in the secured destroy bin must also be double wrapped in opaque paper, taped, and sent to the RO at the end of the SC. In addition to the statement about Title 13/PII confidentiality, the clerks will write that these materials are from the secured destroy bin. A sample note could be Title 13/PII materials to be destroyed.

title: Shipping Materials to the RO
content:
Once the items are packed and the boxes sealed in preparation for shipping, call the RO for instructions on shipping the materials to the RO. The RO provides guidance as to which shipping carrier to use (e.g., FEDEX, UPS), and which service to use for the shipment (two-day, ground, etc.).
The RO has contracts with shipping companies and will provide the SCS with the shipping company labels and the RO account number for the shipping company. The SCS completes the shipping labels and contact the shipping company for picking up the boxes.

title: Packing and Shipping Materials to NPC
content:
The packing and shipping of enumeration materials for NPC start when all field operations are over. The materials shipped to NPC all contain Title 13 data and **must** be double wrapped with opaque paper and taped before placing them in the box.
When packing Title 13/PII materials, they must be securely double wrapped in opaque paper and taped, so the materials do not show through the wrapping.
The outer wrapping must specify that the package or envelope is for delivery only to a specific recipient, preferably an individual where possible. The outer wrapping should be opaque and NOT indicate that the package or envelope inside it contains controlled unclassified information (CUI).
The inner wrapping must be opaque, tamper-evident, and be labeled as follows:
**Important:** CUI//SP-CENS
>
**Important:** Disclosure Prohibited\--Title 13 U.S.C.
>
**Important:** To be opened by addressee only.
The CUI marking CUI//SP-CENS must be distinguishable from other information in the label.
To prevent loss when the outer wrapping/packaging is damaged, the inner wrapping also must be addressed to a specific recipient, preferably to an individual wherever possible.
The clerks also write on the outside wrap the following:
This package contains Title 13 and/or PII information. The release of which to unauthorized persons is prohibited by law.
All completed questionnaires must be scanned and placed in a box before any Address Registers. After all the questionnaires are scanned and placed in a box, then the clerk scans and places the address registers into a different box.

title: Packing SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaires
content:
The questionnaires must be packed by AA. The clerks sort the questionnaires by AA, if not already done so. The clerks place as many whole AAs as will comfortably fit face up in the box, trying not to split AAs between boxes.
If Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, has one or more Form SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, the clerk must scan the associated Form SC-CQ, Special Census Questionnaire, into the box before he or she can scan or key another questionnaire. **DO NOT** place continuation questionnaires inside the parent questionnaire.
In instances where a Spanish version of Form SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, was used, DO NOT scan the corresponding English version into a box. The corresponding English version must be sent to the RO to be destroyed.
As a reminder, the SCO ships the following to NPC:
- Address registers, including the map envelope with the maps
- SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, with their corresponding SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaire, if applicable
- SC-RQ, Special Census Reinterview Questionnaire
- SC-116, Special Census Group Quarters Control Record
- SC-Q-GE, Special Census Individual Census Questionnaire (used for GQ)
- SC-Q-TL, Special Census Transitory Units Questionnaire, with their corresponding SC-CQ-TL, Special Census Transitory Units Continuation Questionnaire, if applicable
    This item, while not scanned from MOJO, does get sent to NPC in the same box.
- SC-1222, Special Census Observation Checklist
- SC-116(CP), Special Census Group Quarters Control Record Continuation Page
    - The SCO will put the SC-1222 checklists and the SC-116(CP) pages into an envelope.
    - The office will mark the outside of the envelope indicating that observation forms and continuation pages are inside.
    - The envelope is then put into the same box as the barcoded forms and shipped to NPC.
The number of questionnaires added to a box must equal the number of questionnaires that were checked in. The SCS must resolve these discrepancies. Questionnaires may be stuck together or may have been misplaced in the SCO. When found, scan the questionnaire into the appropriate box and re-scan the address register into MOJO.
If an open box will no longer be used to ship materials to be send to NPC, then the clerk must delete the box in MOJO. Only an empty box can be deleted. If materials have been scanned into a box, then the materials must be removed before the box can be deleted. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for instructions for scanning and packing questionnaires.

title: Packing Address Registers
content:
The Address Registers can be scanned into a box after all Forms SC-Q, Special Census Questionnaire, and Forms SC-CQ, Special Census Continuation Questionnaires, have been scanned into a box.
Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for instructions for boxing Address Registers.
If, after all materials have been scanned into a box, the SCS determines that any materials are lost, the SCS must report this incident to the Census Service Center at 1-877-343-2010, within one hour, then select option #1 for Cyber Security, Physical Security, and PII Breach Incident Reporting. He or she needs to also contact the RO for further guidance. The SCS may need to go out to the field to collect the information for this questionnaire.

title: Shipping Materials to NPC
content:
The SCS must ensure that all Title 13/PII materials being shipped to the RO or NPC have been packed double wrapped in opaque paper and taped prior to placing the materials in the box. Refer to the instructions provided above on how to ship Title 13/PII materials.
Once the items are packed in preparation for shipping, the SCS calls the RO for the instructions to ship materials to NPC. The RO provides guidance as to which carrier and service to use for the shipment (2-day, ground, etc.).
The RO has contracts with shipping companies and provides the SCS with the shipping company labels and the RO account number for the shipping company.
The SCS is responsible for completing the shipment of materials to NPC. The SCS:
- Ensures the materials in the boxes are properly wrapped.
- Prepares the shipping labels and obtain a shipment tracking number for each box through the current RO shipping vendor.
Before closing a box of materials being sent to NPC, the shipment tracking information must be entered in MOJO. Refer to the SC-445, User Guide for the MOJO, for instructions to enter the shipment tracking information.
Print the shipping document and include it with the shipping document and vendor label placed [inside]{.underline} the box.
Pay careful attention of the placement of these shipping documents. Make sure this document is used with its corresponding box.
Once all boxes are ready to be shipped out:
- Seal them securely with shipping tape.
- Place the shipping document and vendor shipping label [inside]{.underline} the box.
- Call the shipping vendor to pick up the materials.

title: Shipping Notices
content: Inform the RO when the materials are picked up by the shipping vendor and shipped out of the RO. Inform the RO how many boxes are being shipped to the RO and to NPC.

title: Closing the Special Census Office
content:
## Special Census Supervisor Responsibilities
The SCS ensures that the SCO is clean, and **ALL** Census Bureau equipment/materials/supplies ***are removed from the premises***. The SCS will make sure that:
- All employees are separated on or before the closing date.
- All personnel and payroll forms and cost reports are completed and forwarded to the RO.
- All completed administrative documents and files are packaged and sent to the RO or to another place the RO designates they be sent.
- All final reports are submitted to the RO.
- All keys to the locked SCO are turned over to the RO SC Program Coordinator or to the landlord or his or her representative.
- No census materials are left behind.
